home_pitcher_note: Brad Penny gets his first career Opening Day start against the Giants as the Dodgers kick off their 50th anniversary season in Los Angeles. Penny is 3-3 lifetime against the Giants and was 1-1 with a 3.12 ERA last year.
away_pitcher_note: This will be the fourth career Opening Day start for Zito, who's 0-3 with a 9.49 ERA in his previous three. However, he has fared well at Dodger Stadium, where he has won both of his career starts.
summary: 2008-03-31 - San Francisco Giants (0) @ Los Angeles Dodgers (5) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: After starting the last three Opening Days for the Dodgers, Derek Lowe slides into the No. 2 slot. He's coming off an erratic 2007 season in which he was hampered by an injury to his hip or groin that has not been a factor this Spring. He's accepted pitching coach Rick Honeycutt's suggestion to hook his spikes on the edge of the rubber, and it seems to have provided greater stability on his rear leg and given his pitches later life.
away_pitcher_note: Some thought Cain might be named the Giants' Opening Day starter, given the quality of his '07 season and his remarkable maturity at age 23. Poor run support skewed Cain's record last year, as he received the second-lowest run support in the Major Leagues (3.51). His fastball sometimes looks hittable, but at 6-foot-3, he's able to throw it on a downhill plane that eludes bats. When his curveball is equally effective, he's extremely tough.
summary: 2008-04-01 - San Francisco Giants (2) @ Los Angeles Dodgers (3) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Chad Billingsley did not have a good Spring Training, and manager Joe Torre senses the right-hander has been pressing, trying to impress the new boss. Billingsley has complained that extra work on a changeup has messed with his release point. When he gets frustrated, he tries to throw the ball through the catcher and he fell into that pattern several times in the spring.
away_pitcher_note: The Giants, and much of the baseball world, expect big things from Lincecum after he led National League rookies with 150 strikeouts in 146 1/3 innings last year. The combination of his small stature and high-effort delivery may always prompt concern about a possible injury, but Lincecum steadfastly believes that he can rely on his fastball-curveball combination to pitch 200 innings per year.
summary: 2008-04-02 - San Francisco Giants (2) @ Los Angeles Dodgers (1) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Germano won the fifth starter spot -- a spot he held for much of last season -- by outperforming the other candidates vying for the job in Spring Training. Germano has a nice curveball and fastball but has worked hard to refine a changeup that gives him yet another pitch to keep hitters off-balance.
away_pitcher_note: Kuroda will be making his regular-season debut after a spring of transition from stardom in Japan to fourth starter in Los Angeles. Kuroda has a varied repertoire, a lively fastball and knows how to pitch. But his spring command was inconsistent, and he sometimes was puzzled with a strike zone that varied from what umpires called in Japan.
summary: 2008-04-04 - Los Angeles Dodgers (7) @ San Diego Padres (1) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Peavy, the defending National League Cy Young Award winner, allowed three hits over seven scoreless innings and knocked in two runs in the Padres' 4-0 victory over the Astros on Opening Day. Peavy struck out four, walked three and didn't allow a hit over his final three innings.
away_pitcher_note: Because of the Thursday off-day, Penny comes back on Saturday and the Dodgers won't need a fifth starter until April 8 at Arizona. The Padres have given Penny as much trouble as anybody (he's 3-6 with a 5.61 ERA against them lifetime), but in 2007 he had a 1.29 ERA without a decision in only one seven-inning start. Penny was 3-0 last April with a 1.95 ERA in five starts.
summary: 2008-04-05 - Los Angeles Dodgers (1) @ San Diego Padres (4) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: In his first start of the season, Young didn't always have his best command, as evidenced by the five walks he issued. But he managed to keep the Astros off the scoreboard until the sixth inning, when reliever Joe Thatcher walked in a run with the bases loaded, a run that was charged to Young. Still, Young allowed just five hits over 5 2/3 innings with three strikeouts.
away_pitcher_note: Lowe makes his second start of the season after facing the Giants on Tuesday. Last year, he allowed the Padres seven runs over 11 1/3 innings in two starts and is 3-3 with a 3.09 ERA lifetime against San Diego. He was particularly unlucky last year, as his teammates scored only 30 runs in his 14 losses.
summary: 2008-04-06 - Los Angeles Dodgers (3) @ San Diego Padres (2) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Haren made his D-backs debut last Wednesday and aside from one inning in which he allowed three runs on a pair of homers, he was impressive. Haren was acquired by Arizona in an eight-player deal with the A's in December. The right-hander tied for the AL lead in games started (34) last year and was third with a 3.07 ERA. In two career appearances against the Rockies he is 0-2 with a 5.40 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Loaiza, who was tagged with the loss after pitching 2 2/3 innings of relief in the rain-delayed Wednesday-night loss, makes his first start of the year after being skipped the first time through the rotation. Although he won the competition against Chan Ho Park in part because of a guaranteed contract, his 4.50 spring ERA was decent enough for a fifth starter.

home_pitcher_note: Davis was roughed up by the Reds in his first start of the year last Thursday in Cincinnati. The left-hander allowed just three runs (two earned) but he walked six and allowed a total of 10 baserunners in 3 2/3 innings. Davis was diagnosed with thyroid cancer last week and this will be his final start before undergoing surgery April 10. Davis posted a double-digit win total for the fourth year in a row in 2007. Davis can usually be counted on for innings. Last year he worked six or more frames in 19 of his 33 starts and was 11-4 with a 2.30 ERA in those games.
away_pitcher_note: Billingsley makes his first start of the season after two unexpected relief appearances. He was scratched from his scheduled debut last Wednesday before the first pitch because of a rain forecast, relieved for one-third of an inning only for rain to interrupt play for 74 minutes, then was called on in relief again Friday night in San Diego for two scoreless innings. He is 4-1 with a 2.36 ERA lifetime against Arizona and was 2-1 against the Diamondbacks last year.

home_pitcher_note: Owings put his Spring Training struggles behind him in his first outing of the year against the Rockies on Friday. The right-hander was masterful as he allowed just one run on two hits in 6 2/3 innings. Owings had good command of his fastball -- something he lacked during the spring -- and was able to hit both sides of the plate with it as well as elevate it when he needed to. Owings won one of the team's most important games of the year when he beat the Pirates in an emergency start Sept. 27 in Pittsburgh. Owings doesn't have overpowering stuff, but his competitiveness seems to allow him to overcome that.
away_pitcher_note: Hiroki Kuroda's Major League debut was pretty special, as he held down the Padres, allowing only a solo homer to Brian Giles in seven innings. He struck out four without a walk and made only 77 pitches. Kuroda's out pitch is his splitter, but his fastball touches 93 mph and he uses both sides of the plate.

home_pitcher_note: After an effective and scoreless Opening Day victory, Brad Penny encountered a hiccup against the Padres, allowing five consecutive singles in a 38-pitch first inning. Penny got back on track, blanking San Diego over the next five innings, but the damage was done. He'll be facing the Padres again, this time at home.
away_pitcher_note: The Dodgers likely aren't too keen on seeing Peavy again, not after he earned a complete-game victory on April 5. Peavy allowed just one run on two hits with one walk in a 4-1 complete-game victory over Los Angeles, his first complete game since Sept. 2, 2006. The Padres allowed Peavy to throw 116 pitches because he wasn't too tired and because he'll get an extra day of rest before facing the Dodgers again.
summary: 2008-04-11 - San Diego Padres (7) @ Los Angeles Dodgers (5) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Lowe has had no decisions in his first two starts. He pitched out of two jams and allowed only one earned run in six innings against the Padres and faces them again in this one. His sinker was darting enough for six strikeouts, showing no ill effects from the comebacker that knocked him out of his first start.
away_pitcher_note: Young will face the Dodgers for a second time this season, this time in Los Angeles. On Sunday, he recorded his first quality start of the season, tossing seven innings and allowing two runs on five hits to the Dodgers. He walked three while striking out eight. He did give up a home run to Andre Ethier, which matched his entire total of homers allowed at PETCO Park last year in 13 starts. In his first game against the Astros, he did not have his best command, issuing five walks. But he gave up just five hits, and now has allowed 10 hits in two games.
summary: 2008-04-12 - San Diego Padres (1) @ Los Angeles Dodgers (11) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Billingsley only pitched in relief against the Padres in San Diego, but he gets the start in the series finale against Greg Maddux. He threw two scoreless innings at PETCO Park, working out of a jam. He is 4-1 lifetime against San Diego, with a 2.19 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Maddux got off to a rough start in his second start of the season on April 7 against the Giants, walking two and allowing a run on two hits in the first inning. That was the end of his trouble, though, as the future Hall of Famer earned career victory No. 348 as he retired 19 of the last 20 at one point in earning his first victory of the season. He struck out five and walked two. Maddux, oddly enough, didn't allow a single flyout until the seventh inning.
summary: 2008-04-13 - San Diego Padres (1) @ Los Angeles Dodgers (0) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Hiroki Kuroda threw strikes and kept the Dodgers close early, but he couldn't stop the Diamondbacks from sweeping the series. Two of the four runs he allowed were unearned, but he let two leads get away, allowed nine hits and lost the game on a two-out single by Eric Byrnes. He was particularly effective throwing first-pitch strikes, but was hurt several times on 0-2 counts.
away_pitcher_note: With two strong starts under his belt, Duke continues to pile on the confidence that was missing a year ago. The left-hander set himself in great position to notch his first win of the season his last time out, but couldn't get the offensive support he needed to garner that win. Duke threw 116 pitches in seven innings in the outing against Chicago, allowing just one run, while striking out six. So far this year, he's shown a better job on maintaining his poise with runners on base and his pitches have had much better movement than they did a year ago.

home_pitcher_note: Kuo has replaced Esteban Loaiza in the rotation, in part because Loaiza had a rough first inning in his only start of the season, in part because Kuo has not allowed a run this season, in part because Kuo's brittle elbow is not well-suited for relief work. The early-season juggling is an indication that new manager Joe Torre is still getting acquainted with who his players are and what they can do. Kuo gives the Dodgers rotation a left-hander who is effective tying up right-handed hitters. The question about him has never been his stuff, but his health.
away_pitcher_note: Morris continues to battle the command and location of his pitches. As he gets into the middle of games, his pitches are getting flat and moving out and over the plate -? never a good combination. He?s not the staff ace that he was earlier this decade, though there is something positive to be taken from the fact that  he can typically be counted on to give the Pirates at least six innings per start. Morris has made 15 appearances (13 starts) against the Dodgers and is 4-5 with a 5.57 ERA against the Los Angeles club.

home_pitcher_note: What are the odds? For the second consecutive start, Brad Penny faced Jake Peavy and allowed the Padres a four-run, six-single inning. In this one, he was extended to 119 pitches over six innings, allowing 10 singles and three walks. Penny had no decisions in two starts against Pittsburgh last year.
away_pitcher_note: If it wasn't for a lengthy rain delay, Maholm would have pitched much deeper than the 5 1/3 innings his line score shows. Maholm allowed six hits, but kept the Reds scoreless before thunderstorms prompted his early exit. For the second straight start, Maholm showed excellent command of all four of his pitches, and he maintained much better consistency in getting ahead of hitters. Maholm will be facing the Dodgers for the fourth time in his career, though the lefty is still in search of his first win against the Los Angeles club. He is 0-2 with a 6.50 ERA in those previous three starts.

home_pitcher_note: Bennett learned late Thursday afternoon that he'll be pitching Friday's series opener, despite the fact that he made a 28-pitch relief appearance on Wednesday night. The right-hander proved successful as a starter late last year with Triple-A Richmond and had a successful four-inning emergency start in place of Mike Hampton on April 3. He issued four consecutive two-out walks in Sunday's loss to the Nationals and surrendered a decisive two-run homer in Wednesday's setback.
away_pitcher_note: Lowe was the beneficiary of the Dodgers' first bona fide batting explosion of the season, an 11-1 romp over the Padres on Saturday, in which he went eight innings, allowing four hits while striking out six and walking none. Besides inducing mostly groundouts following a semi-shaky, 20-pitch first inning, Lowe was near-perfect over the next seven. After Josh Bard touched him for a single in the second, he retired the next 15 batters, and 20 of the last 21 he faced. In his career, Lowe is 5-0 against the Pirates with a 3.03 ERA, including 1-0 and 4.70 in 2007.

home_pitcher_note: Lefty Chuck James will make his second start of the season, replacing Tom Glavine, who was scratched Friday night due to a strained right hamstring. James has a career record of 22-15, but was hit hard (three innings, six earned runs, five hits) in his only start for Atlanta this season, April 9, in Colorado. James, who is 0-1 with a 1.69 ERA with Richmond, was 1-0 with a 1.80 ERA in his one appearance against the Dodgers in 2007.
away_pitcher_note: Billingsley's last outing, on Sunday, was cause for optimism, albeit coming on the losing end of Greg Maddux's 349th career victory, in which the Dodgers mustered all of five hits. In giving up one run over five innings that day, Billingsley struck out eight, walked two, and gave up a hit in each of the first four innings. Along the way, he lopped more than four runs off his ERA. The 23-year-old has no decisions against the Braves, having faced them once in 2007, when he went a combined 3 1/3 scoreless innings over two games.

home_pitcher_note: Jurrjens struggled with his control, throwing just 56 of his 101 pitches for strikes, against the Marlins on Tuesday night. But still, the 22-year-old right-hander allowed just two earned runs and four hits. Jurrjens has provided the Braves a chance to win each of his first three starts. His three walks on Tuesday matched the total he issued in his first two starts combined.
away_pitcher_note: Making his first at Dodger Stadium, right-hander Hiroki Kuroda continued his impressive introduction to the Major Leagues after and 11-year career in Japan. Through three games and 18 2/3 innings, Kuroda, 2-1, has a 2.89 ERA.  On Monday he gave up seven hits and three earned runs over six innings against the Pittsburgh Pirates.  Next up is an afternoon game against the Braves in Atlanta.

home_pitcher_note: Now 3-0 with a 1.09 ERA in three rehab starts, Belisle will start in place of Josh Fogg. Belisle has been on the 15-day disabled list with a strained right forearm, and Fogg, signed in the offseason, has struggled to start the season.
away_pitcher_note: Penny allowed an unearned run over 5 2/3 innings on five hits on Wednesday against the Pirates. He also struck out four and did not walk a batter to even his record on the year with a win against the Bucs.

home_pitcher_note: In the Reds' 9-2 over the Cubs on Thursday, Volquez allowed one earned run, four hits and four walks and struck out seven over just five innings. Volquez found himself in several deep counts and came out of the game after throwing 112 pitches. Able to rely on his excellent stuff, including a 94-96 mph fastball with movement, he wiggled out of a few tight situations, but it still cost him an earlier exit.
away_pitcher_note: Kuo, who replaced Esteban Loaiza in the rotation, pitched well in his second start of the season, giving up only one earned run in four innings of work in an 11-2 win last Tuesday. Kuo threw 33 pitches in the first inning, when he walked three straight batters to force in a run. He gave up only one hit in the next three innings, but was pulled before qualifying for the victory.

home_pitcher_note: Lowe pitched with a bull?s-eye on him against the Braves, getting struck three times by comebackers. His sinker was a little too active, as he walked four in 4 1/3 innings, but it didn't sink when Chipper Jones launched a three-run homer to center field. Two of the five runs against him were unearned because of Jeff Kent error.
away_pitcher_note: Haren has been outstanding since coming over in a trade from the A's during the offseason. The right-hander is 3-0, but he could easily be 4-0 if the D-backs bullpen had held onto a lead in the season's second game. In his last outing, Haren tossed seven shutout innings in a 9-0 win over the Padres. The D-backs have provided Haren with early run support as they've scored 11 times in the first inning over his last three starts.

home_pitcher_note: Billingsley was overpowering for four innings against the Braves with nine strikeouts, but he lost his command in a 35-pitch fifth inning that included three walks. In this one against the D-backs, he'll be looking to avenge an April 8 loss in Phoenix, when he allowed five runs in only 2 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: The D-backs scored too late in Gonzalez's last start to get him off the winless list, but he pitched credibly for six innings in Saturday's 10-3 win over San Diego, holding the Padres to four hits. The 25-year-old has a track record for being consistently better on the road than at Chase Field, where he has been victimized for 15 of the last 21 homers he has allowed.

home_pitcher_note: Hiroki Kuroda bobbed and weaved through a third quality start in Atlanta. He was hit relatively hard and needed 118 pitches just to get through six innings, but he was able to strand 10 runners and keep his club in the game. He was behind in many counts as his command wavered, particularly with the cut fastball, and too many pitches caught too much of the plate.
away_pitcher_note: Jimenez's talent is evident, but his inexperience is preventing him from achieving results that match it. Against the Astros on Sunday, he gave up four hits and walked five with two out. For the 5 2/3 innings he was in the game, he gave up five hits and struck out six. Jimenez struggled last season in his only start at Dodger Stadium, giving up five earned runs in four innings.

home_pitcher_note: The Dodgers scored early and often against the Reds and Penny knew what to do with the lead, extending his record at Great American Ball Park to 5-0 while allowing one earned run over six innings. He faces his favorite opponent in this start, as he's 12-2 with a 2.92 ERA lifetime against the Rockies and was 2-0 last year. Penny not only is effectively spotting his fastball, but he is finally incorporating his splitter as a regular part of his repertoire.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start, at home against the Phillies, Redman struck out five and forced nine ground-ball outs. He gave up just four fly balls, but three were home runs (one caromed off the wall in right-center for an inside-the-park homer). Working with a less-than-blazing fastball and a changeup that is his best pitch, Redman has little room for mistakes up and over the plate. This time, though, Dodger Stadium is more forgiving than Coors Field and the Dodgers' lineup doesn't match that of the Phillies.

home_pitcher_note: Loaiza got the call, taking over for Hong-Chih Kuo, who had taken over for Loaiza after one start. That's the way it's been for the Dodgers and their fifth starter this year. In Loaiza's only start, he allowed four runs in the first inning, then retired 10 consecutive hitters. In his only start against Colorado last year, he allowed three runs in 3 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: After a rough start, Francis has gone seven innings in each of his last two starts. Tuesday night wasn't as good as his previous start, when he pitched seven shutout innings in San Diego. But he left with a 6-4 lead against the Phillies, only to see the bullpen falter. Francis would have had an even more sparkling outing if not for two hiccups -- the fourth inning, when he walked the opposing pitcher to load the bases and walked in a run, and the seventh when he left a pitch over the plate for a Jayson Werth homer. But he looked more like the pitcher that won 17 games last year than he did in his first two starts.

home_pitcher_note: Nothing is coming easy for Miller, but the 22-year-old is taking some small steps in getting better. In his last start -- his first win as a Marlin -- he labored to get through the first inning and allowed an unearned run at Atlanta. Yet, he regrouped, and despite yielding nine hits, he made it through five innings with his team ahead, 3-2. Miller tossed a season-most 98 pitches, with 55 for strikes. Seven times with Detroit last year, Miller reached the 100-pitch plateau, with his career high being 111 on July 23, at the White Sox in 4 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Lowe left Wednesday night's start against the Diamondbacks after five innings and 67 pitches with a tight elbow, but after a preliminary exam was still listed to pitch the opener of this series in Florida. He was 0-2 against the Marlins last year and is 5-4 lifetime.

home_pitcher_note: Steady progress is the best way to define Olsen's first month. While he wasn't involved in the decision in his previous start, he strung together 7 1/3 scoreless innings while facing the Brewers at Miller Park. Without his best stuff, he allowed the leadoff batter to reach in seven of the eight innings he opened. And for the first time in 73 career starts, he failed to strike out a batter. Olsen has worked at least seven innings in four straight games, and he has allowed just one run in his last 21 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: For the second consecutive start, Billingsley showed flashes of brilliance, but that was not enough to win. He was overpowering enough to strike out a career-high 12 in six innings against the Diamondbacks, but he also was charged with five runs. He was particularly hurt by a two-run homer from Jeff Salazar, but also allowed the go-ahead run to score on a wild pitch. He's 2-0 lifetime against the Marlins.

home_pitcher_note: The silver lining for the 25-year-old in his last start was he battled through five innings after allowing five runs in the first. Basically, Badenhop was his own long-relief pitcher, tossing three scoreless innings. But the damage was done in the first two, as he gave up six runs in a loss at Atlanta. From the third inning on, however, he gave up two hits and retired eight of his last 10 batters. The Marlins are looking for steady progress from Badenhop, who will be making his third start in the Majors.
away_pitcher_note: Hiroki Kuroda got a no-decision against the Rockies, but it wasn't pretty. He allowed five runs on nine hits over six innings and was so off with his mechanics that he started pitching out of the stretch in mid-game. Since his effortless debut in San Diego, Kuroda has had to work hard in his starts.

home_pitcher_note: After two awful starts to open the year, Francis has posted a 2.57 ERA in his last three. But he doesn't have a win, and the Rockies have dropped two of the three games. He's limiting mistakes, having given up just 14 hits in his last 21 innings. His first step to recovery was getting pitches to the proper location on his arm side (outside to right-handers), and lately he has been able to use the other side of the plate for strikes and for balls when he wants. In his last start, held the Dodgers to two run in seven innings and he is 4-1 with a 2.64 ERA in 10 starts against them.
away_pitcher_note: In Penny's last outing, he once again took advantage of an early hitting frenzy, coming out of the first inning of an 11-3 win over the Rockies with a 10-2 lead and continuing to hold Colorado's potent hitting attack in check over seven innings, his longest outing of the season. Beginning with the final out of the first inning, he retired 13 in in a row. Penny is now 13-2 against the Rockies in his career, having won both decisions against the National League champions in 2007 and adding last Saturday night's performance.

home_pitcher_note: By demoting left-handed rookie Franklin Morales to Triple-A Colorado Springs, moving lefty Jeff Francis to Friday night and pushing lefty Mark Redman to Tuesday against the Cardinals, the Rockies created an opening for Saturday, then completed a trade with the Royals for De La Rosa, who was 3-0 with a 1.64 ERA in four starts for the Royals' Triple-A affiliate in Omaha. De La Rosa was the player to be named in the Spring Training deal that sent right-handed reliever Ramon Ramirez to the Royals.
away_pitcher_note: Loaiza made his second start and got into the fifth inning on Sunday against the Rockies at Dodger Stadium. He maintained his stuff through four scoreless frames before the Rockies tagged him for both runs in the fifth inning. Loaiza allowed two earned runs, five hits, one walk and struck out one. He made the most out of 70 pitches, throwing 44 for strikes.

home_pitcher_note: Tuesday night marked the fourth time Cook has started and the Rockies have ended a losing streak. Cook not only stays smooth throughout his outings, but he is showing a knack for making a big pitch. He fanned just three in seven innings against the Giants, when he gave up two unearned runs but won, 3-2. However, with runners at the corners and one out in the seventh, he picked Eugenio Velez off first then struck out Ray Durham -- who entered the game with favorable numbers against Cook.
away_pitcher_note: Lowe dreads Coors Field (5.87 ERA there). In his Tuesday night no-decision in Florida, he didn't seem to show any signs of the tight elbow that shortened his previous start, but was unable to protect a five-run lead. Three of the six runs he allowed in five innings were unearned, but he wasn't able to stop the damage when betrayed by his defense. He allowed an uncharacteristic four extra-base hits.

home_pitcher_note: Billingsley finally hit the win column with seven solid innings in Florida on Wednesday. For the fourth consecutive start, Billingsley struck out at least eight and the only run he allowed came on an infield single. He walked four, hit a batter and had two wild pitches, but pitched out of a pair of jams. He'll be starting against the Mets for the first time in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Perez's inability to deal with adversity, most of it of his own making, overwhelmed him again in his loss to the Pirates at Shea Stadium on Wednesday. He faced 16 batters, walked five, allowed two hits and hardly responded well to an error made behind him. He has walked 21 batters in 29 innings. The Mets have lost four of his six starts.
summary: 2008-05-05 - New York Mets (1) @ Los Angeles Dodgers (5) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Kuroda was efficient in a seven-inning no-decision against the Marlins on Thursday. He allowed only five hits, no walks and made 85 pitches, but he lost a lead by allowing a two-run homer to Cody Ross. After temporarily pitching out of the stretch in his previous rocky start, Kuroda seemed comfortable with his mechanics and returned to a conventional windup.
away_pitcher_note: The Mets skipped Figueroa's most recent turn in the rotation, after last Monday's game was rained out at Shea. He did, however, pitch 3 1/3 effective innings of relief two days later, holding the Pirates to one run on five hits. Figueroa threw 61 pitches in that outing and will return to the rotation on regular rest against the Dodgers, a team that he hasn't faced since 2002. This current group of Dodgers holds a .303 combined average against Figueroa, though none of the at-bats have come since 2004.
summary: 2008-05-06 - New York Mets (4) @ Los Angeles Dodgers (5) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Penny didn't have his velocity or command when he spotted the Rockies a three-run lead in wintry conditions at Coors Field, but he still picked up his ninth consecutive victory over Colorado. Although he went 2-1 against the Mets last year, he's 5-11 with a 5.66 ERA against them lifetime.
away_pitcher_note: Maine was inefficient in his latest outing, needing 107 pitches to complete six innings against the Diamondbacks, but wriggling out of two separate jams to allow only two runs in total. The effort was enough to net Maine his third win of the season, tying him with Jorge Sosa and Johan Santana for the club lead. Maine lost to the Dodgers twice in two starts last year, finishing with a 5.73 ERA.
summary: 2008-05-07 - New York Mets (12) @ Los Angeles Dodgers (1) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: With the day off on Thursday, the Dodgers shift back into a four-man rotation and Lowe starts against the Astros. He went 1-0 against them in two starts last year, allowing one run in 11 innings. He's 2-2 lifetime with a 2.23 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Wandy Rodriguez's strained left groin still hasn't improved enough to allow him to throw a simulated game, so the Astros were prudently giving Moehler some simulated innings in preparation for this game or Friday's at Los Angeles. It will be Moehler's first start since Sept. 29, 2006, when he was with the Marlins.

home_pitcher_note: Chad Billingsley pitched into and out of jams against the Mets, but despite four walks, he was good enough to limit the damage to one run over six innings for his second win. He faced the Astros twice last season, going 1-1 with a 3.86 ERA. He will be pitching on his regular four days' rest, as the Dodgers utilize days off to go with a four-man rotation.
away_pitcher_note: Sampson will receive an extra day of rest this time, with hopes that he can regain control of his fastball. Sampson has had two poor outings in a row, having allowed five earned runs in each start. The right-hander spent extra time between starts working with pitching coach Dewey Robinson in an effort to regain the control that has given him success in the past.

home_pitcher_note: Kuroda had a tough night against the Mets. He lasted only 3 1/3 innings and was pitching out of the stretch almost constantly. He allowed eight hits and three walks and further complicated his job with a throwing error. He even lost command of his fastball, which has been his most consistent pitch this year. It was his sixth consecutive start without a victory.
away_pitcher_note: Chacon extended his club record of consecutive starts without a decision to seven when he faced the Nationals on May 6. The right-hander allowed four earned runs over seven innings but left with the score tied in a game the Astros eventually won. Chacon has a career record of 4-7 with three saves and a 5.85 ERA against the Dodgers.

home_pitcher_note: Villanueva has lost his last four decisions and has really struggled in his last two starts, allowing 13 runs and 19 hits in 10 innings of losses at Houston and at Florida. In his most recent seven innings of work, Villanueva has surrendered six home runs, including back-to-back-to-back homers to the heart of the Astros lineup, and then a pair of two-out shots against the Marlins. It's a surprisingly inconsistent start to the season for a guy who posted a 1.99 ERA in six Brewers appearances last September, five of them starts, to cement his spot in the 2008 starting rotation.
away_pitcher_note: Penny didn't get hard by the Mets on Wednesday, but he was hit often. He either fell behind in counts, or when he got ahead, couldn't put away hitters while allowing a career-high 10 runs. He didn't complete five innings. Penny threw seven shutout innings against the Brewers last year and is 3-2 lifetime, but in his only Miller Park start, he allowed five runs in seven innings and drew a loss.

home_pitcher_note: Parra still has not pitched more than 5 1/3 innings in any of his seven starts, but he probably could have passed that threshold on Friday against the Cardinals. He surrendered three early runs, then settled down over his final three innings and retired the final nine men he faced. Parra was only at 83 pitches when he was lifted for a pinch-hitter in the bottom of the fifth inning, and admitted he wanted to keep working. "When I missed, I missed down," he said. "That's something to build on."
away_pitcher_note: Lowe followed his Coors Field disaster with another rough start at home against the Astros, allowing six runs in 5 1/3 innings. Traditionally an innings-eater, Lowe hasn't gone more than 5 1/3 innings in any of his last five starts, but he's shown no signs that anything is wrong physically.

home_pitcher_note: In his previous outing, Sheets surpassed Brewers great Ted Higuera for tops on the club's career strikeout list, striking out six Cardinals to give him 1,086. He allowed three runs and nine hits with a walk over seven innings. Until Jeff Suppan picked up a win Sunday, Sheets was the only Brewers starter to win a game since Manny Parra on April 5. Sheets is among the National League's top 10 in wins and ERA, along with hits and walks per innings.
away_pitcher_note: Billingsley barely survived the first two innings against the Astros, giving up five runs on six hits and two walks, but then settled down and retired the last nine batters he faced. He has faced the Brewers twice in his career, giving up three earned runs in 1 2/3 innings. He will be pitching on his regular four days' rest, as the Dodgers utilize days off to go with a four-man rotation.

home_pitcher_note: The southpaw is coming off his first loss of the season, in which he scattered one run over six innings, but the Angels' bats were unable to generate any offense. Saunders struggled early, allowing a pair of walks and the lone run in the opening inning, but settled down for five scoreless frames after that.
away_pitcher_note: Hiroki Kuroda rebounded from his shortest start of the season (3 1/3 innings) to keep the Astros hitless through 6 2/3 on Sunday. When the Dodgers desperately needed a starting pitcher to pitch well and go deep in the game, Kuroda did just that, stopping a three-game losing streak and striking out a career-high five batters.
summary: 2008-05-16 - Los Angeles Dodgers (2) @ Los Angeles Angels (4) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: He wasn't as razor-sharp as in recent outings on Sunday in Tampa Bay, but Santana left the game with a lead the bullpen was unable to hold. He needed 113 pitches -- 33 in the first inning alone -- to reach 5 2/3 innings, yielding four runs on nine hits while walking one and striking out seven. Command, for one of the few times this season, was an issue for Santana, whose mid-90s fastball was crackling as usual. He's 2-2 in four career outings against the Dodgers with a 3.42 ERA. He was 1-1 with a 2.08 ERA last year against Los Angeles' other team.
away_pitcher_note: Chan Ho Park gets the nod in his continuing comeback over Hong-Chih Kuo. Park has been exclusively a long reliever this year and on four occasions has pitched three innings. Once a power pitcher, he now possesses a varied repertoire. This will be his first start for the Dodgers since 2001 and his first Major League start since April 30, 2007 when he allowed seven runs in four innings for the Mets.
summary: 2008-05-17 - Los Angeles Dodgers (6) @ Los Angeles Angels (3) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: In one of the most dominant performances of his career, Weaver limited the White Sox to a single and two walks in seven innings on Tuesday night, striking out seven. His 109 pitches prevented him from getting deeper in the game and getting the win he deserved. Weaver, rocked for 12 earned runs in 10 1/3 combined innings in his past two starts, rebounded with a crackling fastball and off-speed pitches to good locations in not allowing a White Sox runner to reach scoring position. Weaver is 2-0 with a 1.50 ERA in two career starts against the Dodgers.
summary: 2008-05-18 - Los Angeles Dodgers (2) @ Los Angeles Angels (10) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: After getting battered by the Mets, Brad Penny was much improved in Milwaukee, but not good enough to win. He couldn't protect a two-run lead and walked the opposing pitcher on four pitches to trigger the winnning three-run rally. Penny still has velocity and he's mixing in his splitter more, but his location hasn't matched his 13-1 start of last year. He already has as many losses as he did all last season.
away_pitcher_note: Arroyo pitched seven scoreless innings but received a no-decision in the Reds' 7-6 win over the Marlins on Wednesday. He allowed five hits, walked three and recorded four strikeouts -- three of which came in the seventh when he struck out the side. Arroyo has pitched 12 consecutive scoreless innings and has allowed just one run over his last 15 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Chad Billingsley is coming off his best start of the year. He took a two-hit shutout into the eighth inning in Milwaukee, displaying exceptional command of his live fastball, even though he lacked any consistent offspeed pitch. He was charged with one run that scored after he left the game. Billingsley missed the Reds in Cincinnati and is 0-1 with a 1.42 ERA against them lifetime.
away_pitcher_note: Belisle was roughed up again in Game 1 of a doubleheader vs. the Mets on May 10. He gave up six runs -- five earned -- and seven hits over five innings in a 12-6 loss. In 19 1/3 innings, he's allowed 16 earned runs and 32 hits. He's allowed less than three runs in only one start this season and none of them have lasted longer than 5 1/3 innings. He was scheduled to pitch Thursday against the Marlins, but the game was postponed because of rain.

home_pitcher_note: Kuroda deserved a better fate than the loss he took in Anaheim. He pitched into the seventh inning and was charged with three earned runs, but every Angels rally was aided by a bad throw from a Kuroda teammate. This followed his best start of the season, when he lost a no-hitter after 6 2/3 innings. Nonetheless, he still has only one win in nine starts.
away_pitcher_note: Cueto had a no-hitter through five innings but started struggling with his location and gave up three hits -- all home runs -- in the sixth to receive a no-decision the Reds' 4-3 win over Cleveland on Friday. He allowed back-to-back home runs to Casey Blake and Travis Hafner, marking the fifth time the Reds have given up back-to-back homers this season. He finished with seven strikeouts, bringing his season total to 53 in nine starts. This will be his first start out west, as he didn't pitch in Cincinnati's three-game series at San Francisco in late April.

home_pitcher_note: Lowe volunteered to start on short rest when Brad Penny's arm tightened and it turned into a short start on Sunday. Lowe was victimized by a James Loney throwing error, then let things get completely out of hand with an 0-2 pitch that Mike Napoli hit for a three-run homer. He was charged with seven runs on 10 hits in five innings and spent most of that time fuming on the mound over all that went wrong. He's gone a month since his last win.
away_pitcher_note: For many pitchers, it would just be a blip, but for Wainwright, two rough starts in a row qualifies as a slump. He's throwing strikes but he's giving up a lot of contact. It's far too early to get worried, but Wainwright needs to be at his best for the Cardinals to keep challenging for the NL Central title.
summary: 2008-05-23 - St. Louis Cardinals (2) @ Los Angeles Dodgers (1) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Brad Penny's last start was pushed back a day because of tightness in his arm during a bullpen session. When he did take the mound, it turned into his third consecutive disappointing performance. He allowed five runs (20 in last three starts) and it took two innings before his velocity reached the mid-90s. On the other hand, he grinded out six innings to save the bullpen and the Dodgers came back to win the game. He already has as many losses as he did all last season.
away_pitcher_note: Lohse looked more like himself last time out, breaking a rough stretch in which he allowed 19 runs in three starts. He should be feeling fresh, with an extra day of rest following a start in which he threw only 78 pitches. Lohse was knocked around in his only previous start at Dodger Stadium.
summary: 2008-05-24 - St. Louis Cardinals (4) @ Los Angeles Dodgers (0) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: The Dodgers' youth movement hit another milestone when 20-year-old left-hander Clayton Kershaw was promoted to the Major Leagues from Double-A. Kershaw was 0-3 with a 2.28 ERA, 47 strikeouts, 15 walks and 32 hits allowed in 43 1/3 innings at Double-A Jacksonville, where his erratic workload was designed to preserve his arm for a pennant-race run in Los Angeles.
away_pitcher_note: Throughout Wellemeyer's career, a lack of consistency has been a major problem. At times he's been excellent, at other times rough. This year, though, he's been impressively steady. And it's been especially true in May -- Wellemeyer has allowed two earned runs or fewer in four consecutive starts. He's gone five starts without giving up a home run.
summary: 2008-05-25 - St. Louis Cardinals (3) @ Los Angeles Dodgers (4) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Dempster made one bad pitch in his last start against the Astros, and they made him pay. He had given up two earned runs over 20 1/3 innings prior to the game, and Hunter Pence doubled that when he connected on his second career grand slam. Dempster was more upset with how the hitters got on ahead of Pence's slam. He fell behind, which led to bad inning management. Dempster struck out five and walked two over six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Billingsley continued to pitch like an ace against the Reds, throwing seven scoreless innings and allowing four singles. In this game, he had complete command of his elusive curveball. Billingsley has quality starts in four of his last five appearances. His only appearance against the Cardinals last year was in relief.

home_pitcher_note: Gallagher took the loss Wednesday in his third big league start. The Astros collected five runs on eight hits and one walk over 4 2/3 innings against the rookie right-hander, who did strike out four. He also took a line drive off his right shin, courtesy of Miguel Tejada. The problem Gallagher has is lack of experience, and the Cubs have to decide if he can handle on the job training.
away_pitcher_note: Kuroda went eight innings against the Reds in what manager Joe Torre called his best start of the season. He scattered five hits and allowed two runs, mixing a live fastball with an effective slider. Although it was only Kuroda's first win since the first week of the season, he came into the game with the lowest ERA of the Dodgers' top four starters.

home_pitcher_note: Zambrano set a career high with four hits in his last start -- that's four by himself. He already had a three-hit game this season, and is batting .343. But let's talk about his pitching. Big Z held the Pirates to two runs on six hits over seven innings and struck out six. He's off to the best start in his career and has reduced the number of walks issued. As Lou Piniella said, when Zambrano has confidence in his pitches and is aggressive, he's effective.
away_pitcher_note: Lowe's winless streak hit the one-month mark, but he showed significant signs of improvement in a 2-0 loss to the Cardinals. He allowed five hits over seven innings, stung by a two-run homer from Ryan Ludwick, but otherwise effectively implemented a slower delivery that ensured a better arm angle and release point and kept his sinker sinking.

home_pitcher_note: Vargas came up big for the Mets at Coors Field Saturday, earning his first win in three starts since his May 13th callup. Pitching on three-day's rest a day after the Mets 'pen was extended in a 13-inning loss to the Rockies, Vargas went seven strong innings, holding Colorado to two runs on four hits. He struck out three and walked only one, inducing eight ground-ball outs with a sinker that played well in the offensively oriented ballpark. He improved to 5-1 against the Rockies, and will try to remain undefeated against the Dodgers, who he has faced once, a complete game victory in 2005 when he allowed one run on six hits while striking out seven.
away_pitcher_note: Penny showed improvement after three really rocky starts, but he still didn't get a win his last time out. This time it was one bad inning, which included back-to-back walks. Penny has had some shoulder stiffness to deal with, but he said after his last start he felt better than he had in five years. His velocity topped at 97 mph, which eased concerns about anything serious physically. But he's still allowing too many hits.
summary: 2008-05-29 - Los Angeles Dodgers (4) @ New York Mets (8) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Maine had a strong outing at Coors Field on Sunday, holding the Rockies to three hits and four walks over six innings while striking out a season-high eight, but it wasn't enough to match the complete-game one-run outing by Aaron Cook. Maine allowed four runs (three earned), and through the first five innings the only hit the Rockies had touched him for was a three-run homer that followed an error on a potential double-play grounder that would have ended the inning. His changeup was off, but he had good velocity. The Rockies were patient in laying off his pitches out of the zone, forcing him to throw strikes.
away_pitcher_note: Kershaw was impressive in his Major League debut on Sunday, limiting St. Louis to two runs on five hits over six innings. The only thing that kept him from getting his first career win was Albert Pujols, who drove in the first Cardinals run and set up the second, and the Dodgers bullpen that surrendered the lead. Overall, Kershaw threw 102 pitchers, 69 for strikes, and consistently touched 96 mph on the radar gun. He struck out seven, including three in the first inning.
summary: 2008-05-30 - Los Angeles Dodgers (9) @ New York Mets (5) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: The 6-foot-7 righty has fallen into a steep slump of late, as he lost his sixth consecutive decision on Monday by giving up four earned runs in four innings to the Marlins. In that short outing, Pelfrey still threw 95 pitches in the 7-3 Mets loss, 52 of those tosses for strikes. And Pelfrey's ERA has suffered in the process, rising from 1.50 on April 15 to his current 5.33 mark.
away_pitcher_note: Billingsley allowed his first home run in a month but continued to pitch like an ace against the Cubs. Working with an extra day of rest, he went six innings and struck out seven, but was lifted for a pinch-hitter with the Dodgers trailing by a run after making only 83 pitches. Billingsley has quality starts in five of his past six appearances.
summary: 2008-05-31 - Los Angeles Dodgers (2) @ New York Mets (3) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Mets manager Willie Randolph believes Santana will only get better as the year goes on and the weather gets warmer, but he showed on May 27 against the Marlins that he can be the true stopper New York is looking for right now. He pitched seven innings and struck out seven in a 5-3 win over Florida, improving his record in games following a loss to 33-24 since the 2004 season. In those games, Santana has allowed three runs or less 54 times.
away_pitcher_note: Kuroda continued to be the tough-luck starter on the staff with another wasted effort in Chicago. After throwing six scoreless innings in the cold, he saw a win turn into a loss in the seventh when his defense and bullpen betrayed him. Kuroda allowed only one earned run in 6 1/3 innings and has allowed more than three earned runs only once in 11 starts.
summary: 2008-06-01 - Los Angeles Dodgers (1) @ New York Mets (6) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Derek Lowe turned in his best start of the year, one of the best in several years and was in position for his first win in nearly five weeks with seven scoreless innings against the Cubs. away_pitcher_note: Reynolds had all kinds of command issues in his last start in Philadelphia, as he walked eight batters and allowed five hits and six earned runs in 5 2/3 innings. Three of those walks led to home runs by Chase Utley and Geoff Jenkins in the fifth inning. Reynolds threw 101 pitches, but only 51 for strikes. This will be the fifth career Major League start for the 22-year-old righty, who is searching for his first victory.

home_pitcher_note: Penny was hammered again by the Mets in general and David Wright in particular. In his last six starts he's 0-4 with a 9.43 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Francis had inconsistent location against a tough Cubs lineup. At times he paid, at times he made key pitches. He went five innings before being removed for a pinch hitter in the sixth, and he held the Cubs to three runs -- one on a Derrek Lee homer -- and six hits, striking out five.

home_pitcher_note: Kershaw allowed a first-inning home run and was wild throughout a 3 2/3-inning outing, being charged with four runs on five hits and four walks. away_pitcher_note: Friday at Wrigley seemed to be a typical Cook start in 2008. He was forcing grounder after grounder. But he gave up three home runs in his final 1 1/3 innings, and wound up charged with 10 hits and seven runs in 6 1/3 innings in a no-decision. At least Dodger Stadium doesn't have the issue of winds kicking up and blowing balls out of the park, as what happened to Cook against the Cubs.

home_pitcher_note: Chad Billingsley continued his fine work, shutting out the Mets for seven innings, only for the bullpen to let another win get away. He's pitching confidently and aggressively and still has a knack for escaping jams with runners in scoring position, which he did in five innings against the Mets.
away_pitcher_note: Don't be surprised to see Dempster exit early, even if he's pitching OK. He threw four straight outings of 109 pitches or more before his last start, when he only tallied 93. Lou Piniella said he hopes to keep the converted closer on a leash for one more outing. Dempster is 7-0 at Wrigley Field but 0-2 on the road.

home_pitcher_note: Hiroki Kuroda threw in a real clunker against the Mets, at 2 2/3 innings his shortest start of the season. Kuroda has generally pitched in tough luck, this being only the second time in 12 starts he allowed more than three earned runs.
away_pitcher_note: Gallagher has rebounded well from his last road start, when he gave up five runs in 4 2/3 innings in a loss at Houston on May 21. After yielding three straight singles with two outs in the first, Lowe only allowed a pair of fourth-inning hits the rest of the game. The sinkerballer has pitched well of late, compiling a 1.23 ERA in his past three starts.
away_pitcher_note: Zambrano had three hits in his last start, the fourth three-hit game of his career and he's now batting .366 this season. The Cubs had hoped to limit Zambrano's pitch count because he was coming off a 130-pitch outing against the Dodgers on May 28. home_pitcher_note: Penny returned to form Tuesday against the Rockies, giving up two runs on six hits in six innings with the help of a good splitter. He also struck out five and walked four. away_pitcher_note: Marquis picked up the win in his last start against the Padres in spite of himself. He got a spirited lecture from Lou Piniella on the mound in the fourth after walking the leadoff batter. Marquis needs to go deeper in the games because the bullpen is overworked.

home_pitcher_note: Maddux came up empty for the fifth consecutive time in his attempt at career victory No. 351, even though he pitched very well in his last start on Wednesday against the Cubs. The Padres have scored three or fewer runs in eight games when Maddux was on the mound.
away_pitcher_note: Kershaw battled the Rockies, and himself, for five innings in his third career start. summary: 2008-06-10 - Los Angeles Dodgers (7) @ San Diego Padres (2) (Final)

He did so against a Mets lineup that was 14-7 against left-handers this season with a .269 batting average. away_pitcher_note: Billingsley had a strange game against the Cubs. He was unhittable striking out eight of the first 10 outs. He came into the game with a 1.80 ERA over his seven previous starts.
summary: 2008-06-11 - Los Angeles Dodgers (1) @ San Diego Padres (4) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Peavy, the 2007 National League Cy Young Award winner, is expected to be activated from the disabled list in time to start against the Dodgers on Thursday. Peavy is 4-3 this season with a 2.91 ERA in nine starts.
away_pitcher_note: Kuroda just pitched the Dodgers' first shutout in three years, what more needs to be said? summary: 2008-06-12 - Los Angeles Dodgers (0) @ San Diego Padres (9) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Galarraga just missed his second straight quality start against the Indians. The Tigers, meanwhile, improved to 7-2 when he starts. Galarraga has never faced the Dodgers, but he did perform well in his only Interleague start. He held the Diamondbacks to two runs over six innings.
away_pitcher_note: It's a homecoming for Michigan native Derek Lowe, who also is coming off a wild win over the Cubs. The Dodgers were losing when Lowe left the game, even though he had taken a no-hitter into the fifth inning. But a rare five-run rally against Carlos Zambrano gave Lowe a second consecutive win and fourth consecutive quality start. Lowe is 7-1 with a 1.82 ERA lifetime against the Tigers.

home_pitcher_note: Though the Tigers still haven't formally announced their starter, manager Jim Leyland said it's 90-percent likely they'll give Bonine his first chance in the Majors. Not a power thrower, he has succeeded by becoming a ground-ball control pitcher.
away_pitcher_note: Penny pitched well for the second straight outing Sunday against the Cubs, yielding three runs on six hits in six innings. He also struck out five and walked three. Penny has not won since May 2, a span of seven starts, but he's pitched much better in his last two, both of which have been quality starts in which his opponent has shut down the Dodgers' offense. Before that, he had compiled a 9.43 ERA in his previous five outings.

home_pitcher_note: Robertson earned his third quality start of the season in his last start against the hot White Sox. He went 6 1/3 innings, giving up three runs on eight hits, while walking two and striking out four. He had solid command, especially of his slider, as 53 of his 87 pitches went for strikes. He surrendered a solo home run to Jim Thome in the second inning, but didn't have many other jams until he left the game with the bases loaded in the seventh. Robertson has only one career start against the Dodgers, in which he gave up four runs on five hits in five innings and earned a no-decision.
away_pitcher_note: Kershaw was better against the Padres, getting into the sixth inning with only one run scoring while he was on the mound and a second that scored on a reliever's wild pitch. Still, he had occasional bouts of wildness that served mainly to run up his pitch count and hasten his exit. He's truly advanced for a 20-year-old, but he'll need to quickly improve on the 13 walks in 20 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Cueto learned a hard lesson in his last outing. It's a lesson that will shorten his career if he doesn't master it. The message: throw strikes. He made 101 pitches against the Cardinals; just 50 were strikes. He issued three walks in the first inning, and all three scored on homers. A five-run first isn't a recipe for success, and Cueto, who had trouble with the Cardinals the first time he faced them, didn't have any success. But he'll need to remember that to win in the bigs he must throw strikes.
away_pitcher_note: Billingsley battled through three shaky innings against the Padres Wednesday, allowing two homers for the second consecutive game, before settling into a groove that proved too little and too late. His velocity was fine, but his location was up and over the plate. He's winless over his last four starts and the Dodgers are 4-9 in his 13 starts.

home_pitcher_note: Arroyo had expressed disappointment over some of his recent outings, but he had no reason to complain about his latest. He turned a 2-0 lead over the bullpen, which couldn't hold it. Still, Arroyo gave the Reds the kind of performance that befits a pitcher whom they've expected to be one of the anchors of their rotation.
away_pitcher_note: Lowe, moved up a day in the rotation after Brad Penny's assignment to the disabled list, pitched well enough to win in his Michigan homecoming, but lost instead. In his six defeats, the Dodgers have scored a total of seven runs. He allowed the Tigers two earned runs in seven innings, struck out five without a walk and made 121 pitches. His sinker has been sharp in five consecutive quality starts, but he has only two victories to show for it.

home_pitcher_note: Harang followed up one of his worst outings of the season with one of his best in a win over the Red Sox on Friday night. Harang is 2-3 with a 4.13 ERA lifetime through five games against the Dodgers. He was 1-0 in one start against them last season, in which he gave up just four hits with no earned runs in eight innings of work.
away_pitcher_note: Stults, who is 5-6 with a 3.59 ERA through 14 starts at Las Vegas this season, will be making his season debut. He made five starts and 12 appearances for the Dodgers in 2007 and two starts in six appearances in 2006. He was called up to fill the roster spot vacated by Brad Penny, who was placed on the 15-day disabled list.

home_pitcher_note: Kershaw was locked in a scoreless duel through four innings when rain delayed his start against the Tigers. Management wouldn't let him restart the game 47 minutes later. He struck out two and walked two, escaping a first-inning mess with a double-play grounder. The two walks continue to illustrate the highest hurdle he needs to clear.
away_pitcher_note: In his last outing, Lee was hardly the pitcher who had displayed razor-sharp control in opening the season. Pitching against the Padres, he threw 105 pitches in 6 1/3 innings, and just 67 of those pitches were strikes. His problem was getting his pitches too high in the strike zone, a lethal combination for a pitcher. Still, Lee kept the damage to a minimum, and he would have picked up his 11th win if the Indians bullpen had held onto a 3-2 lead he gave it.

home_pitcher_note: Park will fill in and start for the injured Hiroki Kuroda on Saturday. Park's only start this season came May 17 against the Angels when he gave up two runs on three hits through four innings of work. Park was also tabbed as a possible one-time replacement for starter Brad Penny, is also on the disabled list. Eric Stults was called up from Triple-A Las Vegas to start instead.
away_pitcher_note: Sabathia only seems to get stronger as this season progresses. After his disastrous four starts to open the season, he has posted a 2.39 ERA over his last 10 starts. He had just one bad inning against the Padres in a win on Sunday, as he allowed three runs on six hits with a walk and 10 strikeouts over eight innings. It marked the 14th time in his career he had posted a double-digit strikeout game. This will be Sabathia's first career appearance against the Dodgers, and the lifetime .297 hitter is probably more excited to pick up a bat than he is to take the mound at Dodger Stadium.

home_pitcher_note: Billingsley was solid in his last outing, pitching 6 1/3 innings and giving up just one run on five hits with three walks and nine strikeouts. It was his first win since beating Cincinnati on May 21. All of his pitches were working, and the right-hander never ran into trouble until he gave up a couple soft base hits in the seventh inning.
away_pitcher_note: Byrd has been very inconsistent this season and especially shaky in his last two starts. He has allowed 10 earned runs over those two outings, lasting a total of just seven innings. The long ball continues to prove his undoing. He gave up another pair in a loss in Colorado on Tuesday -- one of which was an inside-the-park job by Jeff Baker. For the season, Byrd has allowed 19 homers -- the most in the league. He has had trouble commanding his slider of late. Byrd is 0-3 with a 3.79 ERA in six career appearances at Dodger Stadium.

home_pitcher_note: Lowe was stellar in his last start against the Reds on Wednesday, but had to leave early after tiring in the sixth inning. He allowed just one run on three this with two walks and six strikeouts in 5 1/3 innings. His start against he Reds came on short notice. Originally scheduled to pitch Thursday, he was moved up a day in the rotation at Hiroki Kuroda left the team with soreness in his right shoulder. He had thrown 121 pitches in seven innings during his previous start. Through his last six starts, Lowe is 3-2.
away_pitcher_note: Buehrle was dominant for a third consecutive start Wednesday night against the Pirates. He took a no-hit bid into the sixth inning and lasted eight innings for the third straight time. He gave up only four hits and two runs, and retired the first 12 batters he faced. It was the 43rd time in his career he has set down 10 or more in a row. He's 2-0 with a 1.50 ERA in his last three outings and has thrown four straight quality starts. Buehrle has not faced the Dodgers this season, but has faced them twice in his career. He's 1-1 with a 1.20 ERA lifetime against them.
summary: 2008-06-24 - Chicago White Sox (6) @ Los Angeles Dodgers (1) (Final)

He was called up from Triple-A Las Vegas on Tuesday to fill in for the injured Brad Penny, who went on the 15-day disabled list with inflammation and tendinitis in his right shoulder.
away_pitcher_note: Floyd was resilient against the Pirates on Thursday. After allowing six unearned runs in the second inning and watching Nick Masset start throwing in the bullpen in preparation for an early dismissal, Floyd stayed strong. He went 5 2/3 innings and allowed just one earned run in the game while fanning six. The White Sox offense came back from a six-run deficit to earn him the win. He's 4-0 with a 3.66 ERA in his last five starts. He hasn't faced the Dodgers since 2006, but owns a career 1-0 record in Interleague play to go along with a 2.92 ERA.
summary: 2008-06-25 - Chicago White Sox (0) @ Los Angeles Dodgers (5) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Against the Indians, Kershaw couldn't duplicate the four scoreless innings he threw against the Tigers in his previous start. He remained winless for the season and the Dodgers have scored eight runs while he was in the game during his six starts.
away_pitcher_note: Danks' debut performance in the Crosstown Showdown was one to remember, holding the Cubs to one run on five hits over six innings in a no-decision. From the last out in the second to Kosuke Fukudome's one-out single in the sixth, Danks retired 11 straight. Danks also has worked seven innings or more in just two of his trips to the mound but has gone at last six innings on 10 occasions.
summary: 2008-06-26 - Chicago White Sox (2) @ Los Angeles Dodgers (0) (Final)

Sabathia, who was the only Cleveland hitter who really hurt Park with a long solo homer. Otherwise, Park struck out nine in only five innings, while allowing three hits in a no-decision. His only other start of the year was against the Angels, allowing two runs (one earned) in four innings.
away_pitcher_note: Saunders was in complete command, having held the Phillies to two hits, when they struck for a pair of runs with two outs in the seventh. When the Angels rallied in the eighth, the lefty had earned his AL-leading 11th win, giving up two earned runs on five hits and two walks. From the outset, he was throwing strikes and getting early-count outs. The Phillies didn't have a man in scoring position before Jayson Werth's solo homer in the seventh. Saunders won his only start against the Dodgers, giving up two earned runs in 7 1/3 innings. This will be his first appearance at Dodger Stadium.
summary: 2008-06-27 - Los Angeles Angels (0) @ Los Angeles Dodgers (6) (Final)

away_pitcher_note: Weaver used his competitive instincts as much as his talent to limit the Phillies to one earned run in 5 1/3 challenging innings Sunday. He was in trouble from the start, leaving two runners in scoring position in the first inning by striking out Ryan Howard and Pat Burrell. Effectively using his riding fastball, he struck out six while walking three and yielding four hits. Weaver gets pumped against his hometown Dodgers. summary: 2008-06-28 - Los Angeles Angels (0) @ Los Angeles Dodgers (1) (Final)

away_pitcher_note: Continuing a streak of 13 quality starts dating back to last year, Lackey threw eight nearly flawless innings against the Nationals in a 3-2 victory in Washington. He allowed just two runs -- one earned -- and struck out six. He only threw 97 pitches on the outing, 65 for strikes, and picked up his fifth win.
summary: 2008-06-29 - Los Angeles Angels (1) @ Los Angeles Dodgers (0) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Though he took the loss in his last start, 3-2 to the Rangers on Wednesday night, Oswalt pitched well and has had five quality starts in his last six tries. away_pitcher_note: Stults, in only his ninth Major League start, threw a four-hit, complete-game shutout against the White Sox his last time out. Overlooked most of his Minor League career, he's the only Dodgers starting pitcher with a winning record. He was called up to make an emergency start in place of an injured Brad Penny, but now seems to have earned a spot in the rotation. He's a crafty lefty who throws strikes.

home_pitcher_note: Rodriguez tied a career-high with nine strikeouts in his last start, a 7-2 win over the Rangers. His ERA at Minute Maid Park over the last two seasons is 2.64. Rodriguez is 2-1 with a 2.29 in four career games (three starts) against the Dodgers.
away_pitcher_note: Kershaw continues to have the command problems to be expected for a 20-year-old. He issued two leadoff walks to the White Sox in his last start and both scored. He was lifted after four-plus innings, still winless, but all indications from manager Joe Torre was that the left-hander would remain in the rotation. Kershaw has issued 22 walks in only 33 innings and eight of the 16 runs he's allowed have reached base via walks.

home_pitcher_note: The 30-year-old right-hander went five innings against Boston in his season debut Friday night, allowing a three-run homer to J.D. Drew but not much else in a 6-1 loss at Minute Maid Park. Hernandez hit 96 miles per hour with his fastball but his offspeed pitches were inconsistent. He beat the Dodgers 3-2 in his only career start against them on June 14, 2005, when he gave up two runs in six innings of work in a start at Kansas City.
away_pitcher_note: Kuroda returns from almost three weeks on the disabled list to face the Astros. In his only start against Houston, Kuroda allowed only one run in 6 1/3 innings and left leading, but a bullpen meltdown cost him the victory. The Dodgers aren't sure how much to expect from Kuroda, so Chan Ho Park will be on standby. Park is coming off six scoreless innings against the Angels on Friday night.

home_pitcher_note: If Backe's roller-coaster ride continues, he's due for a good outing. Backe earned his first win in a month when he beat the Rays on June 22 with seven strong innings. The next time out he gave up six runs on nine hits in 5 1/3 innings against Boston Saturday night. Backe has no record and a 4.50 ERA in six career innings vs. the Dodgers.
away_pitcher_note: Billingsley has a three-game win streak, the most recent being a bizarre victory in which the Dodgers scored the game's only run without a hit. Billingsley's outing was nearly overlooked, but he pitched seven scoreless innings, allowing only three hits while striking out seven. When he minds his tempo and doesn't rush, he's becoming close to dominating.

home_pitcher_note: Maybe Sanchez isn't on a roll. Maybe he's simply this good. The Giants can entertain that thought in light of his steadiness for more than a month. Sanchez has won six of his last seven starts, allowing more than three runs in only one of them. His only blemish in his last outing was Jack Cust's second-inning homer in San Francisco's 11-1 victory at Oakland on Sunday. Sanchez has no record and a 3.72 ERA in four lifetime appearances against the Dodgers.
away_pitcher_note: Two things seem certain when Lowe starts. He'll pitch well and his club won't hit. The Dodgers have scored only seven runs in his eight losses this year. He's lost 45 games in three-plus years with the Dodgers, which includes 10 shutouts and 14 more losses in which the Dodgers have scored one run. He was on his game again through seven innings against the Angels, allowing only one run.
summary: 2008-07-04 - Los Angeles Dodgers (10) @ San Francisco Giants (7) (Final)

After producing one of his best starts of the season against the Indians on June 25, Zito ran into
trouble at home, allowing five runs -- four earned -- on six hits in five innings against the Cubs. The lefty is 3-3 with 4.53 ERA in seven career starts against the Dodgers
away_pitcher_note: Brad Penny's return from the disabled list has been put off one more cycle through the rotation, so Chan Ho Park gets another emergency start in San Francisco. He's 4-2 overall, but he's been at his best as a starter this year with a 1.20 ERA in three starts, striking out 19 in 15 innings. summary: 2008-07-05 - Los Angeles Dodgers (2) @ San Francisco Giants (5) (Final)
