Cain kept his fastball low and used both sides of the plate to stifle the Cubs potent lineup. In addition to his fastball, Cain used a sharp curveball and deceiving changeup to keep the Cubs off balance. With his 10 strikeouts, Cain is now second on the Giants with 107 strikeouts and is looking to even his record before the All-Star break. In six career starts against the Dodgers, Cain is 0-3 with a 4.88 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Eric Stults, after attending to the birth of his second child, rejoins the club to make his fourth start of the season.  He struggled in his most recent start in Houston, never a kind ballpark for a left-hander. Only five days earlier, he threw a complete-game shutout.
summary: 2008-07-06 - Los Angeles Dodgers (5) @ San Francisco Giants (3) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Three weeks on the disabled list did the trick for Hiroki Kuroda, who returned with seven scoreless innings against the Astros and showed no signs of the right shoulder tendinitis that sidelined him. He scattered five hits, walked only one and threw an efficient 83 pitches, with his fastball clocked around 94 mph.
away_pitcher_note: Campillo uncharacteristically struggled with his control on Wednesday night and paid the price against a talented Phillies lineup. Whenever he falls behind, the right-hander's varied repertoire of pitches becomes limited.  This was the second time the Phillies had seen him as a starter and his fourth appearance against them. The Dodgers haven't seen the 29-year-old rookie hurler this season. But there might be some reason to wonder if the National League will have better success against him when they get their second looks later this year.

home_pitcher_note: Billingsley has a four-game win streak, although his most recent victory in Houston wasn't nearly as bizarre as the previous one, in which the Dodgers scored the game's only run without a hit. Nonetheless, Billingsley has emerged as the most consistent starter on the club, with three quality starts in his last four outings after losing his first four decisions.
away_pitcher_note: Before allowing four runs to the Phillies on Thursday night, Jurrjens had gone three consecutive starts  (21 2/3 innings) without allowing an earned run.   The three homers  --  all solo shots --  he surrendered were two less than he'd allowed in his first 16 starts of the season.  This was the first loss in nine starts for the 22-year-old right-hander, who limited the Dodgers to one earned run in seven innings on April 20.

home_pitcher_note: Lowe has been the victim of stingy run support by his teammates this year, but they got him off the hook and turned a loss into a win by erasing a three-run deficit in a 10-7 win over the Giants. Lowe has pitched much better than that game and suffered defeats this year, so there was some justice in picking up a win despite allowing eight hits in five innings.
away_pitcher_note: Hudson scattered four hits over seven strong innings and picked up his ninth win of the season Friday against the Astros. Hudson struck out six for the first time since May 27, a span of six starts. The only run charged to Hudson came after Kelly Johnson bobbled a potential inning-ending, double-play grounder one batter earlier. Hudson is 5-1 with a 4.07 ERA in nine career starts against the Dodgers. He last faced them on July 5, 2007, when he allowed six runs on 10 hits in three innings and didn't factor in the decision.

home_pitcher_note: With Brad Penny still sidelined, Chan Ho Park remains in the rotation, and he certainly deserves it based on his four starts, including the most recent in San Francisco, where he allowed one run on three hits with seven strikeouts over six innings. Park's ERA as a starter this year is 1.29.
away_pitcher_note: The 24-year-old had Tommy John ligament replacement surgery on Aug. 3 and, after making five Minor League starts, will make his 2008 debut against the Dodgers -- a team he is 1-1 against with a 9.00 ERA in two starts for his career. Johnson pitched eight scoreless innings in his final rehab start for Double-A Carolina on Friday, allowing five hits while striking out seven and walking two while throwing a season-high 111 pitches.

home_pitcher_note: Eric Stults took a three-run lead into the fifth inning against the Giants, but when he let the first two batters reach base, he was yanked, having allowed seven hits and two walks in four innings. Since his shutout of the White Sox, he's allowed 16 base runners in 9 1/3 innings. His preparation was disrupted when he flew home for the birth of his son.
away_pitcher_note: Volstad, the Marlins' first-round pick in 2005, pitched two scoreless innings of relief against the Rockies on Sunday to win his Major League debut. After starter Mark Hendrickson gave up four runs in four innings, Volstad came in for the fifth with the Marlins down, 4-3. But the 21-year-old retired six of the 10 hitters he faced, got of a bases-loaded jam in the sixth and left with the Marlins leading. The 6-foot-7 righty was called up from Double-A Carolina on Sunday. In 15 starts with the Mudcats this season, Volstad went 4-4 with a 3.36 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Needless to say Kuroda is back. He came within one eighth-inning pitch of throwing a perfect game Monday against the Braves, yielding just a single base runner in a one-hit shutout in which he struck out six. Kuroda has not allowed a run in 16 innings since returning from the disabled list (right shoulder) on July 2 and has won consecutive decisions for the first time all season. His last two Dodger Stadium starts have been shutouts.
away_pitcher_note: Nolasco is on a roll, pitching at an All-Star level. The 25-year-old right-hander comes off a brilliant eight-inning, five-hit performance at San Diego. He gave up one run and struck out seven, while not issuing a walk. Nolasco has won his last five decisions, and nine of his last 10.

home_pitcher_note: Billingsley's four-game win streak was snapped by the Braves, who roughed him up for a season-high six runs in 5 1/3 innings. Billingsley had a no-hitter through four innings, but issued a key walk in one inning and started another with a home run by Brian McCann. According to manager Joe Torre, Billingsley still tends to start rushing when things don't go well and that compounds his problems.
away_pitcher_note: In the final game before the break, Miller will look to get back on the winning track. The 23-year-old lefty has dropped three straight decisions, and he seeks his first victory since June 16 at Seattle. Up and down all season, the lefty comes off a five-inning stint at San Diego, where he gave up four runs on six hits with four walks and five strikeouts. He threw 92 pitches, with 55 for strikes. This will be Miller's second appearance against the Dodgers. On April 29 at Dolphin Stadium, he worked three innings, giving up six runs on nine hits in a game he wasn't involved in the decision.

home_pitcher_note: Davis had a quality start in his last outing against the Phillies, but got no decision as the D-backs bullpen spoiled a two-run lead. He allowed three runs on five hits and gave up a homer to Ryan Howard. Davis will be pitching on a full week's rest. In games which he has had at least six days of rest, Davis is 13-10 with a 4.01 ERA in 27 starts in his career.
away_pitcher_note: He didn't duplicate his nearly perfect one-hitter, but Hiroki Kuroda pitched well enough to win against the Marlins. He complained that his breaking ball wasn't as sharp, but it was still a quality start. Don't be fooled by the losing record. He's left four games with leads that the bullpen was unable to protect. In his only Chase Field start, he allowed nine hits in 5 2/3 innings and took the defeat.

home_pitcher_note: Haren was spectacular in his last outing in Washington, holding the Nationals to just one run on three hits in eight innings. Still, the All-Star could not pick up the win as the D-backs bullpen blew two saves in the late innings. Against the Dodgers, Haren is 2-1 with a 4.15 ERA in three starts.
away_pitcher_note: Billingsley went into the break by overpowering the Marlins, striking out a career-high 13 in seven innings. He's won five of his last six decisions and lowered his ERA to 3.25. Billingsley is 0-2 with a 9.72 ERA against the Diamondbacks this year, including a 6-4 loss in which he fanned 12 in six innings.

home_pitcher_note: Just as his other fellow starters had experienced on the last road trip, Webb pitched well enough to win against the Phillies, but Chad Qualls allowed four runs in the eighth inning to spoil his gem. Webb is 9-2 with a 2.61 ERA when pitching on at least six days of rest, and is 9-3 with a 2.78 ERA in 14 starts against the Dodgers lifetime.
away_pitcher_note: Lowe pitches in this game so he'll be sure to miss pitching in Coors Field in the series that follows. He was perfect in his last start for 6 2/3 innings while beating Atlanta. In his last 10 starts, he has lowered his ERA from 5.34 to 3.85. He'll be pitching on 10 days rest.

home_pitcher_note: This will be Wells' return to the Majors. He hasn't appeared in a big league game since April 28, when the blood clot in his right hand made it impossible for him to continue. Also, it's his first start since the Rockies' first game, when he held the Cardinals to one run and four hits in 5 1/3 innings in a no-decision that the Rockies eventually won. The Rockies need rotation leadership and are turning to Wells, who believed he should have been in the rotation when the season began.
away_pitcher_note: Eric Stults isn't overpowering, so his margin for error isn't great, as was demonstrated when he allowed first-inning back-to-back homers to the Marlins. But he made a quick adjustment and kept Florida off the scoreboard for the rest of his six-inning outing. He's already thrown a complete-game shutout, and that ERA is hard to overlook. When he keeps his off-speed stuff down, he can mow through a lineup efficiently.

home_pitcher_note: Jimenez was shaky in the early innings against Pittsburgh, walking two, hitting another and throwing a wild pitch in the Bucs' three-run third inning. But he gathered his composure and slowed his mechanics to retire the final 13 batters he faced. The outing was a microcosm of Jimenez's season. After a slow start to 2008, Jimenez has pitched some of the best baseball in his short career during his past 10 starts. He hasn't surrendered more than four runs in any outing during that span, dropping his ERA from 4.85 to 4.20, and has picked up three of his four victories.
away_pitcher_note: Kershaw will be promoted to make this start for the Dodgers, returning to the rotation after a three-start demotion to Double-A, where he went 2-0 with a 1.00 ERA. Kershaw, a rookie lefty, showed flashes of brilliance in his first tour with the Dodgers, but he also showed the wavering command of a 20-year-old. He has 24 walks in 38 2/3 Major League innings.

home_pitcher_note: Rusch, who spent most of the season pitching for Triple-A Colorado Springs, recorded his second consecutive win after giving up just two runs on six hits in 5 2/3 innings against the Pirates. Rusch stayed ahead in the count and used his curveball and changeup to keep Pittsburgh off balance. Rusch has made 10 starts against the Dodgers in his career, but he's 0-5 with a 14.21 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: The All-Star break did Kuroda no good. After being spotted a three-run lead, he was battered by the Diamondbacks for six runs over the first 1 1/3 innings in his first start. The last time he pitched that ineffectively, he wound up on the disabled list with shoulder problems. Coming into the game, he had a 1.19 ERA in his three previous starts. He's 2-7 on the road.

home_pitcher_note: Billingsley went into the break having won five of his last six decisions, but he fell to 0-3 against Arizona this year and really scuffled doing it. Maybe it was the extra rest during the five days off, but he allowed seven hits and three walks in 5 2/3 innings and was taken deep in the first inning by Conor Jackson on a hanging breaking ball. By the time he straightened out his timing, his pitch count was into triple digits.
away_pitcher_note: Lannan finally got some run support Saturday against the Braves, allowing one run in six strong innings and cruising to an 8-2 win. It was just the second time this season that Lannan had recorded back-to-back wins; the first coming on April 22 and 27. Lannan struck out four and walked three, escaping bases-loaded jams in the fourth and fifth innings with just one run allowed. Entering Saturday's start, Lannan had received the lowest run support -- 2.72 runs per start -- of any qualifying starter in the Majors this season. The 23-year-old lefty has never faced the Dodgers.

home_pitcher_note: Lowe followed the trend in the series against Arizona with an awful first inning, allowing three runs, although there was a defensive breakdown involved. He didn't pick up a ball in his 10 days off going into and coming out of the All-Star break and had no command in the early innings. At a time when the Dodgers have really needed a veteran to step up and assume the role of ace, Lowe has been erratic. And his layoff was the result of avoiding having to start in Coors Field.
away_pitcher_note: Perez was far from perfect Sunday, but he didn't need to be. The Nationals scored 12 runs in the first four innings, and Perez cruised to his third win of the season after allowing five runs on nine hits in five innings. On a hot and muggy afternoon in Atlanta, Perez became tired after running from first to third in the fourth inning. He said his legs felt drained when he came out in the bottom half of the inning, and he gave up three runs. Perez will be facing his former team, the Dodgers, for the first time Saturday since he was traded to the Royals in the middle of the 2006 season. He last pitched against Los Angeles on May 11, 2001, as a member of the Braves. In that outing, Perez pitched 7 2/3 shutout innings, scattering five hits and getting the win. He is 2-0 with a 2.25 ERA in three career starts against the Dodgers.

home_pitcher_note: Kershaw became Coors Field's latest victim. Promoted to start against the Rockies, he was pounded for 10 hits, didn't retire a batter in the fourth inning and was charged with five earned runs. Perhaps a return to sea level will lead to his first Major League victory. He's been rushed to the big leagues and it hasn't been an easy adjustment. He threw only one changeup against the Rockies, after being sent down for three weeks to work on the pitch.
away_pitcher_note: Bergmann struggled to keep the ball in the park in his first post-All-Star break start, when he faced San Francisco. He gave up three home runs -- two to Bengie Molina and one on his first pitch to Fred Lewis -- that accounted for four of the Giants' five runs. Bergmann lasted five innings, striking out one batter and walking none.

home_pitcher_note: Kuroda had another wobbly beginning, following up his two-inning start in Arizona by allowing five runs over the first three innings at Coors Field. As bad as it sounds, he was victimized by some flukey hits and he stopped the damage there, finishing up with three scoreless innings. This start against the Giants should indicate which is the real Kuroda.
away_pitcher_note: Correia emerged with a no-decision from his last outing against Washington, although he blanked the Nationals for four innings. He yielded an unearned run in the fifth before crumbling in the sixth, when he allowed three runs. The one big inning has been Correia's undoing for much of the season. Still, he called this game one of his best of the year, particularly since it followed a 3 2/3-inning, seven-run effort at Chicago.
summary: 2008-07-28 - San Francisco Giants (7) @ Los Angeles Dodgers (6) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Johnson will make his first start with the Dodgers after allowing two runs in seven innings in two long-relief outings since being called up after the All-Star break. He was originally supposed to start July 22 against the Rockies before the Dodgers called up rookie Clayton Kershaw from Double-A. Johnson, who pitches with an insulin pump, has started 214 Major League games and gone 55-98 with a 4.98 in his career, earning a reputation as an innings eater. He may get a second start on Sunday but will likely be bumped when Brad Penny returns to the rotation, which could happen as early as Aug. 5.
away_pitcher_note: Cain will be hard-pressed to duplicate his previous outing, a four-hit shutout against Washington. He fashioned his gem largely by issuing no walks for only the third start of his career. Cain has never beaten the Dodgers, posting an 0-4 record against them with a 5.30 ERA lifetime. This year, he pitched 5 2/3 innings at Dodger Stadium in an April 1 no-decision before losing to L.A. on July 6, when he surrendered five runs and eight hits in six innings.
summary: 2008-07-29 - San Francisco Giants (0) @ Los Angeles Dodgers (2) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Billingsley provided a much-needed quality start for his club on Friday, surrendering just two runs on five hits and three walks, while notching four strikeouts in 7 2/3 innings against the Nationals. In the process, he improved his record to 10-9.
away_pitcher_note: In the second inning of his last start, Sanchez allowed more runs (five) than he previously surrendered in any game since June 12. Following a quick first frame, the lefty walked two, gave up a single and three doubles in the second. He was pulled in the third after throwing 81 pitches (46 strikes). Sanchez's breaking ball wasn't breaking, and, alas, he tallied just two strikeouts
summary: 2008-07-30 - San Francisco Giants (0) @ Los Angeles Dodgers (4) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Lowe had his sinker working on Saturday, holding the Nationals to just one hit over eight outstanding innings. The sinkerballer walked just one and struck out four, showing that when his stuff is on, he's very difficult to beat. Lowe has a win and a no-decision in two starts against the D-backs this season.
away_pitcher_note: Webb seemed to have better command of his sinker in his last start against the Giants. He battled Tim Lincecum in that game before prevailing 5-3 thanks to a three-run eighth inning rally off the Giants bullpen. Webb allowed three runs on four hits over seven innings. Two of the runs came on a two-out bloop single to center by Aaron Rowand on a sinker that was nearly in the dirt.

home_pitcher_note: Kershaw produced his best outing of the season Sunday against the Nationals. He threw six-plus scoreless innings to pick up his first career victory, yielding four hits and a walk without allowing a runner to reach third. He also struck out five in his economical 86-pitch effort. The rookie established his fastball and curveball early while pitching aggressively and getting ahead in the count. That came on the heels of his five-run, 10-hit shellacking in three innings July 22 in Colorado. Kershaw has given up three runs or fewer in seven of his 10 outings.
away_pitcher_note: Johnson is riding a scoreless-innings streak of 15 as well as a four-start winning streak. The left-hander was on top of his game against the Giants last Sunday as he tossed seven shutout innings. It was the second straight start in which he held the opposition scoreless for seven frames. Johnson is eight wins away from 300 for his career. Johnson didn't allow a walk against the Giants and has given up just two free passes in his last 26 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Kuroda committed a mental lapse of throwing to the wrong base and it opened the door for a five-run rally with two outs by the Giants. He lasted only 3 2/3 innings in that game, one start after allowing five runs in six innings in Colorado, which was one start after his two-inning outing in Arizona coming out of the break. His three-start ERA is 13.11.
away_pitcher_note: Petit takes over the spot in the rotation of the recently demoted Micah Owings. Petit has pitched well in two spot starts this year, both in place of Owings. Against the Brewers on July 2, he allowed one run over six innings. His other start was July 22 against the Cubs and he allowed one run over five innings in that one. Petit doesn't have an overpowering fastball but mixes his pitches well and has a good feel for how to attack hitters.

home_pitcher_note: Johnson came up clutch in his first Dodgers start, throwing six scoreless inning in a win over the Giants. It was his first Major League victory in two years, but this could be his last start in a while with Brad Penny possibly returning from the disabled list next weekend. Johnson complained that his command was lacking, although you couldn't tell by the fact that he had no walks.
away_pitcher_note: Davis is coming off his best outing of the year. In his last start in San Diego, Davis took a perfect game into the seventh inning, but eventually allowed a base hit to Padres outfielder Brian Giles. Still, Davis picked up the win, finishing the game allowing just two hits and no runs in 7 2/3 innings. Davis is 2-2 with a 1.40 ERA in his career at Dodger Stadium.

home_pitcher_note: Carpenter will try to stretch it past four innings in his first home start since undergoing Tommy John elbow ligament replacement surgery. He'll likely be on an increased, but still limited, pitch count. That means a major key for the right-hander will be getting off to a good start, so he doesn't use up all of his pitches in the first two or three innings. His pattern in rehab starts as well as his first regular-season start was a slow beginning, followed by significant improvement.
away_pitcher_note: You don't often see shutouts end with a play at the plate, but as Billingsley said, he'll take it. He beat the Giants with a five-hitter and is 7-2 since mid-June. He leads the rotation in all the pertinent categories: victories, strikeouts, innings, etc. He's become the latest staff ace, even though he just turned 24.
summary: 2008-08-05 - Los Angeles Dodgers (4) @ St. Louis Cardinals (6) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Pineiro struggled again Thursday, allowing 10 hits for the fourth consecutive start. The right-hander had no explanation for his recent struggles, other than saying that he was missing up in the zone with most of his pitches. Pineiro also failed to hold onto a lead for the 16th time in 18 chances this season. Thus, he only has three wins. Pineiro has only faced the Dodgers once, on June 20, 2006, when he allowed three runs on 10 hits in 6 1/3 innings and won.
away_pitcher_note: Derek Lowe played his familiar role of tough-luck loser against the D-backs, allowing two runs and losing, receiving only one run from his offense. In his nine losses, the Dodgers have scored 10 runs. On the other hand, he was given a lead to protect and immediately gave it up. The 3.70 ERA is a better indication of his season than the win-loss record.
summary: 2008-08-06 - Los Angeles Dodgers (6) @ St. Louis Cardinals (9) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Making a start against the Phillies, Lohse had to endure one of his toughest starts of the season against a team that had won six games in a row. But he shut them down through his first five innings, only to allow a three-run home run in the sixth inning. Now he has yet another tough assignment against the Dodgers and will have to face slugger Manny Ramirez if he wants to cash in on tying a career high in wins.
away_pitcher_note: Against the Diamondbacks, Kershaw duplicated the six scoreless innings of his previous start, allowing only four hits and pitching out of two jams with runners on third base. Although he settled for a no-decision, he now has given up three runs or fewer in eight of his 11 outings and seems to have secured a regular slot in the rotation.
summary: 2008-08-07 - Los Angeles Dodgers (4) @ St. Louis Cardinals (1) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Zito looked like the Zito of old in his last start against the San Diego Padres on August 2, going eight shutout innings while allowing only three hits and giving up four walks while striking out five. Zito threw 116 pitches and outdueled the Padresʼ Jake Peavy in a battle of former Cy Young Award winners. It was a game that showed that Zito could still be the Cy Young Award-winning Zito and not the Zito who is currently 6-13 on the season. He pitched out of jams and didn't allow the Padres to get into any sort of offensive rhythm.
away_pitcher_note: Penny is scheduled to return from the disabled list to make his first start since June 14, after which he went on the disabled list with a sore right shoulder. The big right-hander came away fine from Saturday's Minor League rehab stint with Triple-A Las Vegas in which he allowed four runs on six hits, reaching 98 mph with his fastball. Manager Joe Torre said Penny could throw around 90 pitches in this outing. Penny had lost seven straight decisions before being placed on the DL, going winless since May 2.
summary: 2008-08-08 - Los Angeles Dodgers (6) @ San Francisco Giants (2) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Correia was solid in his last outing against the Padres on August 3, going 6 1/3 innings allowing two runs on three hits with four walks and two strikeouts but ending up with a loss. The walks came back to bite him, as two of his walks were in a second inning that saw the Padres cross their first run across the plate. Two more walks loaded the bases for the Padres' second run of the game and the last run against Correia. Minus the walks, the game might have been different, as he continued to hold his own in a matchup that put him up against future Hall of Famer Greg Maddux.
away_pitcher_note: Kuroda rebounded after three consecutive poor starts coming out of the All-Star break to beat the Diamondbacks, although it didn't hurt to have the buzz of Manny Ramirez's first game as a Dodger for inspiration. Still, he allowed only one run on four hits in 7 1/3 innings with six strikeouts and no walks. He was able to finish off breaking balls, which was a problem in the three previous starts.
summary: 2008-08-09 - Los Angeles Dodgers (2) @ San Francisco Giants (3) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: It's safe to say Cain is on a roll following a bumpy June and early July. In his past three starts, the righty has limited opponents to one run or less, including his win against the Braves in his last outing. In 6 2/3 innings, Cain allowed a lone run despite walking five -- he hadn't issued a free pass in his previous two starts. He attacked batters with his over-powering fastball, notching his seventh win, matching his 2007 total.
away_pitcher_note: There was nothing wrong with Billingsley's follow-up to his first shutout as he pitched five strong innings in St. Louis, but two rain delays shortened his outing. He was charged with one run and struck out six without a walk. He lowered his ERA t0 3.01, lowest among Dodgers starters.
summary: 2008-08-10 - Los Angeles Dodgers (4) @ San Francisco Giants (5) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: For the second straight start, Lowe was given a lead by his offense and couldn't protect it. Instead, he had his worst start and earliest exit of the year, pounded for eight runs on 13 hits in only 3 1/3 innings. Lowe's ERA at Dodger Stadium is 2.72; on the road it's 5.88. He's 3-1 with a 2.84 lifetime against the Phillies.
away_pitcher_note: Kendrick held the Marlins scoreless on four hits in beating them on Wednesday night at Citizens Bank Park. Though he walked five, he was able to successfully work out of pressure situations. Kendrick was pleased with how well his sinker was working against Florida, a pitch he relies on heavily. The 23-year-old has made two starts against the Dodgers, going 1-1 with a 6.75 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: In his last three starts, the 20-year-old Kershaw has gotten very good. He didn't quite match his back-to-back six scoreless innings of his previous two starts, but in his most recent start he might have been more impressive in limiting the Cardinals to one run over seven innings because of the way their explosive offense had scored 15 runs the two previous games. Kershaw has never faced the Phillies.
away_pitcher_note: Hamels has now gone six consecutive starts without earning a win, the longest winless drought of his career. In that span, Hamels has been hit hard at times, but also fallen victim to a lack of run support, such as his loss to the Marlins on Thursday afternoon. Hamels tossed 6 1/3 innings, allowing three runs -- two earned -- as the Phils were shut out for the seventh time in 2008. During his past six starts, the 24-year-old is 0-3. Hamels has never faced the Dodgers.

home_pitcher_note: Penny returned from seven weeks on the disabled list and looked like he had just been on the disabled list, rarely surpassing 90 mph with his fastball. Somehow, he limited the Giants to only one hit in five innings and snapped a seven-game losing streak with his first win since May 2. But he walked three without a strikeout, further evidence of his rustiness.
away_pitcher_note: Though the Phillies ended up losing on Friday to the Pirates, Joe Blanton came up big, tossing seven innings of one-hit ball. In four games with the Phils, he has just one win, but he has compiled a solid 3.27 ERA and has held batters to just a .205 average.

home_pitcher_note: Kuroda is coming off back-to-back strong starts, now that he is able to finish off breaking balls without worrying about his shoulder being sore. In his most recent start, the only run he allowed the Giants in eight innings scored on a sacrifice fly in an inning extended by a wild pitch third strike. It was the fourth time this year he's pitched at least eight innings. He's never faced Milwaukee.
away_pitcher_note: Myers is cruising since his return from a July Minor League stint, recording a 2-0 record with a 2.10 ERA since re-joining the Phils. On Saturday night, he limited the Pirates to one run in 7 2/3 innings, striking out six and walking one. Myers' competitive spirit got the best of him as he exchanged heated words with manager Charlie Manuel when the skipper removed him in the eighth. In nine career starts against the Dodgers, Myers is 3-1 with a 2.76 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Against the Giants, Billingsley did a high-wire act, pitching into and out of jams in five of his six innings, allowing three runs on nine hits, but stranding nine baserunners. He kept the ball in the park, and a two-run inning off him needed a bloop double to drop. He struck out six, but walked three. He's never started against the Brewers.
away_pitcher_note: Following complete-game shutout gems from CC Sabathia and Ben Sheets in the first two games of the Brewers series against the Nationals, Parra delivered one of his best starts of the season in his last outing. The lefty allowed just six hits through seven innings, walking none and tying a career-high with nine strikeouts.  He left the game with the score tied at one run apiece and got no decision as Milwaukee took the back-and-forth game in 13 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Lowe bounced back from his worst start of the season by throwing a quality start Monday against the Phillies, giving up three runs on five hits in 6 1/3 innings. Lowe's sinker worked as he induced 13 groundouts and just three flyouts besides striking out three. In his outing before that, Aug. 6 at St. Louis, he served up season highs in runs (eight) and hits (13) in 3 1/3 innings of a loss. Lowe has compiled a 1.78 ERA while going 3-2 in his last five starts at Dodger Stadium.
away_pitcher_note: Bush has been sharp since manager Ned Yost abandoned his fifth starter platoon between Bush and Seth McClung. In two starts since the move, Bush has allowed two earned runs and eight hits in 13 1/3 innings for victories at Cincinnati and at home against Washington. The road win over the Reds was encouraging, but Bush is 2-6 with a 6.19 ERA in his 10 appearances away from home, nine of them starts. He lost his only career start at Dodger Stadium, in 2006, allowing four earned runs in six innings of a 10-2 Brewers loss.

home_pitcher_note: Kershaw wasn't quite as sharp as his previous three starts, but he gave his team a chance to win. He allowed three runs in six innings with a career-high eight strikeouts. He served up a solo homer to Chase Utley and allowed a steal of third that turned into a run. He also struck out Ryan Howard twice.
away_pitcher_note: Suppan has been outstanding in three starts since his dismal July 27 outing against the Astros. On Tuesday, he held the Padres to two runs on four hits over eight innings, and over his three starts since he allowed eight runs in six innings against Houston, Suppan is 3-0 with a 2.05 ERA (five earned runs in 22 innings). The Brewers hope Suppan continues his trend as a second-half pitcher. In 2007, his first year with Milwaukee, Suppan posted a 5.00 ERA before the All-Star break, but lowered it to 4.12 afterward. Over the previous three years, Suppan had a 4.98 ERA before the All-Star break and a 3.09 ERA after it.

home_pitcher_note: Kuroda has his act back together, having posted his third consecutive strong outing by pitching a two-hitter for seven innings against Philadelphia. Kuroda has overcome the mental block about getting full extension on his slider and the pitch is now as sharp as it was when he threw two shutouts. He made only 79 pitches against the Phillies and has a 1.21 ERA over his last three starts.
away_pitcher_note: Jimenez labored through six innings Tuesday, throwing 108 pitches and giving up four runs on 11 hits against the D-backs. While he clearly didn't have his best stuff, Jimenez kept the Rockies in the game by striking out four and wiggling his way through several jams. The right-hander struggled in his last outing against Washington on Aug. 7. He gave up six runs on eight hits in five innings to take the loss.

home_pitcher_note: Billingsley allowed the Brewers three runs on four hits in the first two innings before shutting them down on one hit over the next five innings. He's won his last three decisions and eight of his last 10. Billingsley is 0-2 lifetime with a 6.46 ERA against the Rockies and hasn't faced them yet this year.
away_pitcher_note: Francis, in his second start since returning from missing time with a shoulder injury, displayed his old velocity and command in his most recent start, when he gave up three runs over six innings of a no-decision against the D-backs.

home_pitcher_note: Lowe's standout start against the tough Milwaukee lineup got lost in the late-inning back and forth, but he pitched well enough to deserve a 10th win. He allowed only one run over seven innings without a walk and as soon as manager Joe Torre gave the game to the bullpen, everything unraveled. Lowe hasn't been the most consistent as a Dodger, but he has been an innings-eater.
away_pitcher_note: De La Rosa's strong start against the Nationals on Friday -- when he went six innings, struck out seven and gave up three hits in a win -- and the fact he's been on more than off since the All-Star break, have earned him a chance to stay in the rotation and prove that he's viable there in the future.

home_pitcher_note: Kendrick is finding it increasingly difficult to survive when his sinker isn't quite right. After a strong rookie season and a promising start to 2008, the sophomore has compiled a 6.90 ERA in his past six outings. He was unable to last five innings for the sixth time this season, and allowed six or more runs for the fifth time. That happened once each last season.
away_pitcher_note: Look who's back. Maddux resumes his Dodgers career, acquired to replace the injured Brad Penny in the starting rotation. Maddux was slipped into this start because he just did a pretty good job neutralizing the potent Phillies lineup, allowing only a solo home run to Pat Burrell in seven innings for the Padres last week. Putting Maddux back to back with rookie Clayton Kershaw could result in some short starts and put a burden on the bullpen.

home_pitcher_note: Hamels' brilliance finally translated into a win, as he broke a seven-start stretch in which he went 0-3 with four no-decisions. He went eight innings against San Diego and allowed one run in his hometown. He's starting against the Dodgers for the second time this month. He limited them to two runs in seven innings on Aug. 12, but Chad Durbin allowed the tying runs to score in the eighth.
away_pitcher_note: Kershaw continued his impressive turnaround against Milwaukee's potent lineup with a fifth consecutive quality start, during which his ERA is 1.45. It might have been a win, but manager Joe Torre is exercising a quick hook with Kershaw, more to protect his young arm than to indicate he can't get the job done. Against the Brewers, Kershaw allowed only one run in six innings on 96 pitches.

home_pitcher_note: Though his ERA in August is 3.38, Blanton is coming off a second straight outing in which he allowed four earned runs in five innings. He received no-decisions in each of those starts. The first of the two came against the Dodgers, on Aug. 13, when the right-hander struggled to protect a 6-1 lead.
away_pitcher_note: Kuroda allowed the explosive Rockies lineup four runs over the first 2 1/3 innings, then held them scoreless over the next 3 2/3 innings. He served up a home run to Brad Hawpe immediately after taking a smash off his left ankle. He said it didn't effect him on the pitch and wasn't sore afterward, but it was heavily taped to minimize swelling and could pose a problem in his next start.

home_pitcher_note: Myers has been a completely different pitcher than the one who compiled a 5.84 ERA through June 27 and required a head-clearing trip to the Minors. In six stats since his return, the right-hander has posted a 1.94 ERA and the team has won four of those outings. He's coming off a shutout of the Nationals, his first shutout in more than four years, and he's restored the organization's confidence in him.
away_pitcher_note: Billingsley left his most recent start against the Rockies leading, but the victory got away when the bullpen allowed an unearned tying run. Nonetheless, he pitched in with another quality start, grinding out six innings despite allowing baserunners in each of them. His key moment was pitching into a bases-loaded situation with no outs and limiting the damage to only one run.

home_pitcher_note: Last Wednesday, Balester gave the Nationals six effective innings, giving up three earned runs, but Washington couldn't push a run across despite notching nine hits off Philadelphia starter Brett Myers. Balester is on a personal three-game losing streak.
away_pitcher_note: Lowe remains on a short leash. Once known as an innings eater, he was lifted with a 2-1 lead after issuing a one-out walk in the seventh inning against the Rockies, having thrown 107 pitches. He allowed four hits and struck out seven. He also has double figures in wins in seven consecutive seasons. Lowe went 8-1 two years ago after Greg Maddux was acquired and he's 1-0 this year with Maddux as a teammate.

home_pitcher_note: He hasn't won a game since Aug 4 and had a good month since May, when he went 3-1 with a 3.86 ERA. In his last start, however, he pitched six innings and gave up one run against the Phillies.
away_pitcher_note: In his first start since returning to the Dodgers, Maddux cruised through his first three on Friday in Philadelphia, facing the minimum while throwing just 23 pitches. Then he struggled, yielding seven runs on nine hits and completing 5 2/3 innings, the knockout blow being Chris Coste's three-run homer after Ryan Howard took him deep earlier. Maddux had been pitching great in August for San Diego before being traded to Los Angeles, compiling a 2-1 record and a 1.89 ERA in three quality starts.

home_pitcher_note: Lannan had a so-so start, as he allowed five runs in 6 1/3 innings against the Cubs last Friday. Chicago didn't waste time scoring runs early against him. In the first inning, Alfonso Soriano swiped home on a double steal for the game's first run. Two innings later, Derrek Lee drilled a home run over the left-field wall. In the bottom of the fourth, Mark DeRosa hit a two-run homer. After watching his team score the six runs in the sixth, Lannan settled down a little bit, allowing just one run over his final 1 1/3 innings. Despite the mediocre outing, Lannan needed just 84 pitches in the game.
away_pitcher_note: After five straight quality outings, Kershaw encountered some difficulties Saturday in Philly, allowing six runs on seven hits in four-plus innings. He pitched fairly well after giving up a three-run homer three batters into the game, but a ball misplayed by Matt Kemp in center led to the three other runs. Kershaw entered the game with a 1.45 ERA in his five previous starts, beginning with his first career Major League win July 27 against the Nationals, when he threw six shutout innings.

home_pitcher_note: Amid concerns of a stiff back, Davis had one of his better outings on Sunday, when he limited the Marlins to three runs in seven innings. For the first time all season, he didn't walk a batter, but he still was outpitched by Marlins starter Ricky Nolasco. Against the Dodgers, Davis is 1-1 this season in three starts.
away_pitcher_note: Kuroda dominated the Phillies for the second straight start Sunday evening, giving up one run on two hits in six innings. Kuroda has thrived in August after a rough end to July, compiling a 3-1 mark and a 2.10 ERA this month while yielding one run in four of his five starts. That stretch started with a one-run, seven-inning win over the D-backs at Dodger Stadium, but Arizona has hit him in his two starts in Phoenix.

home_pitcher_note: Haren pitched well against the Padres his last time out. The right-hander allowed two runs on nine hits over seven innings of work. He struck out a season-high 11, the third time in his career that he has reached double digits in strikeouts. While he gave up plenty of hits, Haren was able to pitch out of jams adjusted from his previous start against the Padres, when they jumped on him for three runs in the first inning.
away_pitcher_note: Billingsley tossed another quality start on Monday in Philadelphia, giving up three runs on seven hits in six innings despite struggling at times with his control, as he walked five (two intentional) and ran up a pitch count of 107. Still, the outing accounted for his ninth consecutive start in which he's yielded three runs or less, and he's compiled a 3.04 ERA in that time. Billingsley has struggled against the D-backs this year, going 0-3 with a 7.71 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: In his quest to become the National League's first 20-game winner since 2005, Webb was knocked around by the Padres at PETCO Park the last time out, as he allowed six runs and didn't even last five innings for just the second time all season. Webb had one bad inning and gave up a three-run homer to Brian Giles. Maybe pitching under the national limelight on ESPN against the Dodgers -- a team he has had great success against in his career -- will help him get win No. 20.
away_pitcher_note: Lowe did not deserve to lose Tuesday's start in Washington when he threw a complete game of eight innings and gave up just two runs on six hits, but the Dodgers' struggling offense made that so. After a disaster outing in St. Louis, Lowe has thrown four straight quality starts, compiling a 2.28 ERA in that time. He is 1-1 with a 3.78 ERA in three outings against Arizona.

home_pitcher_note: Maddux gave up four runs (two earned) on eight hits in 5 1/3 innings Wednesday against the Nationals. He did not strike out a batter and walked just one. The future Hall of Famer has not provided the Dodgers with the impact they were hoping for in his first two starts, yielding 17 hits in 11 innings and compiling an ERA of 7.36. It will be interesting to see how he fares in his first outing against the Padres since they traded him to Los Angeles on Aug. 19.
away_pitcher_note: Young will be activated from the disabled list before his start against the Dodgers. Young suffered a strained forearm in a start against Colorado on Aug. 10, which was just his third effort back from missing 59 games after being hit in the face with a line drive in a game in May. He threw 65 pitches in a simulated game on Tuesday and reported no pain in his forearm.
summary: 2008-09-01 - San Diego Padres (2) @ Los Angeles Dodgers (5) (Final)

Before that, his five previous outings were considered quality starts in which he went 2-0 with a 1.45 ERA. Kershaw was optioned to Triple-A after the game to add bullpen depth but will be back for this start.
away_pitcher_note: Baek pitched well in his last start, a loss to the Diamondbacks on Aug. 27, when he allowed two runs on six hits over 5 2/3 innings. Otherwise, Baek continues to pitch well in stretches during what amounts to an open tryout for a spot in the Padres' 2009 starting rotation. Baek struck out three Diamondbacks and walked one in his last start.
summary: 2008-09-02 - San Diego Padres (4) @ Los Angeles Dodgers (8) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Kuroda retired the first 10 D-backs he faced and appeared on his way to another dominating performance, but a bloop single led to one run and a Nomar Garciaparra throwing error led to two more unearned runs, and the Dodgers had to hit for Kuroda in the sixth. He struck out four and walked only one in five innings, his shortest outing in a month.
away_pitcher_note: LeBlanc, recalled Monday from Triple-A Portland, will make his Major League debut against Los Angeles in the final game of a three-game series at Dodger Stadium. summary: 2008-09-03 - San Diego Padres (4) @ Los Angeles Dodgers (6) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Lowe stepped up big time his last time out and outdueled Brandon Webb with Lowe's seventh quality start in his last eight appearances. He will switch spots in the rotation with Chad Billingsley to remain on a five-day cycle and, more importantly, avoid pitching at Coors Field later this month.
away_pitcher_note: Haren said he is going through a mechanical funk. In six starts in August, Haren had a 5.63 ERA and gave up six homers, raising his ERA from 2.62 to 3.24. D-backs manager Bob Melvin thinks Haren may have to adjust his approach now that National League teams are starting to see more of the right-hander. home_pitcher_note: Blessed with a lead Saturday, Billingsley knew what to do with it. He's gone 10 consecutive starts without allowing more than three runs and has pitched at least six innings in seven of his last eight starts.
away_pitcher_note: For the second straight outing, Webb was roughed up by a National League West rival in search of his 20th win of the season. Webb lasted just 3 1/3 innings against the Dodgers on Sunday night, allowing eight runs -- six earned -- on eight hits. The ace also couldn't find the plate, as he had five walks -- two intentional. The Dodgers put the game out of reach in the first inning when Andre Ethier hit a solo home run and Casey Blake hit a three-run shot four batters later.

home_pitcher_note: Kershaw rebounded from a pair of poor outings on the road with a masterful performance Tuesday against the Padres. Kershaw credited a tip from Derek Lowe to keep his front leg back in part for his stellar outing. He had racked up a 15.63 ERA in his previous two starts, both losses, but went 2-0 with a 1.45 ERA in five consecutive quality starts before that.
away_pitcher_note: Scherzer will get Sunday's start in place of Randy Johnson, who is suffering from what the club says is left shoulder fatigue. This is expected to be a one-start break for Johnson, who is next scheduled to pitch on Aug. 13. Scherzer was 1-1 with a 2.72 ERA in 13 games (10 starts) for Triple-A Tucson. He made his Major League debut on April 29 against the Astros and fanned seven in 4 1/3 innings to set an Arizona record for a pitcher making his debut. Scherzer has held right-handers to a .159 average in the big leagues.

home_pitcher_note: Baek might not be too excited about the prospect of facing the Dodgers for the second time in less than a week. Baek lasted 3 2/3 innings in his last start against the Dodgers on Tuesday, allowing a two-run home run to Manny Ramirez and a solo home run to Blake DeWitt. Baek allowed seven earned runs on eight hits with two walks as he struggled with his command.
away_pitcher_note: After losing his first two starts since rejoining the Dodgers, Maddux rebounded against his former club, the Padres. He allowed two runs in 5 2/3 innings and added an RBI single. Although six innings is about the max for Maddux at age 42, that really is no longer an issue for the Dodgers now that rosters have expanded, as long as he's as effective as he was against the Padres.
summary: 2008-09-08 - Los Angeles Dodgers (0) @ San Diego Padres (4) (Final)

All told, LeBlanc allowed five runs on eight hits with three walks. He pitched behind in the count most of the game in a 100-pitch stint over four innings.
away_pitcher_note: Kuroda will make his second straight start against the Padres after beating them Wednesday in an up-and-down performance, giving up four runs on 10 hits in 5 1/3 innings. Kuroda has now failed to get through the sixth in consecutive starts after doing so in his previous five outings. The right-hander hopes to build on his strong August in which he went 2-2 with a 2.29 ERA and yielded a single run in four of his six starts.
summary: 2008-09-09 - Los Angeles Dodgers (6) @ San Diego Padres (2) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Estes, back from a fractured thumb, impressed in his first start in more than three months his last time out. The veteran lefty held Milwaukee to one run in six innings, scattering seven hits for the win. Estes got a lot of help from third baseman Kevin Kouzmanoff and only struck out one, but the outing was a step in the right direction for a guy who's trying to showcase his stuff to get a contract for next season. Estes hasn't faced the Dodgers since 2005.
away_pitcher_note: In his last two starts, Lowe has defeated Arizona's Brandon Webb and Dan Haren. He's on the best roll of the season, going 3-1 in his last five starts with a 1.02 ERA, not to mention 19 consecutive scoreless innings. He's the only pitcher in the Major Leagues with at least 12 victories in each of the last seven years and he leads the club in innings pitched. His spot in the rotation was juggled to make sure he would start in San Diego and not in Colorado.
summary: 2008-09-10 - Los Angeles Dodgers (7) @ San Diego Padres (2) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Francis pitched extremely well for the second straight outing, a good sign that the left shoulder troubles that plagued him earlier this season have completely subsided. Unfortunately for Francis, he went up against two aces -- Jake Peavy and Roy Oswalt -- and went 0-1 in the two games. The lefty made just one mistake against the Astros on Saturday, leaving a changeup up in the strike zone that was pounded for a two-run home run. However, Francis has given up just three runs on 13 hits in his past 13 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Billingsley threw another gem on Saturday against the D-backs, yielding four hits and a walk in 6 1/3 scoreless innings, striking out nine. Billingsley -- Los Angeles' leader in wins, ERA and strikeouts -- has now gone 11 straight outings without allowing more than three runs, a period in which he's 6-2 with a 2.48 ERA. The right-hander is 0-2 with an 8.76 ERA in three career outings (two starts) at Colorado, but he threw six innings of two-run ball on Aug. 20 against the Rockies at Dodger Stadium.

home_pitcher_note: De La Rosa had been dominant in his past three outings before Sunday, giving up just two runs in 19 innings. But he struggled with his command against the Astros, giving up four runs on six hits and walking four in 5 1/3 innings. De La Rosa surrendered just one run in six innings the last time he faced the Dodgers on Aug. 21.
away_pitcher_note: In his last outing, Kershaw had a difficult start against the Diamondbacks. The left-hander pitched out of a bases-loaded jam in the first inning, but he couldn't protect a two-run lead while allowing home runs to Chris Snyder and Adam Dunn. Kershaw's pitch count soared, and he was lifted after four innings, even though he walked only one batter. This next start will be in Coors Field, where Kershaw was pounded for five runs on 10 hits in three innings by the Rockies on July 22.

home_pitcher_note: Cook has been stymied twice in his attempt to match Kevin Ritz (1996), Pedro Astacio (1999) and Jeff Francis (2007) for the club single-season record for victories (17). The first time, against the Giants, he lasted just three innings. The second time, he gave up three first-inning runs against the Braves, and four runs total before leaving too early for a decision. Cook said the Braves hit a couple of good pitches during the first, and he felt he was in a better place mechanically.
away_pitcher_note: After beating his former Padres teammates in Los Angeles, Maddux lost to them in San Diego, allowing four runs over six innings. The Dodgers were blanked, so Maddux had little chance, but he trailed almost from the start, allowing a two-run homer to Adrian Gonzalez in the first inning. Maddux is 1-3 since joining the Dodgers for the stretch run, with two of the losses coming against last-place teams (Washington was the other).

home_pitcher_note: The high-90s velocity that Ohlendorf was said to possess has still not shown itself in a Pirates uniform. That would be OK if he substituted some velocity for command, but that wasn't the case in his most recent outing. Ohlendorf allowed six runs on nine hits against the Astros and was bumped from the game after four innings with his velocity hovering in the mid-90s. It will likely not creep much higher during these final two weeks of the season. Ohlendorf continues to audition for a starting spot and will be making his first career appearance against the Dodgers with this start.
away_pitcher_note: Kuroda delivered a gritty performance with little support in his 10th no-decision at San Diego. Lacking a go-to pitch all night, he allowed nine hits and had to pitch out of trouble four of his six innings, but allowed only two runs. He'll be pitching in Pittsburgh for the first time and allowed the Pirates three runs in 6 2/3 innings in a no-decision at home April 14.

home_pitcher_note: Karstens made quite a first impression upon arriving in a trade with the Yankees, throwing 15 shutout innings in his first two starts, the second one a complete game. His five starts since then, however, were mediocre to bleak and he lost all of them. He allowed eight runs in three innings to the Giants in his last start.
away_pitcher_note: Derek Lowe expects to be fine for this start against Pittsburgh, although he was driven from last week's outing in San Diego after taking a comebacker off the back of his right knee. He allowed one earned run in 5 1/3 innings to continue his late-season roll, having won his last three decisions and four of his last five. He's allowed five runs in 40 2/3 innings (1.11 ERA).

home_pitcher_note: Though Duke started out extremely sharp in his last outing against the Astros, he was undone by some fielding errors and then by his own poor pitch location. Duke came into that start after putting together one of his better stretches this season. He had thrown at least six innings in six consecutive starts, though he lasted just 4 2/3 against Houston. With only two more starts left this season, Duke will look to improve on the results he had against the Dodgers in a start against them back in April. Duke allowed four runs -- three earned -- in six innings in that outing.
away_pitcher_note: Billingsley came into Coors Field with an 8.76 ERA in Denver, but he delivered a solid start, allowing two runs over six innings. It wasn't overpowering, as he struck out three and stranded five Rockies in scoring position. He leads club starters in wins, ERA and strikeouts, and has gone 12 straight outings without allowing more than three runs, a time in which he's 7-2 with a 2.52 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Maholm shows no signs of wearing down as the season comes to an end, putting in a performance in his last outing as good as any he's had this season. Though he fell just short of notching his first shutout of the season, Maholm pitched eight strong innings on his way to another dominant victory. He is approaching the 200-inning count rapidly, which may force the Pirates to be more hesitant to extend him in his final two starts. Maholm will get another shot at the Dodgers after losing to L.A. in April, when he allowed six runs (four earned) in five innings.
away_pitcher_note: Kershaw made all the right adjustments, rebounding not only from four shaky innings in his most recent start, but the kind of Coors Field debut that can leave a 20-year-old pitcher permanently scarred. Instead, he allowed only one run on four hits over six innings. He was able to do it by relying on a curveball in the thin air, and not many can do that. He'll be facing the Pirates for the first time in his career.

home_pitcher_note: Maddux put on a clinic for pitching in Coors Field. He came away with a tough-luck no-decision because the Dodgers couldn't score off Aaron Cook. Maddux is 30-14 lifetime against the Giants, 2-0 with a 1.38 ERA this year.
away_pitcher_note: Zito admitted that he lacked rhythm in his last start, when he allowed six runs -- five earned -- in 4 2/3 innings at San Diego. In five starts before that, though, Zito was 3-1 with a 3.90 ERA. He'll be returning to the scene of his Opening Day start, in which he allowed four runs in five innings as San Francisco lost, 5-0. Zito beat the Dodgers on July 5 at AT&T Park by striking out 10 while yielding two runs in seven innings, but he couldn't duplicate that magic on Aug. 8 at home, surrendering five runs in five innings in a 6-2 loss.
summary: 2008-09-19 - San Francisco Giants (7) @ Los Angeles Dodgers (1) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Kuroda was deprived of his third shutout of the season only because manager Joe Torre needed the last two innings as an impromptu rehab assignment for Takashi Saito and Brad Penny. Kuroda allowed only three hits and one walk over seven scoreless innings and used only 83 pitches. Despite the losing record on the season, he lowered his ERA to 3.77. He'll be facing the Giants, who have knocked him around for eight runs in 11 2/3 innings over two starts.
away_pitcher_note: Hennessey's coming off his first Major League complete game, though it probably wasn't the experience he had envisioned. He yielded Adam Dunn's two-run, tiebreaking homer with two outs in the eighth inning last Monday that gave Arizona a 3-1 victory. Hennessey's durability -- 14 innings in two starts since replacing Kevin Correia in the No. 5 spot in San Francisco's rotation -- is no surprise. He pitched three complete games this year with Triple-A Fresno. Hennessey faced the Dodgers in relief on April 1, allowing two runs in two-thirds of an inning.
summary: 2008-09-20 - San Francisco Giants (7) @ Los Angeles Dodgers (10) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Lowe had no lingering effects from his early departure in San Diego, when he was struck on the knee by a comebacker. His ERA over his last 47 2/3 innings is innings is 1.13, bringing his overall ERA from 4.10 to 3.40.
away_pitcher_note: After recording a 7.71 ERA in his previous four starts, Cain sparkled at Arizona last Tuesday, allowing two runs and seven hits in seven innings. Unfortunately for Cain and the Giants, they couldn't score for him, marking the seventh time this year they've been blanked while he's on the mound. The 23-year-old Cain has provided plenty of highlights in his three-plus seasons with the Giants, but beating the Dodgers isn't one of them. He's 0-5 against them lifetime, including 0-2 with a 3.51 ERA this year. He has thrived in two starts this season at Dodger Stadium, however, yielding two runs (one earned) in 12 2/3 innings.
summary: 2008-09-21 - San Francisco Giants (1) @ Los Angeles Dodgers (0) (Final)

Billingsley had gone 12 straight outings without allowing more than three runs, a time in which he was 7-2 with a 2.52 ERA. Billingsley is 0-2 against the Padres this year, receiving only two runs of support.
away_pitcher_note: LeBlanc hasn't been in the Major Leagues a month and yet the rookie left-hander will face the Dodgers for the third time this month. summary: 2008-09-23 - San Diego Padres (1) @ Los Angeles Dodgers (10) (Final)

Kershaw struck out five but needed 86 pitches and put a burden on the bullpen.
away_pitcher_note: Estes, one of the handful of pitchers trying to make a favorable impression in September as the team looks to 2009, didn't have a good outing in his last start on Sept. 16 against the Rockies. summary: 2008-09-24 - San Diego Padres (4) @ Los Angeles Dodgers (12) (Final)

away_pitcher_note: Peavy fell to 9-11 by allowing five runs on a season-high 11 hits in his last start, a loss on Sept. 12 to the San Francisco Giants. Offensive support continues to be an issue when Peavy pitches. The Padres have scored three or fewer runs in 14 of his 26 starts.
summary: 2008-09-25 - San Diego Padres (7) @ Los Angeles Dodgers (5) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Hennessey had pitched well in two starts since being recalled from Triple-A Fresno, compiling a 2.57 ERA and recording a complete game in a 3-1 loss at Arizona. away_pitcher_note: Blanton delivered against the Brewers in Game 4 of the NLDS, his biggest start since being traded to Philly from Oakland in mid-July.
