But while going 4-1 with a 2.09 ERA in his six July starts, he proved why he's quickly establishing himself as one of the game's top young pitchers. He went 2-0 with a 1.38 ERA in two starts against the Dodgers last year.
away_pitcher_note: Through five innings against the loaded Cardinals lineup in a scoreless duel, Billingsley was cruising with a one-hitter. Then he imploded with a pair of walks and couldn't get out of the sixth inning, charged with six earned runs and six walks (two intentional). It was the second time in three starts that he's allowed six runs. He has one win since June 14 and is 0-2 with a 5.93 ERA lifetime against the Braves.

home_pitcher_note: Kershaw couldn't pitch much better than eight scoreless innings against the Cardinals hitters, only for Jonathan Broxton to blow the save and cost Kershaw a deserved win. Since mid-June, Kershaw is pretty much the best pitcher in the game with an 0.79 ERA. He's 5-0 with four no-decisions in that time, holding opponents scoreless in five of nine starts.
away_pitcher_note: Parra walked in a pair of Nationals runs with two outs in the second inning on Wednesday but nonetheless notched the win thanks to a mid-innings Brewers comeback. Parra worked six innings and struck out seven, but, alarmingly, given his orders to throw strikes, he issued five walks. He's been charged with nine runs on 19 hits and eight walks in 11 innings over his last two starts. In other words, he remains a work in progress.

home_pitcher_note: It's taken roughly half a season, but Kuroda finally seems to be back on track after an Opening Day win followed by two months on the disabled list. A mechanical flaw has been ironed out and he's using his lower body more, which had increased the quality of all his pitches, particularly the splitter that had been an out pitch for him last year, but one he's shied away from until recently. He has only three wins, so a big second half would have the same impact as a trade for a starter.
away_pitcher_note: Gallardo delivered a much-needed gem against the Nationals on Thursday, when he fell one short of a career high with 11 strikeouts and limited the Nats to three runs and five hits in seven innings. In his last two starts, with the rest of the starting rotation in disarray, Gallardo has allowed three runs on nine hits in 14 1/3 solid innings, a good sign that the mechanical adjustments he made during and just after the All-Star break are working. He lost to the Dodgers on July 12 at Miller Park in the first-half finale, allowing five runs on six hits and four walks in five innings, and vowed to make some changes. He's never pitched a regular-season game at Dodger Stadium, though Gallardo did work five shutout innings there earlier in an April 4 exhibition.

home_pitcher_note: Jason Schmidt pitched six innings of one-hit, shutout ball against the Braves on Friday. In what might have been his last chance to show he belonged in the rotation, Schmidt pitched the way he now must against his original team in Atlanta. He kept his 87-mph fastball down, mixed in breaking balls and wasn't afraid to let hitters put the ball in play. He overcame first-inning wildness and an error-aided jam to earn another start.
away_pitcher_note: Looper's two-run single sparked a two-out, seven-run rally in the second inning of Friday's game in San Diego, but he slowly squandered away the lead he helped build. Looper surrendered four runs in the fourth inning -- the second straight outing in which he's allowed a four-spot -- and another run in the fifth before the Brewers were forced to go to the bullpen with a 7-6 lead that slipped away. The Brewers are 13-9 in Looper's starts, but have lost two straight, and he's allowed 11 runs in 11 innings in those games. "I'm going to have to pitch better and we're going to have to play better if we want to win," Looper said.

home_pitcher_note: Wolf deserved a better fate than the most recent loss in Atlanta, but that's the way his season has gone. Sloppy Dodgers defense in the seventh turned a win into a loss, although he did allow nine hits and two walks in six innings, the first non-quality start since June 24. He comes right back against the Braves at home and is 4-12 lifetime against them and 0-5 since 2004.
away_pitcher_note: Lowe beat his former teammates on Saturday in Atlanta, thanks to a late-inning comeback by his offense. After spending the past four seasons in Dodger blue, Lowe threw six innings and allowed three runs on five hits. Besides a shaky fourth inning in which he walked two batters and surrendered two runs, Lowe limited the Dodgers to a solo home run by Andre Ethier. In 66 career starts at Dodger Stadium, Lowe is 33-23 with a 3.21 ERA. His last start there came on Sept. 21 of last season, when he pitched seven shutout innings against the Giants.

home_pitcher_note: Chad Billingsley was cruising with a two-hitter in the fifth inning when he felt a slight hamstring cramp. He finished the inning, but received a quick precautionary hook from manager Joe Torre before the next inning started. Nonetheless, Billingsley struck out nine and was particuarly effective with a sharp breaking ball. He gets another shot at the Braves on Friday night.
away_pitcher_note: Jurrjens hopes to have a much better start against the Dodgers on Friday in Los Angeles than he did on Sunday in Atlanta. Jurrjens went just five innings while surrendering four earned runs in a disastrous fifth inning. After getting two outs, Jurrjens surrendered back-to-back singles before Matt Kemp hit a long three-run homer to break a scoreless tie. Jurrjens struggled with his pitch count, amassing 103 pitches in the five innings. What makes the results more frustrating is the fact that Jurrjens threw first-pitch strikes to 18 out of the 24 hitters he faced.

home_pitcher_note: For three innings Kershaw confounded Brewers hitters and breezed through the order without giving up a hit. But then in the fourth his control faltered, and the Brewers took advantage. Kershaw walked six batters in his most wild outing of the season and lost for the first time since June 10. In the fourth inning, Kershaw walked in two runs and at one point walked four consecutive batters.
away_pitcher_note: Kawakami allowed three runs (one solo homer) on eight hits in six innings on Monday, but the quality start wasn't enough without much run support from his teammates. The Braves fell, 4-2, to the Padres as they were unable to muster any runs after the second inning. Kawakami struck out four and walked none. "Kawakami was good tonight," Braves manager Bobby Cox said. "He threw a lot of strikes, didn't walk anybody, and made maybe two bad pitches."

home_pitcher_note: Hiroki Kuroda was originally slated to start this game, but will get an extra day of rest and pitch Monday in place of injured right-hander Jason Schmidt. After Saturday's loss, manager Joe Torre announced that Stults would be recalled from Triple-A Albuquerque to start this game. His last start was May 30 at Wrigley Field, where he allowed four earned runs on six hits in three innings to take the loss.
away_pitcher_note: Vazquez has made nine quality starts over his last 12 starts. In his last outing against the Padres last Tuesday he allowed two runs on four hits in seven innings. The Braves have won six of his last six starts and he has won four straight decisions, pitching seven or more innings in his last five. He struck out six in his last game and has 164 second in the National League. He is the only active major league pitcher to record at least 10 wins, 30 starts and 150 strikeouts in each of his previous nine seasons. And he will go for his 10th win against the Dodgers, who he will be facing for the first time this season.

home_pitcher_note: Sanchez won for the first time on the road this season last time out. The left-hander was 0-8 with a 6.33 ERA in nine previous starts away from AT&T Park, but he allowed no runs on four hits and struck out eight over seven-plus innings against the Houston Astros. Over his last five starts, dating back to his no-hitter on July 10, he is 3-1 with a 2.75 ERA. Sanchez is 0-1 with a 4.50 ERA in two starts against the Dodgers this season, but he hasn't faced them since May 9.
away_pitcher_note: Kuroda earned his first win of the season at Dodger Stadium on Tuesday night behind a barrage of runs from the Dodgers offense. Kuroda was solid on the mound and escaped one threat in the fourth inning. Kuroda wasn't as fortunate in the fifth as he failed to wiggle out of a similar jam.  That time Brewers batsmen tagged Kuroda for three runs on five hits. Kuroda came back out to pitch a scoreless sixth and finished the night allowing three runs on nine hits in six innings of work.
summary: 2009-08-10 - Los Angeles Dodgers (4) @ San Francisco Giants (2) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Pitching in his first Giants-Dodgers game won't rattle Martinez. After enduring the skull fractures and the concussion caused by the Mike Cameron line drive which struck him in his forehead in the season's third game, nothing should faze the 26-year-old, who won his first Major League start last Wednesday at Houston. This will be Martinez's first AT&T Park appearance since his April mishap, so expect the crowd to be solidly behind him.
away_pitcher_note: Wolf told reporters after Thursday's no-decision against the Braves that he felt he had some of his best stuff of this season on the mound that night. He also said that fact made the four runs he gave up in seven innings a little bit frustrating. Wolf kept the Dodgers within striking distance of the Braves, and his seven innings on the mound gave the bullpen an easier night. In all, Wolf pitched well and was not hit hard except for a few specific instances. Wolf is 6-4 with a 3.44 ERA in his career against the Giants.
summary: 2009-08-11 - Los Angeles Dodgers (9) @ San Francisco Giants (1) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Lincecum received a no-decision in his last outing, though he left with a 4-3 lead after seven innings against Cincinnati. Only two of the runs were earned off Lincecum, who struck out seven to increase his Major League-leading total to 198. As good as Lincecum has been, he owns an ordinary 2-2 record with a 3.05 ERA in seven daytime starts. But he's also 7-1 at home and 3-0 against the Dodgers in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Jeff Weaver gets the spot start as Chad Billingsley's replacement. Weaver is 2-1 with a 3.47 ERA in five starts for the Dodgers this year, the most recent July 11 in a 6-3 loss at Milwaukee, when he allowed four runs (two earned) in 3 1/3 innings. Weaver last pitched three hitless innings of relief on Sunday. He's 3-5 with a 5.00 ERA in 14 career starts against the Giants and 3-3 at AT&T Park.
summary: 2009-08-12 - Los Angeles Dodgers (2) @ San Francisco Giants (4) (Final)

home_pitcher_note:
Once the National League Cy Young front-runner, Haren has been far from an ace over his last four starts, surrendering 16 runs in 23 innings. His latest effort was a loss in which he threw six innings and gave up five runs at Washington.
"It's no secret, I'm scuffling right now," Haren said. "I really haven't had a great rhythm the last few times out. I'm trying to find it right now. I just have to try to dig myself out of a hole, the best I can."
away_pitcher_note: Kershaw certainly pitched well enough to win Saturday night against the Braves. He struck out 10, walked one and gave up just two hits in one of his strongest outings of the season. After being unable to last at least six innings on Aug. 3 for the first time since July 1, Kershaw didn't hesitate to go after the Atlanta hitters. He struck out two batters in each of the first three innings, as his fastball and curveball appeared especially lively. Kershaw is 0-0 with a 2.70 ERA in two career starts against the D-backs.

home_pitcher_note: Davis has put together four straight good starts. The D-backs have won all four of those games and Davis is 3-0 with a 2.08 ERA in that span. Last time out against the Mets he allowed a pair of runs on four hits over seven innings in a 7-4 Arizona win. According to an ESPN.com report, Davis was recently placed on waivers by the D-backs. The left-hander, though, does not seem to be bothered by the news and said if he got traded to a contender it would be a "win-win" situation. Davis is a free agent at the end of the season.
away_pitcher_note: Kuroda responded to the tension of the Dodgers-Giants rivalry as if he was pitching in October. Kuroda allowed one run on six hits over 6 1/3 innings and stopped a three-game losing streak. He was given an extra day of rest for his shoulder and the result wasn't bad. Kuroda has four consecutive quality starts and the Dodgers are 6-1 in his last seven starts. Kuroda is 1-3 in five starts against the D-backs.

home_pitcher_note: Petit could not follow his two exceptional starts with a third, as the red-hot Nationals pounced on him for nine hits and four runs -- three earned -- in four innings. Petit was lifted from the game for a pinch-hitter in the top of the fifth, ending his afternoon at 83 pitches. "I struggled with command," Petit said. "I was leaving the ball up at the plate and they hit it. My command on both sides was not working good.
away_pitcher_note: Randy Wolf allowed a third-inning run after a leadoff walk, but otherwise shut down the Giants for eight strong innings and his eighth quality start in his last nine outings. The Dodgers have scored 32 runs in Wolf's last three wins and he now leads the staff in innings pitched. Wolf is 7-3 lifetime against the Diamondbacks, 1-0 this year.

home_pitcher_note: Haeger will be making his Dodgers debut, and he gets to do it against Albert Pujols, but the right-handed knuckleballer has 10 previous Major League appearances over the past three seasons with the White Sox and Padres for a career mark of 1-2 with a 6.35 ERA. He has a more varied repertoire than most knuckleball pitchers, with a fastball and breaking ball that he's willing to throw.
away_pitcher_note: As Carpenter builds his counting stats, he gets closer and closer to a serious National League Cy Young candidacy. He's hurt by the amount of time he missed due to injury earlier this year, but that's about the only thing going against the right-hander. He keeps pitching deep into games and pitching well. And in his last start, Carpenter's velocity spiked into the mid-90s, adding still another wrinkle to an already impressive arsenal.
summary: 2009-08-17 - St. Louis Cardinals (3) @ Los Angeles Dodgers (2) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Billingsley will be pitching for the first time in 11 days. The right-hander suffered a slight hamstring strain coming out of the batters's box on Aug. 7 and was skipped Wednesday. He received a platelet patch injection and reported significant improvement. Billingsley would be facing the Cardinals, a team he shut out on one hit for the first five innings on July 28 in St. Louis before the roofed caved in on him with a six-run sixth inning.
away_pitcher_note: Boggs is start-to-start at this point, though it's worth noting that the Cardinals aren't thrilled with any of their other options. And Boggs, after a rough beginning in his most recent outing, got things together and lasted six decent innings. That's all he really needs to do as the No. 5 man -- get through six innings or so and keep the game close. With four other starters cranking out good games, Boggs doesn't need to be a world-beater.
summary: 2009-08-18 - St. Louis Cardinals (3) @ Los Angeles Dodgers (7) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: In his last start, Kershaw dug the Dodgers a four-run hole during the second inning, and there was no catching up against D-backs ace Dan Haren. It was more runs than Kershaw had allowed in any start since May 12. He lasted only 4 1/3 innings before using up his pitch allotment while striking out nine batters. Next, Kershaw will be facing the Cardinals, whom he held scoreless for eight innings on four hits in St. Louis last month.
away_pitcher_note: If Chris Carpenter isn't the best National League Cy Young Award candidate in the NL Central, then Wainwright is. He ranks among the leaders in several categories, and he has gone at least six innings in 23 straight starts. Wainwright is durable, efficient, effective and he has fully overcome the command problems that plagued him somewhat earlier this year. He's an elite starter having a superb year.
summary: 2009-08-19 - St. Louis Cardinals (3) @ Los Angeles Dodgers (2) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Dodgers manager Joe Torre announced Tuesday that Jeff Weaver will start on Thursday against the Cubs in place of right-hander Hiroki Kuroda, who's recovering from a mild concussion sustained last Saturday. Weaver has started six games for the Dodgers this season, going 2-1 with a 3.08 ERA. His most recent start came in San Francisco on Aug. 12, when he threw three scoreless innings in what was a bullpen day for the Dodgers. Torre said one of the reasons he decided to go with Weaver was because of how the right-hander matched up with the Cubs' lineup.
away_pitcher_note: Gorzelanny has made three starts since the Pirates dealt him to the Cubs prior to the non-waiver Trade Deadline; two of them have been good. He held the Reds to one run in 7 1/3 innings in his first start, but in his second start -- against the Rockies -- Gorzelanny was hit in the foot by a line drive and left after surrendering six runs in 1 1/3  innings. However, Gorzelanny bounced back on Saturday, pitching against his old team and making his first start at Wrigley Field as a member of the Cubs. Although he lasted only five innings, Gorzelanny held the Pirates to one run on three hits and struck out eight, one short of his career high. Gorzelanny even struck out the side in the third, dominating the opposing hitters with a high fastball that got up to 93 mph.

home_pitcher_note: Wolf restored order in the wake of Hiroki Kuroda's frightening incident and a bitter extra-inning loss. He took a one-hit shutout into the eighth inning for his ninth quality start in the last 10 outings. He struck out a season-high 10 without a walk, effectively spotting both his fastball and slow curve, and he added his fifth career home run. He's 4-7 lifetime against the Cubs.
away_pitcher_note: Wells had his worst start of the season on Aug. 9 against the Rockies but bounced back in his last start, against the Pirates on Friday. He benefited from 17 runs of support, throwing six innings and giving up two runs on seven hits. The rookie has won nine of his past 11 starts behind a two-seam fastball that produces many ground balls and makes up for a lack of strikeouts. Wells has held the opposition to three earned runs or fewer in 14 of his 18 starts.

home_pitcher_note: Haeger pitched seven solid innings Monday night against the Cardinals and could get the starting nod against the Cubs. Dodgers manager Joe Torre said after Monday's game that Haeger definitely earned another start but didn't say with any certainty when or if that would be. Much of the decision hinges on who pitches in place of Hiroki Kuroda on Thursday. Kuroda is recovering from a mild concussion, which he sustained Saturday at Arizona.
away_pitcher_note: Lilly deserved better in his first start back from being on the DL. The lefty threw six scoreless innings against the Padres, giving up four hits and walking one. In his last 64 2/3 innings, he's walked 10 and struck out 59. He hasn't gotten much support, going 2-6 when he gets three runs or less. He beat the Dodgers on May 29 at Wrigley, holding them to one run on four hits over seven innings. Good news is he had no problems with his shoulder or knee and said he felt healthy.

home_pitcher_note: Billingsley looked strong Tuesday night against the Cardinals in his first start back from a strained left hamstring.  Billingsley cruised through the first five innings, allowing just one hit and walking none. And then in the sixth he prevented a big inning by forcing Albert Pujols to ground into an inning-ending double play. Billingsley only threw 77 pitches, which fit in with the Dodgers plan to limit him to between 80-90 pitches in his first outing since Aug. 7 against the Braves. In all, Billingsley gave up two runs on three hits in six innings on the mound. Billingsley is 1-2 with a 3.27 ERA in five career appearances (three of them starts) against the Cubs.
away_pitcher_note: Dempster struck out a season-high 10 batters in his last outing, against the Padres, for his 11th career double-digit strikeout game. He also gave up four runs on eight hits in seven innings, and the Cubs couldn't match that. Dempster wasn't happy with himself -- especially after serving up a solo homer to Adrian Gonzalez leading off the fifth. He's 1-2 with a 4.15 ERA in four starts this month. Opponents were batting .258 off Dempster in the first half. In the second half, they're hitting .296.

home_pitcher_note: Hammel has struggled at Coors Field, where he's 2-3 with a 7.02 ERA, but hopes his continued fastball command will help him keep the Dodgers at bay in a critical series that could decide the outcome of the NL West. The right-hander has been trying to integrate a sinker into his repertoire to serve as a complementary pitch with mixed results -- when it's on, he gets grounders; when the sinker doesn't sink, he gets hit. So he's redoubled his efforts to command his four-seam fastball and throw it for first-pitch strikes. That strategy was successful Thursday in Washington, where Hammel allowed a run on three hits over seven innings, never allowing the Nationals to generate any sustained offense.
away_pitcher_note: Kershaw had another wild inning last time out against the Cardinals and this time couldn't get out of it, running up his pitch count to 97 and bringing manager Joe Torre's hook after only 3 2/3 innings. He had four walks and a wild pitch. Despite an overpowering fastball, Kershaw is most effective when he pitches to contact and conserves his energy. Kershaw is winless in his past six starts and he's 2-2 with an 8.64 ERA at Coors Field.

home_pitcher_note: With Aaron Cook on the disabled list with a sore right shoulder, Josh Fogg gets his first start of the season in a critical game against the Dodgers. Fogg has been the long man out of the bullpen for the Rockies since coming up in late May, and he has allowed more than one earned run only one time in 20 appearances this season. Fogg is holding opposing hitters to a .186 average, the best mark among Rockies relievers. Nicknamed "The Dragon Slayer" for his big wins in the 2007 pennant race, Fogg was a non-roster invitee to camp this year and was 3-1 with a 5.80 ERA in eight starts for the Triple-A Sky Sox before being called up in May.
away_pitcher_note: Against the Cubs, Wolf pretty much repeated his performance in Arizona from five days earlier. He again fired a one-hitter through seven innings and was equally effective with the bat, doubling home both runs the Dodgers scored while he was in the game. Wolf's strikeouts were down from 10 to five, but he was more efficient, posting five 1-2-3 innings. The left-hander was lifted for a pinch-hitter after 88 pitches. He's 3-0 with a 1.99 ERA in his past three starts.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start, De La Rosa lacked his put-away slider. He gave up a pair of two-run homers in six innings. He gave up six runs. But he earned a win in a 14-11 game with the Giants on Saturday night. That was a huge step for De La Rosa, who has pitched well more often than not since the latter part of last season but still must overcome a reputation for falling apart when things go wrong early. That certainly wasn't the case Saturday.
away_pitcher_note: He's not even on the 40-man roster yet, but Padilla is expected to be promoted to make his Dodgers debut in the series finale in Denver, replacing injured right-hander Hiroki Kuroda. Padilla hasn't pitched in a Major League game since Aug. 5, as a member of the Rangers. He's allowed six runs in nine innings at Coors Field over his career.

home_pitcher_note: Bailey survived a shaky first two innings during his most recent outing, on Sunday in Pittsburgh, posting a strong line of one run in seven innings to win for the first time in five starts. The former first-round pick allowed nine runs (six earned) on eight hits and two walks in 2 2/3 innings in one prior career start against the Dodgers, on July 21.
away_pitcher_note: Billingsley continues to pitch with his tender left hamstring wrapped and continues to say it doesn't bother him. He's coming off a quality start against the Cubs that he lost, having pitched out of four jams and struck out five in six innings. He also allowed his first home run in six starts. Billingsley is 3-1 with a 1.40 ERA lifetime against the Reds and 1-1 with a 1.59 ERA at Great American Ball Park.

home_pitcher_note: At Triple-A Louisville, Maloney is 9-9 with a 3.08 ERA. His last start was on Sunday at Toledo and he allowed four runs and six hits over six innings with two walks and seven strikeouts. Maloney made three starts for the Reds and was optioned back to Louisville on June 20.
away_pitcher_note: Rookie knuckleballer Charlie Haeger, making only his third Major League start, pitched a gem against the Cubs and will remain in the rotation for this game, as manager Joe Torre said he'd prefer to keep Jeff Weaver in the bullpen. Haeger took a three-hit shutout into the eighth inning and the bullpen held on to preserve his first victory since 2006. Haeger struck out seven.

home_pitcher_note: Arroyo has a 1.89 ERA in five August starts and a streak of six-straight quality starts but is getting the short end of the deal on victories. He has just one win over his last seven starts. During an 8-6 Reds win in 13 innings, the bullpen blew a 6-1 lead in the ninth inning. Arroyo seemed headed for a win after he pitched seven innings and allowed one earned run and six hits with one walk and four strikeouts. He has allowed two runs over his last 24 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Clayton Kershaw bounced back after a pair of disappointing starts to limit the Rockies to two runs on four hits before reaching his pitch limit after 6 1/3 innings. Kershaw struck out six and walked one, stung by a two-run homer by Brad Hawpe. He's winless in his last seven starts. Kershaw has never faced the Reds. The Dodgers have scored only eight runs in his last 40 innings on the mound.

home_pitcher_note: Randy Wolf has stepped up while the Dodgers have been sagging. He ran his win streak to four with a clutch effort at Coors Field, limiting the torrid Rockies to one run on five hits over 7 1/3 innings. Most importantly, Wolf is consistently eating innings. He's pitched at least six innings in each of his last 12 starts and has 10 quality starts in his last 11 outings. The Dodgers are 18-10 in his starts. He's 2-0 against Arizona this year, 8-3 lifetime.
away_pitcher_note: Davis seemed on his way to certain victory in his last start as he handled the Giants easily through the first seven innings at AT&T Park. To that point, the lone San Francisco run had come on a Juan Uribe homer. Davis got the first two outs of the eighth before allowing a walk and single. In came closer Chad Qualls and he allowed a three-run homer to pinch-hitter Bengie Molina. Davis wound up without a decision and the D-backs took a 4-3 defeat.

home_pitcher_note: Vicente Padilla did a respectable job in his Dodgers debut at Coors Field, limiting the hot-hitting Rockies to two runs on six hits in five innings with one walk and four strikeouts. Padilla was clocked as fast as 96 mph and he was in trouble on in the two-run third inning. He was lifted for a pinch-hitter with the score tied in the top of the sixth inning.
away_pitcher_note: Petit tweaked his mechanics a bit after allowing seven runs on nine hits in four innings to the Dodgers on Aug. 16. He now turns a little more away from the hitter during his windup. It adds a little more deception, which is important because Petit does not have overpowering stuff. Since making the adjustment, Petit has allowed just one run over 12 innings. His last time out, against the Giants, Petit tossed six shutout innings, allowing just four hits. In his start prior to that, Petit allowed one run over six innings in Houston.

home_pitcher_note: Billingsley lasted less than six innings for the first time since Aug. 2 against the Braves. He gave up four runs on seven hits in five-plus innings of a 4-2 loss. After a perfect 1 2/3 innings, Billingsley gave up a run in the second and two runs in the third. He later allowed another in the sixth before exiting. He will look to get back on track against the D-backs, who he is 1-0 against this season.
away_pitcher_note: Scherzer, who like other members of the Arizona starting rotation has suffered his share of tough losses, gained a measure of redemption in his last outing, when he earned a win for the first time while allowing more than two runs. But his troubles in that 14-7 victory over Houston had much to do with a huge early lead softening his customary intensity. Manager A.J. Hinch is going to shorten the leash on the 25-year-old, who has already worked more innings (139 1/3) than all of last season between Tucson and Arizona (109).

home_pitcher_note: Jon Garland will be pitching as scheduled at Dodger Stadium, but instead of facing the Dodgers for the Diamondbacks, he'll be facing the Diamondbacks for the Dodgers after Monday night's trade. He is coming off seven shutout innings against the Astros. Garland is an innings-eater who has been especially effective recently because of his changeup.
away_pitcher_note: Buckner will be making his first start since being recalled Monday from Triple-A Reno. The right-hander will face former teammate Jon Garland, who was dealt to Los Angeles on Monday night. Buckner has appeared in 10 games and made seven starts for the D-backs this season. This is his third stint in the big leagues.

home_pitcher_note: Kershaw made only one mistake in his last start, against the Reds, allowing a two-run homer to Darnell McDonald that gave Cincinnati an early 2-0 lead. Yet Kershaw settled down and struck out 11 Reds batters in all, giving up only four hits in a no-decision. Kershaw has allowed three runs or fewer in 23 of 27 starts this season. The left-hander will look to earn his first win since July 18 against the Padres.
away_pitcher_note: LeBlanc took a no-decision in his third start of the season, allowing four runs on four hits over six innings while striking out two and walking two. The left-hander found trouble in the second and sixth innings but limited the Marlins to two runs in each frame. LeBlanc's next start comes against the Dodgers who are batting .364 (12-for-33)against the 25-year-old.
summary: 2009-09-04 - San Diego Padres (2) @ Los Angeles Dodgers (0) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Randy Wolf came away with his 14th no-decision as the bullpen allowed a Major League-leading eighth win get away. He allowed two runs on six hits over six innings while striking out seven. His pitch count ran up to 102 as the Diamondbacks employed a more patient approach and worked him deeper into counts. This will be his second attempt at career win No. 100.
away_pitcher_note: Latos was perfect for the first three innings of his last start but had a difficult fourth in which he was able to retire only one batter before being relieved by Edward Mujica. The 21-year-old right-hander had the Marlins off balance their first time through the order, but he couldn't silence them the second time around. Latos finished the outing allowing five runs (four earned) on four hits over 3 1/3 innings while striking out two and walking two.
summary: 2009-09-05 - San Diego Padres (4) @ Los Angeles Dodgers (7) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Dodgers manager Joe Torre said he had Kuroda penciled in to start Sunday, and that was before Kuroda allowed one unearned run in five innings of a Minor League rehab start. Kuroda said he's fully recovered from the concussion caused by a line drive off his head. Kuroda also would be dealing with the shadows from a 5:10 p.m. PT start.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start, a 3-1 Padres win over the Nationals on Monday, Stauffer worked past five innings for the first time in a month, allowing one run in 6 2/3 innings. Stauffer showed good life on his fastball, striking out five. And even though he walked three, Stauffer was much more efficient, getting seven outs on fly balls and seven on ground balls. "It's about time," Stauffer joked, alluding to the stretch of five previous starts in which he went exactly five innings. "I still had a couple of walks, but my aggressiveness was better. I felt like I had better stuff."
summary: 2009-09-06 - San Diego Padres (4) @ Los Angeles Dodgers (3) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Scherzer helped the D-backs secure a series split in Los Angeles last week, earning a 4-1 win on Wednesday, when he allowed one run on seven hits and a walk while striking out four over 7 2/3 innings. The win put him on a bit of a roll, going 2-0 with a 3.95 ERA over his last two starts.  He has faced the Dodgers one other time, on May 5 in L.A., putting up a quality start but taking a loss. He pitched six innings and allowing three runs (two earned) on four hits and two walks while striking out four. Though he has won twice as many games at home, his ERA is 0.76 better on the road.
away_pitcher_note: Padilla is expected to return after an extra day off. He sustained a bruised calf when struck by a line drive in the first inning against Arizona last Tuesday, but he hung in there to allow one run in 5 1/3 innings for his second effective start since being picked up by the Dodgers. He escaped a first-inning jam after a mound meeting with pitching coach Rick Honeycutt resulted in an immediate five extra miles per hour on his fastball.

home_pitcher_note: Buckner rejoined the D-backs from Triple-A Reno last week and started against the Dodgers, giving up four runs on eight hits in six innings and taking the loss. After having success in Reno, Buckner knows that he needs to carry that over into the big leagues to help his chances of winning a spot in the rotation next year. Buckner has incorporated a cut fastball into his repertoire and has changed his approach on the mound as well. "I'm a different pitcher than I was last time I was here," said Buckner, who is in his third stint with the team this year.
away_pitcher_note: Billingsley took a perfect game into the fifth against Arizona on Wednesday, then things unraveled. He allowed a two-run homer to Brandon Allen and a pair of RBI infield singles in the four-run inning. His mechanics were much improved from previous shaky outings. He has one win in his last five starts and only three in his last 14. He's now 7-5 lifetime against Arizona.

home_pitcher_note: Haren faced the Rockies for the fourth time this season, and after yielding a run in each of the first two innings, he changed his game plan, getting away from his fastball and relying on his cutter and splitter before finally moving to his curve, which he said he threw more often than he ever has in Coors Field. He wasn't satisfied with his stuff, but it was good enough to get him through six innings with only the two runs on seven hits and a walk while striking out eight.
away_pitcher_note: Garland gets the chance to beat his former team a second time. Garland overcame early-innings jitters in his Dodgers debut to contain the D-backs on two runs for seven innings, retiring the final 14 batters he faced. He was clearly strong enough to keep going, but gave way to closers George Sherrill and Jonathan Broxton.

home_pitcher_note: After seven starts without a victory, Cain finally got elusive No. 13 against the Brewers, holding the high-octane Milwaukee offense to two runs on four hits in six innings. Manager Bruce Bochy credited Cain's increased focus in sticky situations as a mark of maturity this season -- such as a sixth inning in which he walked the first two batters but did not allow a run. He continues to be one of the league's most dominant right arms.
away_pitcher_note: In his first start back, Hiroki Kuroda showed no ill effects from the line drive he took off his head. On the other hand, he didn't pitch well enough to win, either. Kuroda was charged with four runs in five innings and walked three, which the Dodgers hope had more to do with rustiness than any reluctance to challenge hitters. Kuroda originally was going to get extra rest, but was moved up two days because of injuries to Clayton Kershaw and Randy Wolf. He had a bullpen session during Tuesday night's game.
summary: 2009-09-11 - Los Angeles Dodgers (10) @ San Francisco Giants (3) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: The surging lefty struck out nine in the first five innings and lowered his ERA to 2.03 over his past five starts with a snappy nine-strikeout effort in Milwaukee his last time out, though he was long gone by the time the low-scoring affair was decided in extra innings. Sanchez entered that outing leading the league since July 10 in batting average against and lowered it to .165 over that stretch with a convincing performance against the Brewers.
away_pitcher_note: Injuries to Clayton Kershaw and Randy Wolf moved Vicente Padilla into this slot on a normal five-day cycle. Padilla has been a most pleasant surprise considering his checkered reputation in Texas. He's delivered three effective starts, most recently beating the Diamondbacks while allowing two runs over six innings. He is 2-0 with a 2.76 ERA since joining the Dodgers.
summary: 2009-09-12 - Los Angeles Dodgers (9) @ San Francisco Giants (1) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: This matchup will be intriguing, to say the least. Penny excelled for the Dodgers in 2006-07, posting a 32-13 record, making the All-Star team both years and finishing third in the National League Cy Young Award balloting in 2007. But he endured shoulder problems in 2008, wasn't re-signed after a 6-9 finish and was openly criticized by Dodgers coach Larry Bowa, among others. So far, Penny has found new life with the Giants, allowing two runs and eight hits over 15 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Billingsley didn't have typical velocity with his fastball and he fell behind early to the D-backs. But relying on a sharp breaking ball, he kept the game close enough for the Dodgers to pull out a victory after he was removed. Still, he allowed four runs in six innings, hasn't won since August 18 or pitched longer than six innings since July 5.
summary: 2009-09-13 - Los Angeles Dodgers (2) @ San Francisco Giants (7) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Jon Garland starts for the Dodgers for the first time against a team other than his most recent employer. Garland, 1-0 in two starts against the D-backs since they traded him to the Dodgers at the Aug. 31 deadline, will try to stay unbeaten for his new club.
away_pitcher_note: Take away two misplaced pitches to Derrek Lee and McCutchen's outing really wasn't all that bad. Three of the four runs he allowed came on Lee's two first-pitch homers, one a misplaced fastball and the other a poorly located changeup. McCutchen, in just his second Major League start, finished seven innings in all, allowing nine hits and striking out five. He's a command pitcher who lives on his ability to establish his 90-93 mph fastball early and then use his changeup.

home_pitcher_note: Martin is turning out to be the second best pitcher in the Nationals' rotation. Last Friday, he pitched 5 1/3 innings and gave up two runs on seven hits against the Mets. Martin is second on the team in wins with five.
away_pitcher_note: Padilla suffered through his worst start with the Dodgers on Friday against the Giants. home_pitcher_note: Karstens gets the nod to make the start in place of Ross Ohlendorf, who has been shut down for the season. away_pitcher_note: Garland has been a standout addition to the Dodgers' rotation since he was acquired from the Diamondbacks at the end of August. home_pitcher_note: Maholm wasn't at his best in his most recent outing, allowing nine hits (five for extra bases) and three walks in six innings. To his credit, though, only two earned runs scored. home_pitcher_note: McCutchen hasn't been great in any of his four starts with the Pirates, though to his credit he hasn't been knocked out early either. away_pitcher_note: The Dodgers welcome the 21-year-old southpaw back into the rotation after losing him to a shoulder injury Sept. 6 when he collided with an outfield wall while shagging flies, two days after his most recent start. home_pitcher_note: Duke opened PNC Park in April and he'll close the Pirates' home schedule as well with this start. away_pitcher_note: Kuroda continued to look strong in his comeback from a concussion sustained when he was hit in the head by a line drive. home_pitcher_note: Ramos will be making the first big league start of his career. away_pitcher_note: Billingsley rebounded from an abysmal September in which he'd gone 0-2 with a 6.11 ERA by taking a no-hitter into the sixth inning and certainly turning in the performance the club had hoped he would have to put in his claim on one of the postseason starting slots. away_pitcher_note: Garland pitched well enough for a shutout, instead getting charged with three unearned runs and an undeserved loss in Pittsburgh. away_pitcher_note: Jimenez pitched seven strong innings against Adam Wainwright and the Cardinals Saturday night, taking a tie game into his final inning on the hill before yielding a leadoff solo homer that proved to be the Cardinals winning run in their division-clinching victory. He allowed four runs on six hits and three walks, and once he found his fastball command he retired 10 of 11 batters faced after the first inning, and 16-of-20 into the seventh. His seven strikeouts came at big moments. He struck out the side in the fourth, which allowed the Rockies to tie the game in the bottom of the inning.

home_pitcher_note: Kershaw made a decent return to the rotation Sunday after missing three weeks with a separation of his non-throwing shoulder, but he'll need to get deeper than four innings to convince the staff he's ready for prime-time playoff responsibilities. He seems healthy enough, but he struggled with command of his slider against the Pirates. Pitch count is always the key for him.
away_pitcher_note: The Rockies needed De La Rosa on Sunday. Although he wasn't sharp and faced nearly constant traffic in five innings, he finished with eight strikeouts and made enough pitches at key times -- pitching out of bases-loaded situations twice -- to win. He needs one more victory to match the club record of 17, held by Jeff Francis (2007), Pedro Astacio (1999) and Kevin Ritz (1995).

home_pitcher_note: Dodgers manager Joe Torre announced on Friday that Padilla would start the season finale for the Dodgers. Padilla's start against the Rockies probably will be an audition for what kind of role he'll have on the Dodgers postseason staff. If Padilla struggles, he could be relegated to the bullpen for the NLDS, while a good outing could make him a viable option at starter. Padilla's two most recent starts for the Dodgers didn't go well. He gave up four runs on eight hits in five innings on Sept. 18 against the Giants, and he gave up four more runs in five innings on Sept. 24 against the Nationals. On Wednesday in San Diego, Padilla threw two scoreless innings of relief.
away_pitcher_note: Marquis wasn't quite dominant Tuesday night at Coors Field, but he battled his way out of jams and held on for six quality innings of two run ball, leaving with a lead after scattering six hits and four walks. Fourteen of his 18 outs came on groundballs, a great indication that his sinker was in fine form.  He used it with more and more confidence in the game, going to it early in counts and challenging hitters with it.  He felt as comfortable as he's felt in some time, bringing some fine-tuned mechanics and a rejuvenated mental approach to the game. He faced big bases-loaded jams, walking in one run but getting groundout double plays in each case to escape or minimize the damage and set up the Rockies for a critical win.

home_pitcher_note: Not only will Wolf make his first career playoff appearance Wednesday against the Cardinals, but he'll do so as the Dodgers' No. 1 starter. Wolf went 11-7 for the Dodgers this season, but the low win number hides the fact that he was the Dodgers' most consistent pitcher. His 214 1/3 innings led the team, and Wolf could always be counted on to come through in a big game. Before his last start, Wolf had a streak of 17 consecutive starts in which he lasted at least six innings, and Los Angeles is 22-12 in his starts this season. In his only start against the Cardinals this year, on July 27, Wolf gave up two runs on seven hits in six innings.
away_pitcher_note: If Carpenter hadn't missed several weeks early in the season due to a strained oblique muscle, he'd probably be the favorite for the National League Cy Young Award. The only thing separating him, in truth, is a relative lack of innings, compared to teammate Adam Wainwright and the Giants' Tim Lincecum. Even so, it was a brilliant year. Carpenter paced the league in ERA and was a tremendous story as he came back from nearly two full missed seasons due to elbow injuries and a nerve condition behind his right shoulder. There's nobody the Cardinals would rather have on the mound in a big game.
summary: 2009-10-07 - St. Louis Cardinals (3) @ Los Angeles Dodgers (5) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: The 21-year-old lefty turned in one of his more impressive outings of the season during Saturday's NL West clincher against the Rockies. Kershaw struck out the first five batters he faced and K'd seven the first time through the Rockies' batting order. In all, he finished with 10 strikeouts and pitched six scoreless innings in his final start of the year. Kershaw started two games against the Cardinals this season -- one was great and one was bad. On July 29, Kershaw threw eight scoreless innings and struck out seven but earned a no-decision. On Aug. 19 he gave up two runs and walked four in only 3 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Wainwright is a leading contender, maybe the leading contender, for the National League Cy Young Award despite a frustrating outcome to his final start. He pitched very well in that game, though, and that was the most important thing. Although a bullpen and defense meltdowns cost Wainwright his 20th win, he showed no ill effects of having to work very hard in his previous start, when he threw 130 pitches to help the Cardinals clinch the Central division. He's a proven October performer, having closed out all three series in the Cards' run to the 2006 World Series championship.
summary: 2009-10-08 - St. Louis Cardinals (2) @ Los Angeles Dodgers (3) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Pineiro is not coming into the playoffs on a roll. He hasn't been bad, at least not usually, but he hasn't been nearly as good over the past five weeks as he was earlier in the year. Pineiro allowed four or more runs in five of his final seven starts, as his walk rate regressed from microscopic to merely impressive. One benefit, however, of the Cardinals opening on the road is that Pineiro will pitch at home. He's been quite a bit more impressive at Busch Stadium than on the road.
away_pitcher_note: Sometimes you get more than you pay for. Vicente Padilla came to the Dodgers almost for free and maybe all he needed was a change of scenery. Released by the Rangers with a reputation for being a bad apple, he's been a model citizen in the Dodgers clubhouse. More importantly, he went 4-0 with a 3.20 ERA in seven starts and finished up with 10 strikeouts in five innings against the Rockies. He throws hard, has a variety of pitches and attacks hitters with confidence. And despite a reputation as a head hunter, he didn't hit any opposing batters in 39 1/3 innings after hitting eight in 108 innings with Texas and 99 in his career.
summary: 2009-10-10 - Los Angeles Dodgers (5) @ St. Louis Cardinals (1) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: In Game 1 of the NLCS against the Philadelphia Phillies, the Dodgers will hand the ball to the 21-year-old lefty Kershaw. The decision comes after Kershaw threw 6 2/3 innings of two-run ball against the Cardinals in the NLDS in the Dodgers' comeback win. Kershaw didn't show any nerves in his first-career postseason start as he was able to get out of jams and keep the Cardinals from capitalizing on run-scoring opportunities. Kershaw was the Dodgers' most electrifying pitcher this season, using his four-seam fastball and his curveball to pile up strikeouts and limit hitters to a .200 average. He went 8-8 with a 2.79 ERA in 2009 but was 0-2 with a 5.23 ERA in two starts against the Phillies this year.
away_pitcher_note: With an impressive resume against the Dodgers and the benefit of six days' rest, Hamels is set up well to open the National League Championship Series against the Dodgers. During a 2009 regular season that was at times a rough followup to his 2008 heroics, Hamels pitched a shutout at Dodger Stadium on June 4, one of his two on the season. That was after going 2-0 with a 1.93 ERA in two starts against them in last year's NLCS to earn series Most Valuable Player honors, and he is 2-0 with a 1.50 ERA in four career regular-season starts against them. However, Hamels finished the 2009 season 10-11 with a 4.32 ERA, and was 0-2 with a 7.02 ERA in his last three regular-season starts. His NL Division Series Game 2 start against the Rockies didn't alter that trend much, as he allowed four earned runs in five innings of work in a 5-4 loss. He left that game following his exit from the mound to attend the birth of his first child, and remained in Philadelphia to work out as the Phillies clinched their second consecutive NLCS berth in Denver.

home_pitcher_note: Vicente Padilla, a former Phillie, has resurrected his career in a big way after being released by the Rangers. He's unbeaten as a Dodger with four regular-season wins and the first-round clincher in St. Louis, when he threw seven scoreless innings and looked perfectly capable of finishing it up. Padilla had a dicey reputation with the Rangers as headhunter, but has been a model citizen with the Dodgers, impressive enough against the Cardinals to get moved up in the rotation. His teammates watch a sinking fastball that stays around 94 mph and can't believe he was released. He's faced the Phillies only once, allowing seven runs in a six-inning start in 2008. He's had plenty of experience at Citizens Bank Park, going 10-11 with a 4.98 ERA in his last two years with the Phillies after going 15-15 with a 2.97 ERA at Veterans Stadium.
away_pitcher_note: Martinez will be making his first postseason appearance since beating the Cardinals in Game 3 of the 2004 World Series. The 37-year-old right-hander, who joined the Phillies in August, has pitched just seven innings since Sept. 13.  But after watching the veteran hurler complete a simulated game on Tuesday, Phillies manager Charlie Manuel once again reiterated that he's comfortable putting him out there as a starter. Martinez has gone 3-5 with a 4.02 ERA in nine career starts against the Dodgers. This is his first appearance against them since 2006. In 13 career playoff appearances, the three-time Cy Young Award winner has gone 6-2 with a 3.40 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Lee has shown he is more than ready to pitch in the postseason. He looked dominant in Games 1 and 4 of the National League Division Series against the Colorado Rockies. He allowed one run and six hits in a complete-game 5-1 victory over the Rockies in Game 1 at Citizens Bank Park. He allowed just one earned run in 7 1/3 innings in a dramatic 5-4 comeback victory in Game 4 at Coors Field. Lee scuffled a bit late in the regular season, but it appears the postseason has energized him. He seems to want to make the most of the moment. The Cleveland Indians left him off their 2007 postseason roster, which is something he hasn't forgotten. He won the American League Cy Young last season before the Indians traded him and outfielder Ben Francisco to the Phillies on July 29 for prospects Jason Knapp, Carlos Carrasco, Lou Marson and Jason Donald.
away_pitcher_note: Hiroki Kuroda passed a final exam Tuesday, proving to Joe Torre and Rick Honeycutt that the herniated disk in his neck was healed enough to take the ball after being left off the roster for the first round against the Cardinals. While it will be almost three weeks since Kuroda pitched in a Major League game, management believes he's enough of a gamer to give him the first start in a hostile Citizens Bank Park. That conclusion was reached based in large part on how clutch Kuroda was in last year's playoffs, having been the only Dodgers starter to beat the Phillies. In his only start against them this year, he threw six scoreless innings in a no-decision. In three regular-season starts against them he's allowed only two earned runs in 19 innings. It's been a nightmarish season for the Opening Day starter, from a strained oblique muscle to the line drive he took off his head to the herniated disk, but all will be forgotten if he can duplicate last October's success.

home_pitcher_note: Phillies manager Charlie Manuel picked right-hander Joe Blanton over left-hander J.A. Happ for this start. Pitching out of the bullpen, Blanton made two appearances in the NL Division Series against the Rockies, allowing two earned run in 4 2/3 innings. Blanton was 12-8 with a 4.05 ERA in 31 starts during the regular season.
away_pitcher_note: Randy Wolf, another former Phillie, took a demotion to make this start after getting the Game 1 nod in the first round against the Cardinals. On a generally short leash during the regular season, even though he led the club in innings pitched, Wolf got yanked from his first career postseason appearance after allowing only two runs in a shaky 3 2/3 innings. That said, he went 6-1 down the stretch and held opposing left-handed hitters to an average of .159, which should serve him well against a Phillies lineup loaded with lefties. On the other hand, Wolf was 1-1 with a 5.11 ERA against Philadelphia this year and is 9-7 with a 4.30 ERA at Citizens Bank Park, although most of those starts had the Phillies lineup supporting him, not facing him. His 2.78 road ERA was fifth in the league.

home_pitcher_note: Last year's NLCS and World Series MVP has not been sharp this postseason, allowing eight earned runs in 10 1/3 innings (6.97 ERA). Hamels pitched well in Los Angeles in Game 1 before encountering trouble in the fifth. He would earn the win, but he allowed four runs in 5 1/3 innings. With a victory Wednesday, Hamels will seal the Phillies' second consecutive NL pennant.
away_pitcher_note: Manager Joe Torre tends to go with the hot hand, so he selected Vicente Padilla to start what has turned into a do-or-die assignment with the Dodgers facing elimination. Padilla, released by Texas in August, is as close as the Dodgers have to an ace in October. When he starts, the club expects to be in the game. He is coming off a rousing no-decision duel with Pedro Martinez against his former club, allowing only one run over 7 1/3 innings. And that followed seven scoreless innings in the NL Division Series clincher in St. Louis. In fact, Padilla hasn't lost since signing with the Dodgers. He's handled pressure starts, pitched well on the road and impressed the staff with a devastating hard sinker that he throws consistently for strikes.

home_pitcher_note: For the second time in his career, Duke has earned the nod as an Opening Day starter. He first did so in 2007 and responded with seven strong innings, in which he allowed two runs in a no-decision.
