The Pirates have said that they may be a little more cautious with Duke's early workload than they were last year, so that's something to keep an eye on as the season gets underway. The lefty is 2-3 with a 5.68 ERA in eight career starts against the Dodgers.
away_pitcher_note: The surprise choice for Opening Day starter is Vicente Padilla, chosen as much for the way he stepped up late in the season, when the Dodgers took him off the scrap heap after his release by Texas, as anything. When he's right, he can be tough to hit, as he showed against the Cardinals and Phillies in the playoffs. He's admitted to some forearm tightness this spring, and he takes heat treatment before he pitches, not unusual for pitchers. He's 18-5 on the road over the past two seasons. This is his first Opening Day start, although he has won at least 14 games in four different seasons.

home_pitcher_note: At this time last season, Ohlendorf was in the process of establishing himself as a capable Major League starter. With that accomplished through his '09 results, Ohlendorf now takes his spot near the top of the Pirates' rotation. No one finished last season stronger than Ohlendorf, who posted a 2.43 ERA during his 11 post-All-Star Game starts. That ERA was almost two runs lower than it was in the first half of the season. Ohlendorf has really focused on developing his changeup this spring, but overall his Grapefruit League results weren't that good. Command was his biggest problem. This will be Ohlendorf's second career start against the Dodgers. His first lasted only three innings.
away_pitcher_note: It's still a bit puzzling why Joe Torre didn't select Clayton Kershaw as his Opening Day starter, as most opponents would say he's the one pitcher on the Dodgers team they don't want to face. After all, Torre had him start Game 1 of the NL Championship Series last year. You can't tell by his statistics that he just turned 22. Opposing batters hit .200 against Kershaw in 2009, lowest in the Major Leagues. His 2.79 ERA was fifth lowest in the league. Kershaw has dominating stuff, but he prefers to adhere to a regular routine and the juggling of starters coming into the season didn't allow that coming into this race.

home_pitcher_note: Maholm slots into the third spot in the Pirates' rotation because of the club's need to split up its two left-handed starters. The lefty may not have had the most dominant numbers of any Pittsburgh pitcher last season, but he has largely been a model of consistency over the past two years. He is at 100 percent health again, with no reason to be concerned that his left knee will bother him as it did at times in 2009. Maholm is still looking for his first career win over the Dodgers, however. Heading into the start, he is 0-3 with a 5.59 ERA in six starts against the Los Angeles club.
away_pitcher_note: Chad Billingsley once was viewed as a potential ace of the staff. Eight months ago he was an All-Star. Now the Dodgers want to take the pressure off and get him back on track after he struggled down the stretch and was dropped from the rotation in the postseason. So far, so good in Spring Training, as he looks like he might have ironed out the mechanical flaw he believes set in motion his late-season fade. Scouts say Billingsley tends to overuse his cutter and it's taken a foot off his fastball. The Dodgers believe he's throwing as well as he did over the first half last season.

home_pitcher_note: The 23-year-old is hoping to regain the form of his 2008 rookie season when he was 6-4 with a 2.88 ERA. The 6-foot-8 Volstad had a rocky sophomore season. When he was laboring late in the year, he was optioned to Triple-A New Orleans, where he made one start. With the Marlins, he had 29 starts, and he was victimized by the long ball. Twenty nine times he surrendered home runs. Volstad actually was better on the road (5-4, 4.31 ERA) than at home (4-9, 6.06) in 2009.
away_pitcher_note: Hiroki Kuroda is coming off a Spring Training ERA of 1.96, capped by four scoreless innings on one hit with five strikeouts and no walks against the Angels in his final prep Saturday. This is his free-agent year and he says he's healthier than he's been at the start of the last two seasons. Most importantly, he said he's now healed from the herniated disk that made him useless at the end of last year. After two seasons, he's been something of a disappointment, mostly because he hasn't been able to stay healthy. And he was signed mostly because of a reputation as an inning-eating warrior. He's pitched well against the Marlins with a 3.66 career ERA and no decisions.

home_pitcher_note: After weighing their options, the Marlins decided to stick with Johnson pitching on his normal fifth day. Because of an off day on Tuesday, the team was holding back before announcing if Johnson would start on Saturday or Sunday. Now, the Florida ace will be making two of his team's first five starts. Johnson wasn't at his best on Opening Day, giving up four runs in five-plus innings. He walked four and hit a batter. After watching film of his performance against the Mets, Johnson made a minor adjustment to his delivery. He says he is going back to something he did a year ago, but hadn't done yet this season.
away_pitcher_note: Manager Joe Torre is rushing Padilla right back to the mound in a show of support after his awful Opening Day loss in Pittsburgh, where he allowed seven runs in 4 1/3 innings. Torre could have waited a day because of a day off, but instead he will keep Padilla on his five-day rotation, as well as give him a vote of confidence. Padilla's strength is keeping the ball down, which he didn't do against the Pirates. He worked on a possible mechanical flaw in a bullpen session on Wednesday. He did not face the Marlins last year.

home_pitcher_note: Initially, Sanchez was slated to pitch third in the rotation. But he was flipped to the No. 5 spot, as the Marlins opted to move up lefty Nate Robertson to No. 3. For the first time in five years, Sanchez started and finished Spring Training healthy. The 26-year-old Venezuela native has dealt with shoulder troubles in the past. In 2007, he had surgery to repair a torn labrum. Sanchez spent a couple of stints on the disabled list last year with shoulder problems. He lost about 30 pounds from a year ago, and physically he's been fine. Now it is a matter of him regaining the pinpoint command that made him a 10-game winner as a rookie in 2006. Since throwing 114 1/3 innings as a rookie, Sanchez has thrown 167 2/3 innings total in the big leagues.
away_pitcher_note: Haeger gets his first start of the year against the Marlins and he's quite a story, having retired in 2003 to take up golf, only to return to baseball, pick up the knuckleball and make it to the Major Leagues. Now he's in a rotation to start a season. While Haeger has been tutored by legnedary knuckleballer Charlie Hough, he also has enough of a fastball and breaking ball to keep hitters honest. Haeger showed last year that he's got the confidence and poise to handle the unpredictable nature of his money pitch. He had a good spring and, because the knuckleball is easy on the arm, he's got the potential to be the innings eater the Dodgers have been looking for.

home_pitcher_note: If Kershaw was amped up pitching in Pittsburgh, how will he handle the sold-out crowd at Dodger Stadium for the home opener? The Dodgers are curious to see. Even though Kershaw has the experience of two postseasons, he's also still 22 years old and is learning how to harness the adrenaline and maintain his composure on the mound. The Dodgers need him to get deeper than the 4 2/3 innings he lasted in Pittsburgh, and he won't unless he cuts down on the six walks. That said, he is extremely comfortable pitching in Dodger Stadium, where his ERA last year was 1.83. That, no doubt, was one of the reasons the staff arranged the rotation so he would make this start. He will be pitching on five days' rest.
away_pitcher_note: Kennedy was by no means dominant in his Arizona debut, but he kept the D-backs in a game in which they eventually prevailed over the Padres, 5-3, at Chase Field. The right-hander allowed three runs -- all of which came on a Scott Hairston homer in the second -- on six hits over five innings. The Padres made him work hard and ran up his pitch count early and he wound up throwing 94, 64 of which went for strikes. He appeared in just one game for the Yankees in 2009 and four in Triple-A after missing most of the year following surgery to remove an aneurysm near his right shoulder. The right-hander came in the same three-team trade that netted the D-backs Edwin Jackson.

home_pitcher_note: Chad Billingsley was an All-Star last year based on a solid first half of the season, and he got off to a similar start in Pittsburgh last week while allowing one run over 5 1/3 innings and striking out seven. Billingsley seems to have succeeded in working through a mechanical flaw he blames for his second-half fade last year that ultimately cost him a spot in the postseason starting rotation. His winning start in Pittsburgh was a continuation of a solid Spring Training. He was 1-1 with a 3.50 ERA against the Diamondbacks last year, struggling in his only start at Chase Field, a no-decision.
away_pitcher_note: Lopez was outstanding in his Arizona debut last Friday night against the Pirates. The right-hander allowed just one run on six hits over six innings. He even got into the action at the plate when he led off what would turn out to be a six-run third inning with a single to right off Charlie Morton. While not overpowering, Lopez has a good feel for pitching and manages a game well. Lopez came to Spring Training as a non-roster invitee and pitched his way into the No. 4 spot in the rotation, besting Billy Buckner and Kevin Mulvey. The right-hander has battled arm troubles since being the ace of the Orioles' staff earlier in the decade. He throws a fastball, cutter, curveball, slider and change. Lopez appeared in seven games (five starts) for the Phillies last year and also started 18 games for Triple-A Lehigh Valley.

home_pitcher_note: The first time through the rotation and Hiroki Kuroda looked more like the pitcher deserving of last year's Opening Day start than the fourth slot that he now occupies. A determined Kuroda allowed one unearned run over eight innings to a Florida Marlins lineup that scored six and seven runs the next two games against other Dodgers pitchers. Kuroda struck out seven and walked only one. Now he just needs to stay healthy. He suffered his first injury last year in a bullpen session after his first start. Kuroda is 1-3 with a 3.90 ERA in six lifetime starts against the D-backs and 8-6 with a 3.81 ERA in 23 starts at Dodger Stadium. He will again be pitching on five days' rest because of the Monday day off.
away_pitcher_note: Haren turned in an uncharacteristically poor start Saturday against the visiting Pittsburgh Pirates. After allowing six runs (five earned) on nine hits over 6 2/3 frames and picking up his first defeat of 2010, the veteran right-hander admitted he didn't have his best stuff. He left his fastball up in the zone Saturday and, as a result, surrendered home runs to the Pirates' Jeff Clement and Aki Iwamura. On the plus side, Haren did whiff nine batters. Thursday, he will attempt to get back on track against the Los Angeles Dodgers. In four 2009 starts against the Dodgers, Haren went 0-1 with a 2.22 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Padilla gets a third chance to justify his selection as Opening Day starter. The first two tries didn't go very well, with an 11.42 ERA and 18 baserunners allowed in 8 2/3 innings. He's failed to get out of the fifth inning both times. Padilla showed his value after joining the Dodgers for last year's stretch run, but he's since been shot in the thigh and fought through forearm discomfort in Spring Training. He said neither problem bothers him, but he doesn't look like the same pitcher. His hard sinker is hanging and he's been very hittable. He's also hit two batters, a trouble sign considering his previous reputation as a headhunter. He was 1-0 in two starts against the Giants last year.
away_pitcher_note: The Giants obviously have confidence in Wellemeyer, since Thursday's scheduled off-day could have allowed them to skip his turn. Wellemeyer's Giants debut last Saturday began in promising fashion as he blanked Atlanta on four hits through five innings. But after he allowed a Jason Heyward homer in the sixth, the Braves nicked him for three runs in the seventh and proceeded to win. Wellemeyer has made six career appearances against Los Angeles with no decisions and a 4.26 ERA. That includes four outings, all but one in relief, and a 4.00 ERA at Dodger Stadium.
summary: 2010-04-16 - San Francisco Giants (8) @ Los Angeles Dodgers (10) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Yes, it's Charlie Haeger time again. He started Sunday, he relieved Wednesday and Haeger said he's good to go for his scheduled start Saturday against the Giants. The knuckleballer struck out 12 Marlins in six innings in his season debut, the most strikeouts to open a season by a Dodgers starter since Don Drysdale fanned 14 in 1960. Haeger has quickly earned the reliance of manager Joe Torre because of his resilience, but also because he's been effective. While the knuckler dances, he has enough of a fastball to keep hitters off-balance. And at a time when the Dodgers are getting a steady diet of short starts, he's capable of pitching deep into games.
away_pitcher_note: Lincecum has worked seven innings in each of his two starts. His only lapse was Brian McCann's two-run, first-inning homer last Sunday for Atlanta. Lincecum has had mixed success at Dodger Stadium, where he's 1-1 with a 4.50 ERA in four outings. His most recent appearance in Chavez Ravine, last Sept. 20, was atypical. He allowed five runs and four hits in only four innings while walking four and striking out just three. Andre Ethier ranks among Lincecum's most significant Dodgers tormentors with a .294 average (5-for-17) and one home run off him.
summary: 2010-04-17 - San Francisco Giants (9) @ Los Angeles Dodgers (0) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Kershaw beat himself up after his last start, and he was the winning pitcher. He made it into the sixth inning, an improvement on his 4 2/3-inning  season debut, and he picked up his first win since last July, but he walked five and now has 11 walks in 10 innings. It's easy to forget that Kershaw is only 22, but the Dodgers are counting on him to take his game to the next level and not show the inconsistency that plagued him over the first half last year. He was able to work in off-speed pitches in his last start, but struggled with command of his fastball. As important as his other pitches are, Kershaw's calling card is an overpowering fastball that he needs to throw for strikes from the outset.
away_pitcher_note: Zito, who has made 100 starts as a Giant, is 2-0 for only the second time in his career. He hasn't started this well in any of his nine previous full seasons since 2003, when he pitched for Oakland. Zito proceeded to finish that season with a career-high 231 2/3 innings, as well as 14-12 record and a 3.30 ERA. That was one year after he won the American League Cy Young Award with a 23-5 mark and a 2.75 ERA. Zito is 6-5 with a 4.46 ERA in 13 career starts against Los Angeles, including 4-2, 3.62 in six Dodger Stadium assignments.
summary: 2010-04-18 - San Francisco Giants (1) @ Los Angeles Dodgers (2) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Through two starts, Bailey hasn't looked like the guys who seemed to turn a corner toward the end of the 2009 season. A pitch-conservation issue is brewing as he's lasted five innings in both starts and thrown more than 100 pitches in that short amount of time.  In a 5-3 loss to the Marlins on Wednesday, the right-hander allowed five earned runs and eight hits over 5 1/3 innings with four walks and three strikeouts. He threw 115 pitches, 72 for strikes. "It's a situation where we have to find a way to get him out of the gate quicker and minimize those pitches earlier so he can go deeper in the game," Reds manager Dusty Baker said.
away_pitcher_note: It's back to the Eastern time zone for the second time this month and an important start for Billingsley, who regressed against Arizona after an impressive season debut in Pittsburgh. Billingsley was roughed up for six runs in 5 2/3 innings by the Diamondbacks, He breezed through the first three innings scoreless, then allowed a home run to Stephen Drew leading off the fourth inning and seemed like a different pitcher thereafter. Manager Joe Torre said Billingsley appeared to start overthrowing when things got bad, which only made them worse. Nobody has mentioned a relapse of the mechanical issues that were blamed for Billingsley's second-half fade last season.

home_pitcher_note: During a 10-2 Reds loss to the Marlins on Thursday, Harang was pummeled for eight earned runs and 10 hits over four-plus innings with two walks and four strikeouts. He faced four batters in the fifth inning and did not record an out. Harang has been staying with mostly fastballs and sliders and in between starts worked on trying to make more use of his offspeed pitches, namely the changeup and curveball.
away_pitcher_note: It's only two starts into the season, but Kuroda, originally the fourth starter in the rotation, has emerged as the early ace. He's throwing strikes (14 strikeouts, one walk), going deep into games (eight innings in one start, seven in the other) and the club has won both of his starts. Kuroda also showed in his last start the ability to adjust, shifting from an ineffective four-seamer to a slider that Diamondbacks hitters waved at. Clearly, Kuroda is healthier than at just about any time last year. And when he's healthy and pitching with confidence, he's probably as well-equipped to be an ace as anyone in the Dodgers rotation.

home_pitcher_note: Leake has two quality starts in two big league outings. His latest performance was a solid seven innings for a no-decision against the Pirates on Friday. He allowed three earned runs and seven hits with five walks and three strikeouts while throwing 99 pitches. Walks have been the one downside of Leake's performances -- he's already racked up 12 in his two games. In the beginning of his start vs. Pittsburgh, Leake was having trouble getting into a groove and locating his sinker. He made the adjustment and started throwing more offspeed pitches, which proved much more successful.
away_pitcher_note: A Padilla sinker that got away broke some bones in Aaron Rowand's cheek last week, but don't expect that to change the way Padilla pitches. He has a reputation for hitting opponents, and while there were no accusations of any malice on his part this time, he doesn't seem to have the personality of shying away. More important to the Dodgers' success, Padilla was much improved against the Giants compared to his first two starts of the season, each ending after 4 1/3 innings. This time he delivered a quality start of seven innings, the first four hitless. Pitching coach Rick Honeycutt said Padilla was able to implement a minor tweak in his mechanics and the results speak for themselves.

home_pitcher_note: Atilano was to be recalled from Triple-A Syracuse to make this start in place of Jason Marquis, who was placed on the 15-day disabled list Wednesday with bone chips in his right elbow. This will be Atilano's Major League debut. The 24-year-old has pitched in two games for Syracuse, giving up two runs in 11 innings. He was acquired from the Braves in 2006 for first baseman Daryle Ward. At the time of the trade, Atilano was recovering from elbow reconstruction, but he went a combined 9-8 with a 4.01 ERA for Double-A Harrisburg and Syracuse last season.
away_pitcher_note: Haeger, the Dodgers' resident workhorse, might've run out of steam during Saturday's outing against the Giants. Haeger lasted just three innings, allowing seven runs, five earned, on seven hits. He walked five and struck out three. Haeger was coming off a relief appearance on Wednesday, three days after he made a stellar season debut, striking out 12 Marlins in six innings, the most strikeouts to open a season by a Dodgers starter since Don Drysdale fanned 14 in 1960. Haeger has quickly earned the reliance of manager Joe Torre because of his resilience, but also because he's been effective.

home_pitcher_note: A conversation with teammate Livan Hernandez helped Stammen make up for his previous two starts, and the Nationals defeated the Rockies, 5-2, at Nationals Park on Monday night. Stammen pitched a combined 6 1/3 innings and gave up 11 runs on 16 hits in those previous two starts. After his second start against the Phillies, in which he lasted only 1 1/3 innings, Stammen had a talk with Hernandez, who pitched a shutout Saturday against the Brewers. Hernandez told Stammen to relax, just like he would on the golf course, and work on his pitches in the bullpen. The advice Stammen received must have paid off. The young right-hander pitched eight innings, allowing two runs on five hits, striking out five batters and walking one.
away_pitcher_note: Dodgers fans have seen the best and worst of Kershaw this season. The 22-year old left-hander has had better command of his fastball and appears to be comfortable on the mound these days. But, then there's the walks. Lots of them. Kershaw issued four free passes in his last start on Sunday. He has issued 15 walks in three starts, comprising 17 total innings. But he's managed to keep his games under control. Kershaw owns a 3.18 ERA, and in Sunday's outing he allowed just one earned run on four hits with nine strikeouts in seven innings.

home_pitcher_note: Olsen had an outing he would like to forget in his last start. He lasted two-plus innings -- including four batters in the third -- and gave up six runs on seven hits. Olsen got off to a good start, retiring the side in order in the first inning, but it went downhill after that. His pitches were up in the strike zone. In the second inning, Troy Tulowitzki led off by hitting his first homer of the season. Miguel Olivo then scored on a double by Ian Stewart. In the next frame, 12 batters came to the plate for Colorado as it scored eight runs. Olsen faced four hitters and didn't retire a single one. Olsen insisted there was nothing wrong with his left shoulder, which was surgically repaired last summer.
away_pitcher_note: Billingsley lasted just three innings in Tuesday night's 11-9 loss at Cincinnati. He allowed seven runs, four earned, on seven hits, struck out two and did not walk a batter. His throwing error on Homer Bailey's sacrifice bunt attempt helped ignite a six-run second inning for the Reds. Although it was his second consecutive rough outing, Billingsley insists he feels fine physically and is pleased with the location of his pitches. Dodgers manager Joe Torre, who met  with Billingsley on Wednesday, said poor location has been his primary issue. Pitching coach Rick Honeycutt said it's possible Billingsley is trying to be too fine with his pitches.

home_pitcher_note: The Perez Pendulum continues to swing. Perez's last start wasn't on either ended of the swing. He lost to the offensively-challenged Cubs, allowing 11 baserunners in five innings, including seven in an 11-batter sequence in the his final two innings, but he allowed merely three runs. He didn't break, but he did bend considerably. Now he faces an opponent he has beaten three times in four starts in the last three seasons. Moreover, Perez has a 2.84 ERA in 25 1/3 innings in those starts. His success may be in some jeopardy Monday. Russell Martin, Matt Kemp, Garrett Anderson and Jamey Carroll have batted .486 in 35 composite at-bats against him.
away_pitcher_note: Kuroda wasn't too pleased with his outing on Wednesday except for the fact that the Dodgers won, largely due to a 14-run, 18-hit outburst against the Reds at Great American Ball Park. Kuroda kept the game close, giving the Dodgers a chance to rally from an early 3-1 deficit. He allowed six runs, three earned, on seven hits, struck out four and walked two in a 103-pitch effort. He allowed two home runs. Prior to Wednesday's outing, Kuroda had gone 15 innings without allowing a home run and had issued just two walks in 14 innings. Dodgers manager Joe Torre wasn't concerned with Kuroda's outing and was impressed with the way he battled for a victory despite not having his best stuff.
summary: 2010-04-26 - Los Angeles Dodgers @ New York Mets (Postponed)

home_pitcher_note: Santana has allowed one run in 13 1/3 innings over his past two starts, and he's off to an exceptional start, walking only six and striking out 22 in his first 24 1/3 innings. Santana is 2-0 with a 0.61 ERA in two career starts against the Dodgers.
