Haeger will make this start with three days' rest, which is less of an issue with a knuckleball pitcher. By doing that, the club can keep Jon Link an extra day for bullpen use. Haeger is coming off an improved start in Washington, but a loss nonetheless. He did take the game into the sixth inning and kept his club in it. He allowed two homers to Adam Dunn, a solo shot on a knuckleball that didn't knuckle, and a two-run shot on a fastball down the middle. He walked only one, the last batter he faced.
summary: 2010-04-27 - Los Angeles Dodgers (5) @ New York Mets (10) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Maine was removed from his most recent start, Friday against the Braves, in the fourth inning because of muscle spasms and pain in his left -- yes, left -- elbow. He threw 63 pitches in 3 2/3 innings, allowing four hits and two walks and striking out three. Now he is to pitch against an opponent that has been a problem for him. Maine has a 1-4 record in six career starts against the Dodgers. Beware Ronnie Belliard, who has a .600 average and one home run in 15 career at-bats against Maine, and Rafael Furcal, who has batted .545 in 11 at-bats against him. The Mets have lost five of Maine's eight most recent starts over two seasons.
away_pitcher_note: Ely's name dropped out of the probable pitchers list for the Triple-A Albuquerque Dukes and showed up in the Dodgers clubhouse Tuesday, although the club has not confirmed he will make this start. The Dodgers need a pitcher Wednesday to take the place of disabled Opening Day starter Vicente Padilla, and Ely -- a 23-year-old right-hander taken out of Miami (Ohio) University in the third round of the 2007 Draft -- could be it. He went 14-2 with a 2.82 ERA at Double-A last year and is 2-1 with a 3.00 ERA in three starts for Albuquerque, having last pitched April 21. He has 12 strikeouts, but also eight walks, in 18 innings.
summary: 2010-04-28 - Los Angeles Dodgers (3) @ New York Mets (7) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Kershaw put on an escape act in Washington in his last start. He allowed eight hits and three walks in six innings, wiggling out of enough jams for the Nationals to strand eight runners, six in scoring position. The 18 walks in 23 innings are a troublesome sign for the left-hander, but he is keeping his club in the game as the Dodgers were able to pull out a win from his last start in the 13th inning. Kershaw didn't make it out of the fifth inning in his first start of the season in Pittsburgh, but after the first three batters scored on Garrett Jones' first-inning homer, he didn't allow a run.
away_pitcher_note: The Pirates have named Burres their spot starter for Thursday. The Pirates continue to try to bridge the gap to Ross Ohlendorf's return to the rotation, and they are hopeful that Burres can get the job done. Burres was called up on Sunday to provide reinforcement to an overworked bullpen and pitched 1 2/3 innings in Sunday's game. He allowed two earned runs on three hits and three walks in that outing. This is already Burres' second stint with the big league club this season. He allowed six runs on eight hits in a four-inning start against the Giants on April 12. Burres has never faced the Dodgers before.

home_pitcher_note: Billingsley came up with the rebound effort the Dodgers were counting on after the serious meeting he had with manager Joe Torre and pitching coach Rick Honeycutt in the wake of his three-inning start in Cincinnati. Sticking with just a fastball and curve, Billingsley said he tried to simplify his pitching approach and the hardball style really suited him, as he shook off a first-inning run and allowed the Nationals nothing further in six innings. It was the closest Billingsley has looked to the first-half All-Star he was a year ago.
away_pitcher_note: Morton has been nothing close to the reliable arm that the Pirates expected to have this season. He has not pitched a full four innings in three of his four outings and has allowed at least five runs per start. Morton has had a hard time pinpointing the issues, too. In some cases, pitch selection has been a problem. In other starts, it's been fastball command or a hesitancy to be aggressive enough with his fastball. You have to wonder if the terrible season start is starting to have an effect on Morton's mental fortitude, particularly given his lack of big league experience.  This will be Morton's first career appearance against the Dodgers.

home_pitcher_note: Rookie reliever Carlos Monasterios is scheduled to make his starting debut. Monasterios has six strikeouts and three walks in 10 2/3 innings over seven appearances, although he's allowed the only two runners he's inherited to score and hasn't been relied on in magnified spots. Manager Joe Torre said he hoped Monasterios could throw 70 to 75 pitches. If Monasterios struggles, Ramon Ortiz (0-1, 6.39 ERA), who was also a candidate to start the game, could work in long relief.
away_pitcher_note: Command has been a serious issue for Duke in his last two starts, both of which were losses to Milwaukee. Typically efficient and in the strike zone, Duke walked eight in nine total innings against the Brewers. His last outing lasted a season-short four innings. And altogether, Duke has allowed 15 runs in his last nine innings. For Duke to get back on track, it will start with getting ahead in counts and regaining dominance with his sinker. Duke was sharp early in the season, so the hope is that this two-game stretch has been nothing more than a hiccup. He is 3-3 with a 5.50 ERA in nine career starts against the Dodgers.

home_pitcher_note: Kuroda has been the most consistent starter in the Dodgers' rotation this year, an interesting achievement after one month, considering that he was coming off an injury-plagued season that relegated him to fourth on the depth chart at the start of the year. He's proven to be healthy and effective so far. In his latest start against the Mets last week, he delivered another quality outing of six innings with two runs allowed and pitched out of two jams, but the Dodgers scored nothing against Johan Santana in support of Kuroda. He's 2-1 with a 2.74 ERA in four career starts against the Pirates and 1-0 with a 3.00 ERA in two starts against Pittsburgh at home.
away_pitcher_note: Called up from Triple-A to plug a rotation vacancy, Karstens is here to stay for the time being. His 6 2/3-inning outing on Tuesday was enough to earn Karstens another start for a Pirates team that has been looking for anyone to seize the opportunity to claim a rotation spot. Karstens allowed just two hits and never labored much in the 101-pitch effort against the Brewers. The start came after he moved from a relief role to a starting one in Triple-A because that club was running out of starting options.

home_pitcher_note: Kershaw walked the first two batters in his last start, they both scored on a misplay by center fielder Matt Kemp, and that was all it took to saddle the left-hander with a loss. Almost overlooked was the fact that he pitched the Dodgers into the seventh inning, allowed no other runs and only two other hits. He's still a little erratic and walks too many batters, but he's the Dodgers starter most capable of dominating an opponent. Nothing wrong with a 3.07 ERA. He's allowed Colorado only two runs in 16 innings at Dodger Stadium.
away_pitcher_note: Narveson allowed three runs and two home runs in five innings in his first start of the season against the Pirates. He struck out five and walked two and got a no decision. He has taken Jeff Suppan's place in the rotation. In his first stint with the Brewers last season, he struggled with an 8.44 ERA in nine relief outings before being sent to Nashville. He was switched to a starting assignment in Nashville and later returned to the Brewers, going 1-0 with a 3.38 ERA in four starts in September.

home_pitcher_note: If two starts is a trend, Billingsley is back on track. After two shaky starts, he's rebounded with two quality starts against Washington and Pittsburgh while trimming his ERA from 7.07 to 4.85. He's done it by returning to the basics, throwing fewer cutters and relying on fastballs and curves. He said his goal is to simplify his approach. The Dodgers can't argue with the results. His only start last year against the Brewers was in Miller Park, and it wasn't pretty: five earned runs and four walks in a five-inning no-decision.
away_pitcher_note: Davis took the loss on Thursday in San Diego, but suffered an unusual fate, as all eight of the hits he allowed were singles.  He gave up six runs (five earned) over four innings, and the Padres proceeded to hit only singles throughout the course of the game as the Brewers fell, 9-0.  Davis fared better in his previous start, allowing only two runs over 6 1/3 innings, but has been knocked out of each of his other five starts prior to the fifth inning.  He is 5-4 for his career against the Dodgers, with a 3.51 ERA in 12 starts.

home_pitcher_note: Eight days after his Major League debut, Ely gets another shot at being the fifth starter. Against the Mets, he made it through six innings, which is more than some of his more experienced teammates have done this year. He showed enough poise to rebound from two shaky innings early, but he looked the part of a rookie in those shaky innings and cost himself three runs with a poor defensive decision on a comebacker. He also allowed four extra-base hits, perhaps an indicator that he doesn't have the velocity to get away with mistake pitches. He came into that start with only three games above Double-A.
away_pitcher_note: Bush pitched well enough against the Padres on Friday (three runs on six hits in seven innings), especially considering that he had been shelled in his previous outing against the Cubs to the tune of nine runs on 10 hits, including a career-high four homers, in 3 2/3 innings. But he didn't get any support at all from an offense that ran its scoreless streak to 22 innings in a 3-0 loss. Nevertheless, Bush will try to build on the positives from that outing when he faces the Dodgers for the fourth time in his career. He owns a 3.98 ERA in his three previous starts against them, including a 4.15 ERA in two starts at Dodger Stadium.

home_pitcher_note: Kuroda started the year fourth on the rotation depth chart but he's become the de facto ace. He showed why again on Sunday with eight dominant innings against the Pirates, pitching efficiently with a large lead. Unlike the other Dodgers starters, Kuroda is crafty enough to thrive even when he doesn't have all of his pitches working. And he doesn't cause his own problems, throwing enough strikes to post a strikeout-to-walk ratio  of better than 3-to-1. This is the Kuroda the Dodgers thought they were signing, but his first two seasons were marred by injuries. He is 0-2 with a 7.00 ERA in three career starts against the Rockies.
away_pitcher_note: Rogers wasn't terrible in his first start of the season, but he wasn't efficient either. The Rockies were hoping to get more than four innings out of their rookie, but with his pitch count at 92, he was finished. He gave up five runs on five hits and four walks. He struck out two. Rockies manager Jim Tracy said Rogers would get another start just so he doesn't feel like the team is losing any confidence in him. He's got great stuff and he started the year with the Rockies as a reliever. Once he understands his starting role, Rogers should be quite effective. He'll be making his first career appearance at Dodger Stadium.

home_pitcher_note: Charlie Haeger's move to the bullpen was never exactly official, but that's the flexibility manager Joe Torre has with a knuckleballer. Haeger threw four innings of one-run ball Tuesday out of the 'pen, just his second relief appearance of the season and his first since his pseudo-demotion. It was enough to impress Torre to return Haeger to the fifth-starter's role he had out of Spring Training -- at least for one start. Haeger, 0-3 with a 6.56 ERA, has had trouble controlling his floater: he has 23 strikeouts to 17 walks, and a 1.84 WHIP in 23 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Chacin, 22, made nine appearances for the Rockies last season and displayed secondary pitches that were comparable to those of some of baseball's top pitchers. However, one start against the Pirates unmasked the fact that when called up, he didn't have location or command of his fastball. But on Sunday, after being called up because of injuries to the rotation, Chacin showed what he can do when he's spotting his fastball. He held the Giants to one hit and struck out nine in seven scoreless innings. With consistent fastball command, he could emerge as a Rookie of the Year candidate.

home_pitcher_note: Kershaw did not seem rattled after he managed just four outs and allowed seven earned runs in a start against the Brewers on Tuesday. Kershaw saw his ERA jump by nearly two runs to 4.99 ERA. His strikeout rate is good: 36 in 30 2/3 innings, but he's struggling to locate, with 24 walks. He hasn't fared well against the Rockies, who have a .260 batting average against him. Only the Phillies (.269), and, after Tuesday, the Brewers (.279) have hit him at a better clip in the NL.
away_pitcher_note: Jimenez celebrated the May 3 announcement that he was the NL Pitcher of the Month of April by slamming the door shut on the Padres with a career-high 13 strikeouts and one run against in seven innings of a 5-2 victory. Knowing the Padres wanted to take pitches, Jimenez pounded them with high-velocity strikes early and often. Now comes another test for Jimenez. He is 2-1 but with a 7.53 ERA in six starts at Dodger Stadium.

home_pitcher_note: Lopez pitched well enough to win in his last start against the Astros in Houston, but came away with a no-decision. The right-hander allowed two runs on three hits over seven innings. He left with the game tied at 2-2 -- both Houston runs came on a Tommy Manzella homer in the second -- and watched the bullpen lose it in the ninth. Lopez contributed to his own demise in his start prior to that. The right-hander tried to field a pop fly in the infield and collided with first baseman Adam LaRoche, who had a better play on the ball. The Cubs went on to score four runs in the inning and eventually prevailed, 11-5. While not overpowering, Lopez has a good feel for pitching and manages a game well. Lopez came to Spring Training as a non-roster invitee and pitched his way into the No. 4 spot in the rotation, besting Billy Buckner and Kevin Mulvey. The right-hander has battled arm troubles since being the ace of the Orioles' staff earlier in the decade. He throws a fastball, cutter, curveball, slider and change.
away_pitcher_note: Chad Billingsley has yet to make it into the seventh inning this season, yet he bounced back from a four-run first inning in his last start against the Pirates to go six innings and allow no further scoring. That's Billingsley's season in a nutshell: some good, some bad, but nothing consistent in either direction. At 2-2 with a 5.06 ERA and a 1.59 WHIP, he's nowhere near the first-half pitcher he was last season when he was selected to the All-Star Game.

home_pitcher_note: Haren notched his first complete game of 2010 in his last outing against the Astros in Houston. The right-hander allowed three runs (two earned) on seven hits and struck out nine. He had a bit of a stomach bug the morning of his previous start against the Cubs at Wrigley Field. Still he managed to scatter 10 hits over six innings and depart with a 5-3 lead. The bullpen, though, let him down and the Cubs wound up winning 7-5. He's been a force at the plate this year, going 10-for-22 with a three doubles. Haren has been used as a pinch-hitter once this year already.
away_pitcher_note: John Ely takes his regular turn in the rotation, despite being optioned and recalled since his last start in a classic example of roster manipulation. In his second Major League start, Ely allowed Milwaukee one earned run on four hits in 6 2/3 innings after the Brewers had scored 11 runs in back-to-back games. Although he never broke the 90-mph mark on the radar gun, he worked the corners and lived up to his winning reputation in the Minor Leagues for being a smart pitcher. Ely can throw four pitches for strikes and seemed to gain confidence pitching in the comfortable environment of Dodger Stadium after a shaky debut in New York.

home_pitcher_note: Jackson's last start was an improvement over his two previous ones. The right-hander allowed three runs on six hits over seven innings to the Brewers at Chase Field. The D-backs didn't do much with the bats against Yovani Gallardo in the game and Jackson took a 3-2 loss. In his previous two starts, Jackson allowed 18 runs in 6 1/3 innings against the Rockies and Cubs. The key for Jackson is to be aggressive early in counts and not fall behind. When hitters get the advantage in the count, they are more apt to dial up to reach his mid-90s fastball. Jackson was acquired by Arizona in a three-team trade during the Winter Meetings that sent Max Scherzer and Daniel Schlereth to the Tigers. The D-backs are his third team in three years. He pitched for Tampa Bay in 2008 before being dealt to the Tigers before last year. Jackson throws a fastball, curve, slider and change.
away_pitcher_note: Hiroki Kuroda is coming off his worst start of the season, although the Dodgers got lucky because of sloppy Colorado defense and won the game anyway. He allowed more runs (four) and recorded fewer outs (16) than in any of his other starts and set a career high with five walks (two intentional). This also will be Kuroda's first start at Chase Field since he was taken off the mound in an ambulance after getting drilled on the head by a Rusty Ryal line drive last Aug. 15 while in the midst of a three-hitter. Kuroda returned from that frightening episode in three weeks but was left with a whiplash-induced herniated disk in his neck. He's been healthy enough to make every start so far this year.

home_pitcher_note: Garland, who followed Mat Latos' eight shutout innings one night earlier in Houston with seven of his own, continues to shine in his first season with the Padres. Garland, in lowering his ERA to 1.71, allowed two hits with just one walk as well as two strikeouts. As he does when he's going well, Garland got 10 ground outs with a sinking fastball, a slider and a vastly improved changeup. "He pounded the strike zone, down and outside," said Padres catcher Yorvit Torrealba. "He was throwing every pitch I wanted him to throw -- where I wanted him to throw it."  Garland continues to get a lot of mileage out of his changeup as well as his sinker.
away_pitcher_note: The Dodgers continue to give new meaning to the word "rotation" by handing a spot start to Ramon Ortiz. A non-roster pitcher who made the club out of Spring Training as a reliever, Ortiz will be making his first Major League start since May 26, 2007. He's been in Triple-A and Japan since then and gets his start almost by default, considering a 5.24 ERA. But in his most recent outing, he picked up the pieces when starter Charlie Haeger could not retire a batter and went five innings out of the bullpen, allowing two runs on six hits, including a home run to the first batter he faced. The Dodgers would take a duplication of that outing in this start against the Padres. With just one career PETCO Park start, Ortiz is 1-0 with a 3.00 ERA.
summary: 2010-05-14 - Los Angeles Dodgers (4) @ San Diego Padres (3) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Correia will be making his first start since his younger brother died in a fall while hiking last Saturday. Correia was originally scheduled to start a game on May 11 in Houston but flew back to San Diego instead. He is the owner of the highest run-support numbers (9.26 runs per game) in the league and is a perfect 20-0 when he gets at least four runs of support. Correia -- who has gotten double-digit run support twice this season -- has seen his teams go 14-0 when he gets six runs of support. The 29-year-old right-hander is 24-4 when he gets at least three runs. The runs would be much welcomed, considering the Padres have struggled at times in scoring. On Tuesday in San Francisco, they stranded 15 on base in a 3-2 victory over the Giants.
away_pitcher_note: Kershaw gets an extra day of rest coming off his best start of the year, in which he allowed two hits in eight shutout innings in a win over the Brewers. Kershaw repeated a pattern he's used before, rebounding from a horrible start (1 1/3 innings, seven runs) with a masterpiece. Three of the five base runners he allowed came in the first inning. After that, he retired 21 of 23 batters, including the last nine he faced, four by strikeout. It's the flash of overpowering brilliance of which he's capable, and when he put it together last year, he was able to repeat for a two-month run. He's 2-2 lifetime against the Padres and has no-decisions in both career starts at PETCO Park.
summary: 2010-05-15 - Los Angeles Dodgers (4) @ San Diego Padres (1) (Final)

away_pitcher_note: Chad Billingsley still has a ways to go to regain his manager's confidence. With a 4-1 lead in the sixth inning, Billingsley was yanked with one out and runners on second and third in Arizona in his last start, a very quick hook for a club whose starters have struggled getting deep into games. He struck out seven, but walked four and his 4.82 ERA is more than a run higher than his career average. He's 8-4 with a 2.71 ERA in his career against the Padres, 3-2 with a 2.77 ERA at PETCO Park.
summary: 2010-05-16 - Los Angeles Dodgers (1) @ San Diego Padres (0) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Most winning teams get contributions from the least expected places, and that's the case with Ely, who gets Monday's start against the Astros. Rebounding from a wobbly debut, Ely has posted back-to-back impressive starts. He throws strikes, works both sides of the plate with four reliable pitches and isn't intimidated by Major League hitters or his lack of an overpowering fastball. He's a cheerleader in the dugout, energetic on the field and fun to watch. And to opponents, he's still something of a mystery. His next challenge will be to make the adjustments necessary as opposing teams get a more thorough scouting line on him.
away_pitcher_note: Still searching for the rhythm that made him a feared piece of the Astros' rotation last season, Rodriguez surrendered five runs (four earned) over six innings in a winning effort against the Cardinals in his last start. Still, Rodriguez hasn't posted a quality start in May. He'll look to pick up win No. 3 when he takes on the Dodgers, against whom the lefty is 3-2 with a 2.70 ERA in his career.

home_pitcher_note: Hiroki Kuroda delivered another quality start in his return to Chase Field, site of last year's frightening drilling by a Rusty Ryal line drive. Kuroda admitted first-batter jitters led to a four-pitch walk, but he regrouped to allow two earned runs over 7 1/3 innings while striking out nine. Kuroda relied on his slider while lacking his customary two-seam fastball, but he's become the de facto staff ace this season by being able to win without his best stuff. He is 1-0 with a 1.93 in three career starts against the Astros.
away_pitcher_note: Norris is coming off the perhaps the best start of his career Thursday in St. Louis in which he held the Cardinals to six hits and one run and struck out eight batters without walking anybody to snap a three-start losing streak. He improved to 4-0 lifetime against St. Louis, which accounts for half of his career wins.  This will be the California native's first career start against the Dodgers. He's 4-2 with a 4.22 ERA in eight career games (seven starts) on the road in his career, including 2-1 this year.

home_pitcher_note: Ortiz, making his first Major League start in nearly three years, was charged with three runs in four-plus innings Friday night, when the Dodgers rallied to beat the Padres. That, and the fact that the Dodgers have few other options, convinced manager Joe Torre to give him another spot start. Torre praised Ortiz's ability to minimize damage, and while that's a back-handed compliment of sorts, the manager also said he went with Ortiz instead of rookie Carlos Monasterios because Ortiz's pitch count is now approaching 90. A career starter, Ortiz said he finds it easier to prepare for starts with a regular five-day routine after pitching the first month out of the bullpen.
away_pitcher_note: Garland was in line for his fifth victory of the season in his last start against the Dodgers on Friday, but a rare blown save by reliever Luke Gregerson cost him. Garland, who entered the game with a 1.71 ERA, had trouble with his command almost from the start of the game, though his occasional knack for keeping his sinker where it belonged -- buried in the strike zone -- bailed him out of trouble twice, as he got inning-ending double plays in the second and third innings. All told, he allowed two runs over six innings.  Garland felt he could have pitched better. "Way too many balls, way too many walks. ... I gave them too many opportunities," he said. "It definitely seemed like a big struggle out there."
summary: 2010-05-19 - San Diego Padres (10) @ Los Angeles Dodgers (5) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: In his last outing on Saturday, Kershaw held the Padres to one run on three hits in seven innings, his second outstanding start in a row after he outdueled Ubaldo Jimenez on May 9. Kershaw has rebounded from the worst start of his career on May 4 to allow just five hits and one run in his last 15 innings over his last pair of starts, both wins. He's also struck out 16 and waked just five in that span.
away_pitcher_note: In his first start since his young brother, Trevor, died in a fall while hiking, Correia allowed four runs on five hits in 5 1/3 innings in a loss to the Dodgers. "I wish we could have given him something special," Padres second baseman David Eckstein said.  In a sense, Correia said, they did. "It's good that everyone came up and showed their support," Correia said of the support of his teammates. "It helps to know they are thinking about you when you are not here." Correia allowed a solo home run to James Loney in the second inning but yielded only two hits over the first four innings.  "From pitch one, I felt pretty good," he said. He ran into trouble thereafter, as he admitted he started to tire.
summary: 2010-05-20 - San Diego Padres (1) @ Los Angeles Dodgers (4) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Billingsley has gotten away from trying to sink the ball, relying more on his four-seamer and curveball, and the result his last two starts has been an ERA drop of more than a full run. Billingsley went 7 1/3 scoreless innings in a 1-0 victory over the Padres on Sunday, and in his previous start he went 5 1/3 innings and allowed two runs in a win over the D-backs. He had a 5.06 ERA entering that start in Arizona.
away_pitcher_note: The Tigers' comeback against the Red Sox last Saturday night allowed Willis to stretch his unbeaten streak to three starts, but it didn't let him escape the frustration of a wild outing. With seven walks over 3 1/3 innings and just 40 of his 86 pitches for strikes, it marked the first time this season that Willis showed signs of his past control woes for more than an inning. He was pitching for the first time in 11 days, and he still seemed lethargic after missing his last start with the flu, but he didn't want to use that as an excuse. If pitching in his hometown doesn't give him a little energy boost, it would be a surprise.

home_pitcher_note: Ely is a strike-throwing machine, not having issued a walk to any of the last 84 batters he's faced. He's one of the rare players who actually has pitched better in the Major Leagues than he did in the Minor Leagues prior to his promotion. His manager likes the way Ely competes, and he surely is not intimidated by the opposition at the Major League level. He doesn't throw hard, but never has and has refined the more subtle skills of pitching, like command and composure to win a spot in the Dodgers' starting rotation.
away_pitcher_note: What was initially thought to be a spot start for Galarraga last Sunday against the Red Sox became a two-start audition once the Tigers sent down the struggling Max Scherzer. The Tigers' series opener at Dodger Stadium is the latter half of that stint, but another solid outing would make it all but impossible to pull Galarraga from the rotation. He held Boston to a run on three hits over 5 2/3 innings, retiring 10 Red Sox in a row at one point, striking out five for the day and showing the aggressiveness that he seemed to lack for much of last year, partly due to a forearm injury. He's 4-2 with a 4.61 ERA in Interleague Play over the past two seasons, including seven scoreless innings against the Dodgers two years ago at Comerica Park.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start, Kuroda uncharacteristically blew a three-run lead. But he stopped the damage there and went the final 3 1/3 innings without allowing a run while giving his offense a chance to come from behind and beat the Astros. This time, Kuroda said his slider wasn't working. Although he throws four pitches, it's rare when they all are effective together. Nonetheless, he's adept enough at pitching to win without his best stuff, which is what he did against Houston.
away_pitcher_note: Porcello has used his sinker for 24 groundouts over his last two starts, but unlike his seven scoreless innings against the Yankees, the White Sox managed to turn one extra-base hit and seven singles into four runs and another loss for Porcello in what has been a rough couple months to his sophomore season. Though he has alternated wins and losses in his last four starts, he has only one quality start in his last six outings and just two all season. Perhaps Interleague Play will be a remedy; he went 3-0 with a 1.90 ERA in four starts against the National League last season.

home_pitcher_note: Dempster has lost four straight decisions, and did not get a decision in his previous start, against the Phillies. He's been roughed up this month, going 0-3 with a 5.00 ERA after compiling a 2.78 ERA over five April starts. He's 6-3 in his career against the Dodgers, including two wins last year.
away_pitcher_note: Kershaw could have put himself into Pitcher of the Month consideration if it weren't for his first start in May, a 1 1/3-inning, seven-run disaster. Everything since then has been gold. He's allowed just two runs in 22 1/3 innings and struck out 23 in three starts, all wins. The key for Kershaw has been controlling his emotions early in the game. Opponents still have a .353 batting average against him through his first 15 pitches.

home_pitcher_note: Gorzelanny had to leave his last start against the Phillies after getting hit on the left hand with a pitch. X-rays were negative and he was not expected to miss a turn. The Cubs do have an off-day Monday, which gives the lefty one extra day of rest. Against the Phillies, he threw 6 2/3 shutout innings, giving up three hits and striking out five.
away_pitcher_note: Billingsley, along with Clayton Kershaw, has given the Dodgers a one-two punch in their dominant May as the team has soared up the standings. Billingsley has gone at least seven innings in his last two starts, and he's allowed just one run and eight hits combined in that span. He has wins in his last three starts, and he's maintaining a strikeout-to-walk ratio better than two-to-one (44 strikeouts and 21 walks). Billingsley was an All-Star and incredibly consistent in the first half of last season, and the change he's made that seems to have him back on that path is a focus away from sinking his fastball. He said he was trying to be something he's not, and has gotten back to his bread-and-butter: his four-seamer and his curveball.

home_pitcher_note: In his previous start, against the Rangers on Friday night, Lilly pitched 6 2/3 innings while giving up two runs on six hits with four strikeouts in a 2-1 loss. In five career starts and one relief appearance against the Dodgers, Lilly is 3-1 with a 3.94 ERA. In three starts at home this season, he is 0-2 with a 5.68 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Ely has been "found money" for the Dodgers in manager Joe Torre's eyes, and it's hard to argue. The rookie right-hander was called up at the end of April because the Dodgers were desperate for pitching, and all Ely's done is throw strikes. He went 89 batters without issuing a walk until the first inning of his last start, against the Tigers. That was his only walk in his last four starts. He went six innings, allowed two runs on eight hits and notched his third straight win. All five of Ely's starts have been six innings or longer. His velocity sits in the high-80s, but he's striking out batters too: 28 in 31 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Francis, after missing last season because of shoulder surgery and having to delay his start to this season while the recovery continued, has had all three of his pitches working in his two starts. When that occurs, it's possible for Francis to achieve what he did in 2007, when he won 17 games and two in the playoffs. A fastball that reaches the low 90s enhances his curve and changeup.
away_pitcher_note: Monasterios makes his first start since May 1, when he allowed one run in four innings of a 5-1 win. He gets the call because Ramon Ortiz allowed eight runs in two starts that lasted a total of 7 1/3 innings. The rookie keeps batters off-balance with a quality changeup, but manager Joe Torre is likely to keep him on a short leash because his arm isn't stretched out. Additionally, because of his lack of experience (only three games above Class-A coming into this season) he's been kept out of most pressure situations whenever possible. He's pitched only five innings since May 8.

home_pitcher_note: What started so good on Sunday ended not so good. Cook held the Royals scoreless for the first four innings but gave up four runs and didn't escape the fifth. The Rockies, who had given Cook a 9-0 lead, still won, 11-7, but Cook didn't get a decision. Cook finished that game with four walks in 4 1/3 innings, and has 25 walks and 25 strikeouts in 50 2/3 innings. The wildness is uncharacteristic.
away_pitcher_note: Kuroda has been a quality-start machine for the Dodgers this year, even though the most recent one was a loss to Detroit. Even in that, after allowing three runs in the first inning, he help the Tigers scoreless over the next five innings. He's walked only one batter in each of the last three starts after an uncharacteristic five-walk wild spell against these Rockies. In his only previous Coors Field start, he was pushed around for five runs in six innings. In four career starts against the Rockies, Kuroda is 0-2 with a 6.94 ERA. Kuroda's turn in the rotation should have come up Friday, but manager Joe Torre wanted to give him an extra day of rest.

home_pitcher_note: Chacin continued to pitch well against the National League West on Tuesday, this time holding the D-backs to four hits and two runs in six innings. He'll be facing the Dodgers on Sunday for the second time, having pitched 7 1/3 scoreless innings against Los Angeles on May 8 for his second win of the year.
away_pitcher_note: Kershaw's three-game win streak was snapped in Chicago, even though he didn't allow an earned run. That made it four consecutive quality starts, during which his ERA is 0.64 with 27 strikeouts in 28 1/3 innings and he's 1-1 with a 2.28 ERA on the road this year. In his most recent start, the Cubs made him work, fouling off enough pitches to run up his pitch count to triple figures after only six innings. But aside from a disastrous start against Milwaukee that lasted only four outs, he's shown the ability this year to control the damage, a very good trait at Coors Field, where he's 2-2 with a 6.92 ERA. The Dodgers have scored 10 runs in his last four starts.

home_pitcher_note: Billingsley had to endure defensive and electrical failures at Wrigley Field in his most recent start, but he still came away a winner, the first Dodger to win six games this year. He went 5 1/3 innings and allowed 10 hits, although several of his innings were extended by poor fielding behind him. But he was good enough to run his win streak to four. Billingsley continues to insist his turnaround after a bad finish last year and slow start this season is to simplify his approach and focus on the fastball and curveball that got him to the Major Leagues. He went 4-1 with a 2.61 ERA in May, including a win in Arizona.
away_pitcher_note: Lopez faced an uphill battle in his last outing starting opposite Colorado's Ubaldo Jimenez at Coors Field. Lopez allowed a first-inning homer, and just missed escaping a jam in the third when he allowed a two-out, two-run triple to Brad Hawpe. He eventually left the game trailing 4-0 after six and the D-backs went on to lose 7-3. While not overpowering, Lopez has a good feel for pitching and manages a game well. He came to Spring Training as a non-roster invitee and pitched his way into the No. 4 spot in the rotation, besting Billy Buckner and Kevin Mulvey. The right-hander has battled arm troubles since being the ace of the Orioles' staff earlier in the decade. He throws a fastball, cutter, curveball, slider and change. Lopez appeared in seven games (five starts) for the Phillies last year and also started 18 games for Triple-A Lehigh Valley.

home_pitcher_note: Now manager Joe Torre is calling John Ely "a God-send." Ely keeps throwing strikes, and even in defeat against the Cubs, he couldn't have been much more impressive, taking a three-hit shutout into the eighth inning at Wrigley Field. All five of the rookie right-hander's five starts have been six innings or longer. He's fun to watch pitch, sometimes compared to Mark "The Bird" Fidrych for his energetic enthusiasm on the mound. He's made a believer out of Torre, who pushed him back a day to give his arm extra rest because he expects him to be starting regularly from here on out. He went 3-1 with a 2.18 ERA in five May starts.
away_pitcher_note: Haren has struggled mightily this year, and that has left him searching for answers. Following his last start when he allowed eight runs in 6 1/3 innings against the Rockies, Haren took stock of his year to date. His conclusion? That his stuff is there, but he is not executing pitches and he is giving up far too many homers. Hitters are still swinging and missing as evidenced by his strikeout total. So far in 74 innings, he has allowed 16 homers. Last time out, the Rockies hit four, including three in a row at one point. It is a trend that he knows he has to reverse if he hopes to start posting more Haren-like numbers.

home_pitcher_note: By default (Charlie Haeger's toe injury), Monasterios gets another start after a respectable five innings (two earned runs) against Colorado at Coors Field on Friday night, good enough for the win when the Dodgers rallied in the top of the sixth inning. Monasterios needed only 67 pitches to get that much done. He's 2-0 with a 2.20 ERA, better results than the club could have hoped for a Rule 5 Draft rookie who had only three appearances above Class A coming into the season. Monasterios has been a starter for most of his Minor League career and said he feels more comfortable in that role because he can use all of his pitches, including a deceptive changeup.
away_pitcher_note: Jackson has pitched better of late after a rough start to the year. The right-hander took the loss in his last start against the Giants at AT&T Park. In that game, he allowed just three runs on four hits over seven innings, but his mound opponent that night, Matt Cain, threw a one-hitter. When Jackson is at his best, he is aggressive early in games with his fastball. If he falls behind in the count, he runs into trouble because hitters are more able to dial up to hit his mid-90s heater. Jackson was acquired by Arizona in a three-team trade during the Winter Meetings that sent Max Scherzer and Daniel Schlereth to the Tigers. The D-backs are his third team in three years. He pitched for Tampa Bay in 2008 before being dealt to the Tigers before last year. Jackson throws a fastball, curve, slider and changeup.

home_pitcher_note: Kuroda has taken losses in his past two outings, but his most recent start on Saturday against the Rockies was his worst of the season. He lasted four innings and allowed five runs on 10 hits, walking one but also striking out just one. Kuroda has owned the Braves in two career starts, allowing two runs and eight hits with four walks and 10 strikeouts in 15 innings. Pitching at home hasn't made much of a difference to Kuroda this season: his ERA is 3.62 at Dodger Stadium and 3.48 on the road, with five starts made at each.
away_pitcher_note: With Braves pitcher Jair Jurrjens out until late June with a strained left hamstring, Medlen has continued to be invaluable in his switch from the bullpen to the rotation. In four starts, the 24-year-old has an ERA of 3.25 while completing 22 1/3 innings. Manager Bobby Cox has stressed the need to stretch out Medlen's pitch count, and thus far, the right-hander has hovered close to 95 pitches. Medlen hasn't been overpowering with his repertoire of pitches -- instead preferring to let opposing batters put the ball in play. However, the righty did have a season-high six strikeouts against the Mets on May 18.

home_pitcher_note: Kershaw's ERA going into May 9 was 4.99. He's lowered it to 2.95, and though his last start -- two runs in five innings to the Rockies on Sunday -- wasn't his best, Kershaw had turned in four straight quality starts previous to it. His 72 strikeouts have him close to the league lead, and he struck out 10 Braves in the only start he ever made against them on Aug. 8, 2009. He went seven scoreless innings and allowed two hits and one walk in a game the Dodgers lost, 2-1.
away_pitcher_note: After becoming the first Braves pitcher to lose his first seven starts to begin a season since 1985, Kawakami once again look poised to earn his first victory of the year against the Pirates on May 30. But after allowing a game-tying two-run home run in the seventh inning, Kawakami again left with a no-decision. Still, the 34-year-old has performed extremely well lately. In his past three starts, the right-hander has completed 18 2/3 innings with a 2.41 ERA. Kawakami hasn't won since last Aug. 31, but his start against the Pirates tied his longest outing of 2010.

home_pitcher_note: Even when things have gone badly for Billingsley lately, they've gone well. He gave up three home runs in the first two innings on Monday, but the D-backs took away only four runs from them. Billingsley settled in and went a season-high eight innings without allowing another run, and in all-or-nothing fashion, struck out the side in the first and second innings. He finished with 11 strikeouts, another season high. He took a no-decision that game after winning his last four in a row and five of his previous six. Billingsley had an even 3.00 ERA in six May starts, and struck out 38 batters to 10 walks.
away_pitcher_note: After issuing three walks and throwing half of his first 38 pitches for balls during the first two innings of Monday's game against the Phillies, Hanson couldn't figure out what was wrong with his pitching mechanics. Teammate, roommate and fellow starter Kris Medlen told Hanson to raise his arm and stay on top of the ball. The 23-year-old right-hander did and completed 6 2/3 innings, allowing one run and just three hits. Overall, though, the month of May was a struggle at times. Hanson started six games and completed 35 1/3 innings, conceding 35 hits with a 5.09 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Ely's success has been mystifying, and it's been nothing but consistent. The rookie right-hander has gone at least seven innings in his last two outings and three of his last four. His last start was a showdown with Dan Haren, where Ely tossed seven shutout innings and allowed just two hits and two walks and struck out five. He didn't get a decision in that game, and took a loss in his previous outing, where he allowed just one run to the Cubs but the Dodgers scored none. The opposition has a .267 batting average on balls put in play, the lowest BABIP against any Dodgers starter aside from Carlos Monasterios, who's more of a fill-in anyway. So there could be some luck involved for Ely -- but it hasn't run out yet.
away_pitcher_note: Even with a second straight start being interrupted by a rain delay, Tim Hudson still couldn't be stopped. The 34-year-old starter won his fifth straight outing, completing six innings while allowing five hits and two runs against the Phillies on Tuesday. Even more remarkable, the right-hander hasn't conceded more than three runs in any start this season. If not for rain hampering a start in Florida, Hudson's shortest outing of the year would be 5 2/3 innings. And since May 1, Hudson has been nothing short of incredible. He has a 5-0 record in 45 2/3 innings with a 1.79 ERA. Heck, Hudson even has a five-game hitting streak.

home_pitcher_note: Monasterios' last outing Wednesday was cut short after five innings because of a finger blister, but he is still in line to start Monday in the opener of a three-game series against the Cardinals -- as long as his bullpen session on Saturday goes as planned. The rookie right-hander is 2-0 with a 1.87 ERA in 14 appearances, only three of which have been starts. He has yet to go more than five innings, but he's also yet to take a loss.
away_pitcher_note: The Cardinals have yet to announce whether Hawksworth or P.J. Walters will get this start, and in either case, manager Tony La Russa has said he will view it as a "bullpen game." It would appear that Hawksworth may have the edge, though, for one reason: Walters is the incumbent, having already made two starts. If he were getting the call for a third time, it doesn't seem that the club would hesitate to say as much. If Hawksworth is the choice, it will be his first big league start.
summary: 2010-06-07 - St. Louis Cardinals (4) @ Los Angeles Dodgers (12) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Kuroda's one career start against the Cardinals, on July 30, 2009, went well: he let up four hits and two runs in six innings, striking out five and walking none. Matt Holliday's 14 career at-bats against Kuroda? Those haven't gone as well. Holliday is 7-for-14 with two doubles, a home run and six RBIs against Kuroda lifetime and has struck out once. Kuroda rebounded in his last start on Thursday, going six and allowing four runs, three earned to the Braves. The start before, he had let up seven runs, five earned, in four innings.
away_pitcher_note: Carpenter recorded what may have been his finest outing of the season last Wednesday against the Reds. Pitching eight strong innings, allowing four hits to go with a solitary run, Carpenter effectively worked both sides of the plate to keep the Cincinnati hitters frustrated all game. With a career 2.20 ERA in six starts against the Dodgers and a perfect 5-0 record when facing L.A., Carpenter appears primed for another dominant outing.
summary: 2010-06-08 - St. Louis Cardinals (0) @ Los Angeles Dodgers (1) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Were it not for a five-inning start on May 30, Kershaw would have six consecutive quality starts in a row. He allowed three earned runs in 6 2/3 innings to the Braves in his last outing Friday, the first time he had allowed more than two runs in a start since May 4. Kershaw's walks and strikeouts have both been up over his last two starts: he's walked nine and struck out 17. None of the Cardinals have homered off Kershaw, but Matt Holliday is 4-for-10 and Albert Pujols is 4-for-7 with two doubles lifetime.
away_pitcher_note: Wainwright returns to the site of some of his most memorable outings. Back in 2007, he got knocked around at Dodger Stadium in a game that he considered a major turning point in his career. Two years later, he pitched absolutely brilliantly in a playoff game at Chavez Ravine but came away with nothing to show for it after Los Angeles rallied in the ninth. This time around, the Cardinals mostly need innings, since two of their regular starters are on the disabled list.
summary: 2010-06-09 - St. Louis Cardinals (3) @ Los Angeles Dodgers (4) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Billingsley let up three earned runs in his last start against the Braves on Saturday, but he was deserving of a better line, tossing a shutout through six innings. He hasn't allowed more than three runs since he gave up four runs on May 5, and his ERA after that game was at 5.06. Now with his ERA at 3.80, and as low as 3.63 two starts ago, it's looking more and more like Billingsley has turned a corner. He has been a considerably better pitcher on the road, where his ERA is 2.78 in six starts, than at home, where his ERA is 4.66 in as many starts. Matt Holliday has a strange career line off Billingsley: five hits - three of which were home runs - four strikeouts, and six walks in 20 at-bats.
away_pitcher_note: Pineiro overcame a rough start to pitch tenaciously through six innings and claim a win on Sunday in Seattle, his former home park. After giving up three first-inning runs, he held the Mariners to one the rest of the way, giving up nine hits and three walks (one intentional) while striking out five men. It was his first win since May 16. Pineiro is 2-0 with a 3.38 ERA in three career starts against the Dodgers, and he's 1-0 with a 4.26 ERA in his lone outing at Dodger Stadium.
summary: 2010-06-11 - Los Angeles Angels (10) @ Los Angeles Dodgers (1) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: He doesn't light up the radar gun or the national consciousness like Stephen Strasburg, but this rookie forced his way into the starting rotation of the team with the best record in the league, so there's something going on here too. Ely is a strike-thrower not afraid of pitching to contact, a rare approach since amateur pitchers have had to adjust to aluminum bats.  And what he lacks in velocity he makes up for in pitching savvy, utilizing four pitches and appreciating the value of pinpoint location. He's already pitched in New York and Chicago, so the big stage of the Freeway Series won't bother him.
summary: 2010-06-12 - Los Angeles Angels (4) @ Los Angeles Dodgers (2) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Manager Joe Torre has been treating this Rule 5 right-hander with the kid gloves you'd expect to show a rookie with little experience, except that the right-hander has been pitching well beyond his years. Torre has been using Monasterios as a fill-in until Vicente Padilla returns from the disabled list. But Monasterios considers himself a starter and is pitching so well that he is making it tough for Torre to send him back to the bullpen. In a year when rookie pitchers are making an impact throughout the league, none of them has a lower opponents batting average than Monasterios.
away_pitcher_note: Weaver endured a rare ineffective outing on Tuesday night in Oakland, surrendering six earned runs on 12 hits in six-plus innings. It was only the fourth time in 13 starts in which the angular right-hander had yielded more than two earned runs. The crushing blow was a three-run homer in the seventh by Kurt Suzuki after a pair of infield rollers for singles. Weaver struck out six, giving him 89 in 81 2/3 innings. He is 3-2 with a 2.94 ERA in six career starts against the Dodgers and has been brilliant at Dodger Stadium despite a 1-1 record in three outings with a 0.55 ERA.
summary: 2010-06-13 - Los Angeles Angels (6) @ Los Angeles Dodgers (5) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Harang started the season 1-4, but has worked his way back to the .500 mark. He's now 3-0 in his last five starts and hasn't lost since May 14. In Wednesday's win over the Giants, he pitched seven innings for the second time in three games and gave up two runs and five hits. Harang has lost his last two starts against the Dodgers, allowing double-digit hits in each. Current Dodgers hitters have combined to hit .364 against him in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Kuroda threw the game that threw the Dodgers into first place on June 8. It wasn't his longest start of the season, but it might have been his best with seven innings of no-run ball. He gave up four hits and walked one. Kuroda's May (4.42 ERA) wasn't close to his April (2.36 ERA), but June seems to be going closer to the latter: he's 2-0 with a 2.08 ERA through his first two starts in the month. Kuroda's also won his two carer starts against the Reds, who have scored five runs off him in 13 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: The Giants took an aggressive approach to Leake on Thursday and managed 11 hits and five runs off of him. It was Leake's shortest start of the season, as he was pulled from the game after 4 1/3 innings. However, the Reds made a comeback and won 7-6, meaning Leake still has not lost a game in the Major Leagues. Four of his last five starts have resulted in no-decisions, but the five runs he gave up against the Giants were more than the total earned runs he allowed in the previous five starts combined (four).
away_pitcher_note: Kershaw has gone at least seven innings in five starts this season, something he had done just three times by this point in the season a year ago. He struck out a season-high 10 in his last start against the Cardinals on Wednesday and walked just two. His ERA on the road is 2.51, nearly a full run better than it is at home, but opponents are hitting just .189 against him at Dodger Stadium. On the road they're batting .224.

home_pitcher_note: Arroyo has gone three starts in a row without a win after going 5-0 in his previous six starts from April 29 to May 26. He pitched seven innings in the series opener with Kansas City last Friday, allowing five runs and six hits with three walks and four strikeouts, but the Reds lost, 6-5, in 11 innings and Arroyo got a no-decision. Thursday's game will be a 12:35 p.m. start, and in his career, Arroyo is just 22-31 with a 4.54 ERA in day games, as opposed to 69-55 with a 4.15 ERA at night.
away_pitcher_note: A rough patch for the rookie has come. Ely has allowed four runs in five innings in each of his past two starts and has given up a combined three home runs -- he hadn't allowed a long ball in his first seven starts of the season. Four runs in five innings isn't the worst day, but Ely also walked more batters (three) than he struck out (two) on Sunday against the Angels. When Ely is right, and successful, he has almost pinpoint control. He needs to have that control, with a fastball that doesn't reach much beyond the high 80s. A two-run blast (fourth inning) and a bloop (fifth inning) undid him last time, but that's a lesson Ely's learning: two bad pitches can make all the difference.

home_pitcher_note: The 22-year-old lefty from Venezuela will make his Major League debut in this one, filling in for the injured Daisuke Matsuzaka. Doubront has certainly earned this start, putting up terrific numbers this season at both Double-A Portland (4-0, 2.51 ERA) and Triple-A Pawtucket (2-1, 1.08 ERA). Doubront impressed the Red Sox in Spring Training, pitching seven shutout innings. Doubront has been in Boston's farm system since 2005. He was signed out of Venezuela on July 12, 2004. He has made 109 career starts in the Minors, going 42-30 with a 3.55 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Monasterios was expected to move out of the rotation with the return of Vicente Padilla from the disabled list. However, Chad Billingsley was sent to the DL, meaning Monasterios will stay and make another start. The 24-year-old native of Venezuela has made 11 appearances as a reliever and five as a starter. In those five starts, he's 2-1 with a 3.97 ERA. Most recently, he picked up his first loss of the year by allowing four runs and seven hits in just 2 2/3 innings.
summary: 2010-06-18 - Los Angeles Dodgers (6) @ Boston Red Sox (10) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: The veteran knuckleballer had one bad inning in his last start, and it cost him. Wakefield gave up four runs -- all in the fourth frame -- over 7 1/3 innings in a 5-3 loss to the Phillies. Wakefield has made three starts in June, going 1-2 with a 4.79 ERA. In 10 starts this season, Wakefield is 2-5 with a 5.32 ERA. Uncharacteristically, Wakefield has struggled at Fenway this season, going 0-4 with a 6.86 ERA in eight games, six of them starts. Wakefield has pitched four times against the Dodgers in his career, going 1-2 with a 6.64 ERA. Wakefield hasn't faced former teammate Manny Ramirez since 2000. Lifetime against Wakefield, Ramirez is just 6-for-26 with no homers and one RBI.
away_pitcher_note: Padilla will return to the Dodgers' rotation after nearly two months on the disabled list with an inflamed radial nerve in his pitching arm. He has not pitched since April 22, when Los Angeles lost at Cincinnati, 8-5. He made three rehab starts, and in his final one for Triple-A Albuquerque on Sunday, he allowed six runs and eight hits in 5 2/3 innings.
summary: 2010-06-19 - Los Angeles Dodgers (4) @ Boston Red Sox (5) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: The righty continued his streak of solid pitching in his last start against the Arizona Diamondbacks, going 5 2/3 innings and yielding a team-high ninth win, while giving up only three runs on seven hits. It was his sixth win in his last seven starts, a streak which began on May 14. In that time he has posted an ERA of 1.84 and made a solid case for why he should be included in the talk for a possible All-Star appearance. Sunday's start against the Dodgers will be the first of his career.
away_pitcher_note: Kuroda pitched on both sides of a 2-hour, 24-minute rain delay Tuesday at Cincinnati. He pitched four scoreless innings before the delay and one after, although he had to escape a bases-loaded jam in the fifth. He picked up his first win since May 18 after three losses in four starts. Kuroda has struggled in Interleague Play so far in his career, going 1-5 with a 4.89 ERA in six starts. In one Interleague start this season, Kuroda allowed three runs in six innings against the Tigers and lost on May 23.
summary: 2010-06-20 - Los Angeles Dodgers (0) @ Boston Red Sox (2) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Santana admitted his slider was not particularly strong a week ago when he let up season-highs in runs (six) and hits (10) to the Brewers, the second straight poor outing for Santana. He's 2-3 with a 3.94 ERA in five career Freeway Series starts, but he's also pitched much better on the road (3.04 ERA) than he has at Angel Stadium (5.12 ERA). Casey Blake, of all the Dodgers hitters, has given Santana the most trouble. Blake is 6-for-14 with two homers and three walks and three strikeouts against Santana.
away_pitcher_note: Kershaw, even if by default, has become the de facto staff ace. He just out-pitched Rookie of the Year candidate Mike Leake in Cincinnati, taking the game into the eighth inning, raising his record to 7-3, and 6-1 in his most recent stretch. He's right there with the best pitchers in the league for strikeouts, and opponents are batting only .206 against him. He still leads the league in walks allowed but had a season-low one against the Reds. He's allowed the Angels only one run in 12 lifetime innings and threw seven scoreless innings in his only previous start in Anaheim.
summary: 2010-06-22 - Los Angeles Dodgers (3) @ Los Angeles Angels (6) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Pineiro backed up a complete-game victory against the Dodgers with another sterling effort, going eight innings and holding the Brewers to a solo homer and three hits in a victory on Wednesday. Pineiro was economical and efficient, walking only one man while striking out five and throwing 109 pitches. His sinker was in command when he needed it, and his complementary stuff also was on target. Pineiro is 3-0 with a 2.67 ERA in four career starts against the Dodgers.
away_pitcher_note: Ely gets a chance to turn things around after three consecutive wobbly starts that saw his ERA jump from 2.54 to 4.15. Previously, he was one of the better rookies in the NL, stringing together six consecutive quality starts. With a fastball that peaks at 90 mph, Ely needs to be a strike thrower with all four pitches. Lately he's been falling behind, leading to six home runs allowed in those last three starts. Have opposing scouts and offenses caught up to Ely or has he just been slumping? The Angels will be a good test to answer the question. They scored four runs off Ely in five innings at Dodger Stadium earlier in the month.
summary: 2010-06-23 - Los Angeles Dodgers (1) @ Los Angeles Angels (2) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Kazmir continues to win -- four straight decisions, five in the past six -- with solid work, but he's still not getting quite as deep in games as he or manager Mike Scioscia would like. Kazmir lasted six innings in the Chicago heat on Friday, yielding two earned runs on five hits and three walks while striking out three. Over his past four starts he has surrendered just six earned runs in 29 1/3 innings. He beat the Dodgers at Dodger Stadium on June 12, going five innings, and is 1-0 with a 4.09 ERA in two career starts against the Dodgers. Kazmir is 2-2, 5.91 in four starts this season at Angel Stadium.
away_pitcher_note: Haeger has a make-or-break start and a chance to snap the Dodgers' six-game losing streak. It will Haeger's sixth start of the season, the others coming as the fifth starter out of Spring Training, but first since he went on the disabled list May 9 with the first of what was officially two foot injuries. The knuckleballer said he's regained his confidence after throwing six scoreless innings in his most recent Minor League injury rehab start. He'll be pitching on three days' rest.
summary: 2010-06-24 - Los Angeles Dodgers (10) @ Los Angeles Angels (6) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Padilla returned from nearly two months on the sidelines with an inflamed nerve in his pitching arm and he did it in Fenway Park, so the Yankees shouldn't faze him. All things considered, it didn't go too badly as he allowed four runs and made it into the sixth inning. Padilla was healthy enough to deliver 89 pitches, his fastball still hitting 95 mph in his last inning. He struck out four and walked one.
away_pitcher_note: Sabathia goes for his fifth consecutive victory as the Yankees open a three-game series at Dodger Stadium. Sabathia was perhaps his sharpest on June 20, hurling eight innings of scoreless, four-hit ball against the Mets in the Bronx. Sabathia would have had a shot at a complete game if not for a rain delay that cut him short after 100 pitches. Sabathia faced the Dodgers once previously- - in 2008, when he hurled seven innings of one-run, five-hit ball in a win.
summary: 2010-06-25 - New York Yankees (2) @ Los Angeles Dodgers (1) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Kuroda is coming off a disappointing pitchers' duel in Boston against Clay Buchholz, in which the Dodgers gave him no run support. Kuroda said his back-to-back quality starts on the trip have been accomplished with the return of slider command and he said he can't get frustrated by a lack of run support.
away_pitcher_note: Burnett will try to snap his four-start losing streak on Saturday, trying to bounce back from a rough outing on Monday in which he allowed seven runs in four innings, including a five-run first inning in which the D-backs hit three home runs. Burnett said he is having trouble pitching out of the full windup and throwing his fastball for strikes, and is 0-4 with a 10.35 ERA in his last four starts. Burnett is 3-2 with a 2.45 ERA in seven career starts against the Dodgers, but he has not faced them since 2005.
summary: 2010-06-26 - New York Yankees (4) @ Los Angeles Dodgers (9) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Kershaw had a one-hitter through five innings against the Angels on Tuesday, but was done in on a three-run homer by Bobby Abreu, the rally beginning with a walk, a department that Kershaw still leads the league in. He came into the game having won six of his previous seven decisions. He has now incorporated a slider into his previous repertoire of fastball and curve.
away_pitcher_note: Pettitte will try to keep his run of strong pitching going on Sunday as the Yankees wrap up a three-game series against Joe Torre and the Dodgers on Sunday. Pettitte has ventured at least seven innings in each of his past six starts, including June 22, when he logged his ninth win by hurling seven innings of two-run, seven-hit ball against the D-backs at Chase Field. Pettitte is 2-2 with a 2.48 ERA in June and opponents have hit just .206 against him. He is 2-0 with a 3.33 ERA in four career starts against the Dodgers, having last faced them in 2006.
summary: 2010-06-27 - New York Yankees (8) @ Los Angeles Dodgers (6) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Zito lasted only four innings in his last outing against Houston, giving up five runs on seven hits. In Zito's last start against the Dodgers in April, the lefty tossed 7 1/3 innings of one-run ball en route to a no-decision.
away_pitcher_note: Billingsley is returning from a stint on the disabled list with a tight groin suffered in his last start, but he passed a simulated game test Thursday and reported no stiffness Friday. He is 4-2 lifetime against the Giants and 2-1 at AT&T Park.
summary: 2010-06-28 - Los Angeles Dodgers (4) @ San Francisco Giants (2) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Cain's steady streak of impressive outings went up in smoke against Houston in his last outing, in which he last only 2 2/3 innings, giving up seven runs on nine hits. The seven-run outing caused Cain's ERA to jump from 2.16 to 2.72.
away_pitcher_note: Ely bounced back in Anaheim after repeated wobbly starts, allowing only one earned run in seven innings and drawing the loss because his offense ran out of a tying rally in the ninth. He's a strike thrower who doesn't throw hard enough to get away with misses.
summary: 2010-06-29 - Los Angeles Dodgers (4) @ San Francisco Giants (2) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Sanchez struggled early in his last outing against Boston, including a 37-pitch first inning in which he gave up a three-run homer to Kevin Youkilis. Sanchez managed to regrup and pitch into the sixth inning, only giving up those three runs but walking four.
away_pitcher_note: Padilla, in only his second start off the DL, went seven solid innings against the potent Yankees with seven strikeouts, hurt mainly by two extra-base hits from Alex Rodriguez. Padilla maintained his velocity, which helped make his Eephus slow-curve even more effective.
summary: 2010-06-30 - Los Angeles Dodgers (8) @ San Francisco Giants (2) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Jackson tossed a no-hitter in his last start against the Rays on Friday. While he did not allow any hits, Jackson did walk eight and hit a batter so the effort took him 149 pitches. With that in mind, the D-backs are giving him two extra days rest before this start.
away_pitcher_note: Kuroda was a little too fired up facing the Yankees, walking the first two batters and allowing a first-inning homer. He settled after that and the Dodgers rallied for a win that wasn't his most impressive. He was nailed by a line drive last year in Arizona.

home_pitcher_note: Lopez has been pretty consistent all season. His ERA continues its dip after stellar starts against American League East giants, New York and Tampa Bay. Most recently, the veteran right-hander allowed just one earned run in a six-inning win over the Rays.
away_pitcher_note: Kershaw pitched well enough against the Yankees to win, and would have if Jonathan Broxton had not blown a four-run lead in the ninth inning. It was Kershaw's first start without a walk. He's fourth in the league in strikeouts.

home_pitcher_note: While his ERA remains uncharacteristically high, Haren hasn't allowed more than four earned runs in six straight starts. In his previous outing against the Dodgers, on June 1 in Los Angeles, the righty threw eight scoreless innings but received a tough-luck no-decision.

John Ely has battled through a June slump and four-game losing streak to rebound with a pair of quality starts, most recently beating the Giants. He's not overpowering, but he has a full repertoire of pitches and he's not intimidated by Major League competition.
away_pitcher_note: With a little more luck, Robertson would have come out with a victory in his last start. Instead, he finished with a no-decision, but the team ended up beating the Mets. The lefty gave up four runs in six-plus innings. His season innings high is 6 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: In his third start off the disabled list, Vicente Padilla pitched a gem against the Giants, allowing one run in seven innings. The return of the Opening Day starter has been a big boost to a starting rotation that was looking quite ragged without him.
away_pitcher_note: Perhaps it's a sign of maturity. Volstad overcame a 28-pitch first inning in his last start, a frame in which he gave up three runs (two earned) to the Mets. He regrouped and posted five innings in a no-decision. This is his second meeting with L.A., having lost on April 9.

home_pitcher_note: Hiroki Kuroda is coming off his worst start of the year, lasting only 1 2/3 innings while allowing six earned runs. The worst part is that neither he nor the staff could really explain why, other than a lack of command of any pitch other than the fastball.
away_pitcher_note: It's been dominating and frustrating when Johnson has pitched of late. In his last four starts, he has received five runs of support. The result is he's 1-2 in those outings, including a no-decision against the Braves. In six innings at Atlanta, he struck out eight.

home_pitcher_note: Kershaw's allowed more than three runs just twice this season and is pitching like a true ace. He wasn't able to finish six innings in his last start, but he let up just four hits and two walks, striking out eight. He's only faced the Cubs once his career, earning the win.
away_pitcher_note: Wells no-hit the Reds until the seventh inning in his last start, the second time he's done that in his career, and won for the first time since April 30. He's switched to a more compact delivery, and it's helped.

home_pitcher_note: Billingsley has gone six innings in his last two starts, allowing three total runs. After a rough April and an injured June, Billingsley is pitching more confidence now that he's not worrying about his pitch counts, which can still climb high, but the club has accepted it.
away_pitcher_note: Lilly was roughed up in his last start vs. the Reds, serving up a career-high 11 hits, including four home runs. The problem was location. In late May, he threw seven shutout innings vs. the Dodgers.

home_pitcher_note: Ely's last start, a 2 2/3-innings, five-earned run performance against the Marlins, was a regression after he had gone seven innings and allowed one run in each of his last two starts. The rookie, who relies on control, needs to show consistency. He's 1-4 in his last five.
away_pitcher_note: Gorzelanny has pitched quite well since rejoining the rotation on June 30. Most recently, on Monday in Arizona, he yielded three runs to the D-backs over five innings. Walks -- he issued a season-high six -- cost him a chance at pitching deep into the game.

away_pitcher_note: Allard is getting his third start of the season after moving from the bullpen to the rotation on May 27. He's performed admirably, allowing two earned runs in each of his starts. His 3.41 ERA is second among Rangers starters.

home_pitcher_note: Buehler is unbeaten in his last 21 starts, tying Clayton Kershaw and Julio Urías for the longest streak since the team moved to Los Angeles. Buehler's last loss came on Sept. 21, 2019, against the Rockies.
away_pitcher_note: Dunning notched his fourth scoreless start of the season in his outing against Tampa Bay last Sunday, when he took a no-decision in the Rangers' loss. The rookie right-hander seems to have found his footing after a seven-run outing vs. the Angels on May 26.

home_pitcher_note: Gonsolin will make his second start of the season. He didn't make it out of the second inning on Wednesday vs. the Pirates after he issued five walks and allowed one earned run and two hits in 1 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Spencer Howard had the shortest of his three starts his last time out against the Nationals. Howard allowed one unearned run, two walks and one hit in 2 1/3 innings. The 24-year-old has a 2.89 ERA in 9 1/3 innings as a starter this season.

home_pitcher_note: Urías continues to show his value in his first full season as a starter. He’s tied for the MLB lead in wins. Urías has yielded 10 home runs and only 11 walks over 13 starts.
away_pitcher_note: His last start may have been the bounce-back outing Zach Eflin he needed. He scattered eight hits while allowing just one run in six innings against the Braves. Eflin is searching for his first win since May 7, as he has gone 0-4 in his last five starts.

home_pitcher_note: Kershaw bounced back in his last start Friday vs. Texas with six innings, one unearned run, three hits and one walk. Before then, he combined for 10 runs, 15 hits and four walks over two starts. Opponents are hitting .214 vs. Kershaw.
away_pitcher_note: In eight of his last nine starts, Zack Wheeler has completed seven or more innings. Wheeler went eight scoreless innings and struck out 12 batters his last time out. He has allowed two runs in 15 1/3 innings in June after posting a 2.08 ERA in six May starts.

home_pitcher_note: Since transitioning back to the starting rotation, Smith has done a solid job of helping eat up innings. In his last three starts, Smith has a 4.40 ERA across 14 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: After being dominant through May, Bauer has struggled to find success in June. In his last two starts, Bauer is 0-2 with a 5.11 ERA. He has struck out 15 in 12 1/3 innings of work, but has also walked six. Opponents have a .300 batting average off the right-hander in those games.

home_pitcher_note: Peacock, who has been thrust into rotation duty due to injuries, will look to turn around what has been a rough June. In three starts this month, Peacock has allowed nine earned runs in 11 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Buehler has been the Dodgers' most consistent starter this season and he'll look to extend his streak without a loss to 23 consecutive regular-season starts.

home_pitcher_note: Young will make his second start of the year. His first came five days ago, when he tossed four innings before turning things over to Corbin Martin. It's likely that the D-backs will do something similar with Young this time around.
away_pitcher_note: Gonsolin has struggled with his command since being activated from the injured list. In his two starts this season, Gonsolin has walked eight over 5 1/3 innings. He has also recorded nine strikeouts and has posted a 3.38 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: The Padres won 11 of Darvish's first 12 starts, but they've now lost two straight. Still, Darvish was mostly sharp in those two outings. He's allowed just 59 hits while striking out 97 across 84 innings this season.
away_pitcher_note: Urías has made eight career appearances (three starts) against San Diego, going 1-0 with a 2.08 ERA. This will be his first start against the Padres this season.
